abstract_en: ADGA Group is a 100% Canadian-owned company headquartered in Nepean (Ottawa), Ontario, and was founded in 1967 as an engineering consultancy. It works in four service lines: C5ISRT and mission systems, simulation and training, program delivery, and full-spectrum security. Its two lines of business are Defence and Critical Infrastructure & Public Safety. Since 2021 it has been part of Commissionaires Ottawa.

Ontario Shipyards, formerly Heddle Shipyards, was founded in Hamilton in 1987. It operates shipyards in Hamilton and St. Catharines, plus a Thunder Bay yard that trade press reports as idled since 2024. Its core business is ship repair and maintenance, with new builds, conversions, vessel recycling, heavy industrial fabrication and project support services. It states that it has completed over 100 dry-docking and alongside refit projects on Canadian Coast Guard vessels since 2012. It is also a partner in Team Vigilance, a bid for a Canadian naval corvette.

Voyageur Aviation Corp. is headquartered at Jack Garland Airport in North Bay, Ontario, and is a wholly owned subsidiary of Chorus Aviation Inc. It holds Approved Maintenance Organization and Design Approval Organization status and provides aircraft modification, supplemental type certificate engineering, heavy maintenance, component repair and overhaul, and used serviceable parts sales. It also operates charter, ACMI, air ambulance and special mission flights, and supports Department of National Defence programs such as the CT-142 upgrade, MAISR in-service support and AETE support.

Armo Tool began in 1969 as a precision grinding and coating shop and now designs, builds and tries out stamping dies, tooling, fixtures and custom automation in-house, from design through machining, programming and run-off. Its work is mainly for automotive customers, with additional automation work for medical device, food and beverage, consumer and nuclear customers. Together with its Abuma Manufacturing division it also supplies fabricated and machined assemblies to the Canadian defence industry. It operates two plants in London, Ontario and publishes an ISO 9001:2015 certificate.

Patriot Forge Corporation was founded in 2001 and operates two plants in Brantford and Paris, Ontario. It forges bars, shafts, sleeves, rings, disks and die-tooled parts in carbon, alloy, stainless and other steel grades, and heat treats and machines them in house. It states it supplies raw forged material for artillery components, Navy shipbuilding components and submarine pumps, and for nuclear, aerospace landing-gear, power generation, oil and gas, mining and infrastructure uses. Its own 2026 CANSEC announcement says it is now producing rifled 105mm howitzer barrels and forged 120mm mortar tubes.

InDro Robotics is an engineering and operations company based in British Columbia, with its research and development base at Area X.O in Ottawa. It makes and integrates uncrewed ground and aerial systems and related software. It also distributes and integrates robot platforms from AgileX and Unitree. It offers custom robot builds, a prototyping lab (InDro Forge), a drone and robot test and training zone, and drone pilot and survey services. In September 2026 it announced selection as a Qualified Supplier under the federal Defence Drone Initiative.

D-TA Systems Inc. was founded in 2007 in Ottawa and sells spectrum sensing and spectrum creation systems to armed forces, defence primes and government laboratories. Its products pair a sensor interface unit with a commercial server linked by 10/40/100 GbE fibre, with software-based processing. It operates a 25,000-square-foot headquarters with its own anechoic chamber and a mobile system integration facility. It reports more than 50 active customers in Five Eyes, NATO and QUAD countries.

Newcon Optik is a Toronto-based designer and manufacturer of image-intensified night vision devices, uncooled thermal imagers, laser rangefinders (including modules for OEM integration) and tactical optics. It states that it has operated since 1992, assembles products in-house, including on an SMT line, and services them at its Toronto facility. It states that its products are in use in more than 70 countries through a dealer network, and that it holds a Department of National Defence contract for the LRM 3500M laser rangefinder monocular.

Palitronica Inc. is a Waterloo, Ontario company that applies physics-based testing and machine learning to electronics quality assurance and hardware supply chain cybersecurity. Its Anvil Checkpoint platform compares a unit under test with a known-good profile without needing schematics, firmware or bills of materials. It states that it serves the automotive, aerospace and defence, government and infrastructure, medical, and high-reliability manufacturing sectors. It has published a Department of National Defence contract and a selection by Bell Textron for the MV-75 Cheyenne program.

Labforge is a Waterloo technology company established in 2013 by founders from University of Waterloo research groups. It designs perception systems that fuse imaging, radar, depth, acoustic, seismic and RF sensing for defence and industrial use. Its products are Snow Flea (ground-based sensing and electronic warfare nodes with Tower and Micro Pod configurations), ICTN (a distributed camera tracking network) and Bottlenose (stereo and monocular smart cameras sold through Mouser Electronics). It reports funding from DND, Innovative Solutions Canada and Ontario Centres of Innovation, and in September 2026 reported qualification under Stream 1 of the Defence Drone Initiative Marketplace.

Robotics Centre is an Ottawa-headquartered developer, manufacturer and integrator of uncrewed systems that states it was co-founded in 2009. It makes its own Shuriken and Kukri FPV drones in Canada and distributes and integrates platforms such as the Skydio X10D, Teledyne FLIR SkyRanger R70 and Milrem THeMIS UGV. It also provides operator and maintenance training and local maintenance and support. It has offices in Ukraine, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Japan and the United States.

FELLFAB Limited is a privately held Canadian company, established in 1952 and based in Hamilton, Ontario, with U.S. sister facilities in Georgia and Texas. It designs and makes soft goods for the aviation, space, rail, industrial and military markets. Its capabilities include advanced stitching, RF welding, foam fabrication, lamination and a Class 100,000 clean room. It holds a combined AS9100D / ISO 9001:2015 certificate and is listed in the Controlled Goods Program registry. Its Canadian military products have included load carriage systems, tents and sleep systems.

VAC AERO International Inc. traces its history to Canadian Vac-Hyd Processing Ltd., which opened in Oakville in 1959. It builds vacuum furnaces (VAH horizontal and VAV vertical series), hot zones and control systems at its Burlington head office, and services and retrofits furnaces of other makes. Its heat treatment, brazing and coating plants hold AS9100:D and Nadcap credentials according to its website, and it is registered in the Controlled Goods Program. It names aerospace, medical, industrial and nuclear customers, and in April 2026 announced a $7 million Boeing commitment through the CP-8A Poseidon Industrial and Technological Benefits program.

West-Tech Finishing Inc. was established in 1988 and operates from a single facility in Vaughan, Ontario. It finishes customer-supplied aluminum and stainless steel parts, from prototype through full production runs. It publishes an SGS-issued AS9100 D / ISO 9001:2015 certificate and a Nadcap chemical processing accreditation. It names aerospace and defence manufacturers among its clients and serves customers across Canada and the USA.

Spartec Composites Inc. is a privately held composites manufacturer in Erin, Ontario that states it has operated for more than 40 years. It runs resin infusion (VARTM), hand lay-up, prepreg and autoclave curing, plus CNC textile cutting, robotic waterjet and router trimming, 3D printing, urethane casting and metal fabrication across four facilities. It states it supplies defence and aerospace work as well as automotive, marine and industrial parts. In May 2026 it announced a three-party teaming agreement with Hanwha Ocean and Kolon Spaceworks in support of Hanwha Ocean's bid for the Canadian Patrol Submarine Project.

International Custom Products Inc. (ICP) has operated since 1985 as a cut-and-sew contractor and engineer of mechanically stitched textile products. It supplies defence and aerospace customers with items such as parachutes, load carriage systems, propellant bags and shelters, and supplies logistics, banking and commercial customers with mail bags, scanner holsters and carrying cases. Work is done at a 67,000 sq ft facility in Toronto with automated cutting, stitching and heat-sealing and welding of textiles. The company states ISO 9001:2015 certification and Controlled Goods Program registration.

Shark Marine Technologies Inc. has operated from St. Catharines, Ontario since 1984 and says it designs and manufactures underwater navigation, sonar imaging and communication systems. Its products include the Navigator, Dive Tablet II and E-TAC diver-held units, the MAKO diver delivery system, remotely operated vehicles and DiveLog software. It says its equipment is in service with navies, police, scientists and commercial divers in more than 30 nations. It also offers in-house and on-site training, and its navigation units are integrated with the Patriot3 Hammerhead vehicle and JetBoots.

Ontario Tech University (legal name University of Ontario Institute of Technology) is an Oshawa university that teaches and does research in artificial intelligence, energy, nuclear, engineering and cybersecurity. Its ACE Research and Testing Facility rents climatic, aerodynamic and vibration test environments to industry, government and research clients, and is registered under the Controlled Goods Program. ACE is a designated NATO DIANA test centre, and the university has qualified as a supplier in the federal Defence Drone Initiative Marketplace under Stream 5, Innovation and Experimentation. In May 2026 FedDev Ontario announced $5 million to expand ACE as a defence technology hub.

SKADI Cyber Defense Corporation is a Canadian cybersecurity company headquartered in Bracebridge, Ontario. Its platform, Frostbow™, ingests alerts from existing SIEM, EDR and firewall tools and resolves them without analyst intervention. It escalates a small share of alerts to SKADI's own security team. The company states that its customers include enterprise clients, managed service providers, and organizations in healthcare, mining, legal services, manufacturing and critical infrastructure, with a growing presence in defence-adjacent sectors. It reports a June 2026 reseller partnership with Sharp Electronics of Canada.

Colt Canada Corporation is a small arms manufacturer headquartered at 1036 Wilson Avenue, Kitchener, Ontario, and part of the Colt CZ Group. It produces the C7/C8 rifle family, the C20 sniper weapon, the new C25 carbine selected by the Department of National Defence, and the Eagle 40mm launcher, and it also offers the CZ P-10 pistol. The company says it has maintained Canadian Armed Forces small arms for over 50 years, including repair, overhaul and fleet upgrades. It also delivers factory armourer and operator training and supplies customers in the UK, the Netherlands, Norway and Denmark.

Marswell Metal Industries Ltd. (Mars Metal Company) has operated since 1979 from 4140 Morris Drive, Burlington, Ontario. It makes custom lead castings, ballast, counterweights, test weights and radiation shielding, with in-house pattern making, CNC machining, fabrication and finishing. Its MarsKeel division supplies marine ballast, and in March 2026 the company announced a subcontract from Irving Shipbuilding for lead ballast components for the River-class destroyers. It publishes ISO 9001:2015 and CSA N299.3-16 registrations and a Controlled Goods Program registration.

Zentek develops and commercializes graphene-enabled coatings (ZenGUARD, ZenFire, ZenICE, ZenArmor and ZEN-EMI-01) on a model where the client funds development and Zentek retains the intellectual property. It operates a coating line and a laboratory in Guelph, holds an exclusive McMaster University licence for aptamer technology through its subsidiary Triera Biosciences, and owns the Albany graphite deposit near Hearst, Ontario through Albany Graphite Corp. The company is listed on the TSX Venture Exchange (ZEN) and quoted on the OTCQX (ZTEKF), and reported 10 full-time employees at June 30, 2026.

MG Chemicals (M.G. Chemicals Ltd.) is an independently owned manufacturer and wholesaler of chemical products for the electronics industry, founded in 1955. Its Burlington, Ontario head office also serves as its manufacturing and operations site. Products are sold through a network of distributors in Canada, the United States, Europe and internationally, and the company's published material describes use in aerospace, defence, automotive, telecommunications and data centre electronics. The Burlington site holds an ISO 9001:2015 certificate issued by Intertek.

MTC was founded in 2000 and is privately held. It runs a Canadian campus in Bowmanville, Ontario and a second facility in Fort Wayne, Indiana. Its services include OEM-authorized repair, returns management, refurbishment, medical device repair, vehicle up-fitting for emergency fleets, and blister packaging and fulfillment. For defence customers it publishes bench repair of combat radios and night-vision equipment, and says it is registered in the Controlled Goods Program. It states ISO 9001, ISO 14001 and ISO 13485 certification through Intertek.

Ribbit designs autopilots, optionally piloted aircraft and uncrewed systems in-house, using proprietary software and commercial off-the-shelf components. It retrofits small legacy aircraft for autonomous cargo flights, with Canada's North as its first target. It has a federal contract with Transport Canada to test autonomous cargo flights and has received National Research Council IRAP funding for detect-and-avoid, emergency landing and airdrop navigation software. The company says it serves civilian, defence and humanitarian agencies.

A. Berger Precision Ltd. operates from a facility in Brampton, Ontario that serves as the Berger Group's North American headquarters. It manufactures precision machined components to customer specifications, with a research and development centre and co-engineering services added after a 2023 FedDev Ontario investment. The company states that it holds ISO 9001, AS9100, IATF 16949, ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 certifications and is ITAR registered and registered in the Controlled Goods Program.

A-Arctic describes itself as a Canadian defence technology company focused on data trust, verification and audit across multi-domain operations. Its Arctic Shield platform has four modules (Polaris, Sentinel North, Borealis AI and IceWall) and uses distributed ledger architecture to record data origin, integrity and chain of custody. The company states that it builds on technologies developed by ADAM and does not build AI systems itself. In 2026 it announced an equity position in the software company Iron Thicket.

Accelerate: Canada's ZEV Supply Chain Alliance describes itself as a non-partisan, not-for-profit initiative covering mining, batteries, fuel cells, research and development, vehicle manufacturing, labour and infrastructure. It publishes reports, the Canadian Battery Innovation Roadmap and an interactive ZEV supply chain map. It also runs advocacy work, events and an industry platform for partners. It states that it takes no financial interest in commercial projects in the ZEV ecosystem.
operating_name: Accelerate: Canada's ZEV Supply Chain Alliance

abstract_en: Achieva Tech Incorporated provides board-level cybersecurity advisory services based on NIST CSF 2.0, ITSG-33, CMMC and CPCSC practices. Its services include pre-assessment, evidence packs, proposal attestation and ITB/VP and teaming eligibility screening for defence supply-chain firms. It also sells CMMC playbooks and documentation toolkits and delivers CyberAB CMMC Certified Professional and Certified Assessor training as an Approved Training Provider. Its sole named principal is Arnold Villeneuve, who is listed as Director.

Alchemy Labs Inc. is a Kitchener, Ontario nanotechnology company that says it was founded in 2013 by University of Waterloo nanotechnology engineering graduates. Its automotive unit sells ExoShield windshield protection film, which uses its Endurance Class nanoceramic coating. Its defence unit, Crypsis, develops multi-spectral and thermal-infrared camouflage coatings for fabrics and rigid substrates. The company is listed on the TSX Venture Exchange (ALCH) and has taken part in the NATO DIANA accelerator.

Algonquin Bridge designs, fabricates and supplies prefabricated steel bridges and bridge abutment packages from a plant in Thorndale, Ontario. Its products include custom pedestrian, trail, girder and truss bridges and Bailey-style modular panel bridge systems for permanent, temporary, emergency and rental use. It states that it serves public works, transportation, railway, military, northern, mining, forestry and development customers. It is part of the AIL Group of Companies and lists ISO 9001:2015 and CWB W47.1 certifications.

Alumco Inc. operates a 20,000 sq ft aluminum foundry in Cayuga, Ontario. It produces commercial, industrial and military aluminum castings by sand and permanent mould casting. It also provides prototype patterns, alloy analysis, tensile testing, heat treatment, blast cleaning and finishing, and arranges CNC machining through partner shops. X-ray and dye penetrant inspection are subcontracted. The company states ISO 9001:2015 certification.

Anavo Capital describes itself as a partner-owned holding company that buys Canadian manufacturing and defence businesses and does not plan to sell them. It says it focuses on precision machining, aerospace, defence contracting and nuclear sectors, and on companies with annual revenues of $3M to $20M. Its leadership team states that it has led or co-led 17 acquisitions since 2022. The website does not name any portfolio companies.

Armatec Survivability Corp. is a Canadian-owned defence manufacturer in Dorchester, Ontario that applies aerospace design methods to ground vehicle survivability. It develops, produces, installs and supports passive protection systems and automotive and mobility upgrades for wheeled and tracked armoured vehicles. Its campus includes a 300,000 square foot facility with an indoor ballistics test range, a hill climb area and an off-road test track. It reports AS9100D and ISO 9001:2015 certificates issued by Intertek.

Arrow Machine and Fabrication Group Inc. is a Guelph, Ontario company that owns CGL Manufacturing, Steelcraft, VeriForm, Baumeier, Lumar Machining and Kenona Industries, organized into four divisions: Arrow Off-Road, Arrow Engineered Products, Arrow Automotive and Arrow Precision Machining. It supplies machined castings, fabrications and assemblies to OEM customers in off-road equipment, rail, mining, defence, nuclear, heavy truck and related industries from plants in Ontario, Michigan and China. It states about 900 team members and lists ISO 9001, AS9100, ISO 14001 and CWB welding certifications.
operating_name: Arrow Machine and Fabrication Group / CGL Manufacturing Inc.

abstract_en: AIM Robotics is a Waterloo, Ontario technology company that says it was founded in 2019 and builds software connecting drones, airspace data, sensors and operators. Its products are RPAS WILCO (flight planning, compliance, fleet records and a pilot marketplace), SafeAirspace (RF-based drone detection and authorization correlation) and MANTIS (a common operational picture that works with TAK). The company says it qualified under Stream 1 of the Government of Canada's Defence Drone Initiative Marketplace and was selected for the Department of National Defence's CUAS 2026 sandbox. It also serves airports, public safety agencies and recreational and commercial drone pilots.

Atlantic Industries Limited (AIL) was founded in 1965 and describes itself as a Canadian-owned designer and manufacturer of buried metal bridges, culverts, pipe and drainage systems, retaining walls, abutments and sound barrier walls. It operates manufacturing plants and sales and engineering offices from Newfoundland to British Columbia and sells to transportation, public works, railway, mining and energy, forestry and development customers. Its published projects include stream crossings at CFB Gagetown, supplied through Defence Construction Canada and a contractor. The company belongs to The AIL Group of Companies, whose sister companies include Algonquin Bridge, AIL Sound Walls, AIL Mining and AIL International.

Aversan Inc. is a Mississauga-based engineering and electronics manufacturing company that says it was established in 2003. It develops certifiable airborne electronics and embedded software, builds PCB assemblies and box builds, and designs automated test equipment and hardware-in-the-loop systems integration labs (AvSIL). It also provides DO-178 and DO-254 verification and validation, MRO and reverse engineering of avionics, and engineering staff augmentation. Its published project work covers civil and military aircraft programs, F-35 software testing and Canadarm3 ground test equipment.

AVRO Precision Laboratories Inc. describes itself as an industrial initiative that is building a vertically integrated Canadian defence manufacturing platform. Its website lists precision manufacturing, systems integration, quality and traceability, compliance and sustainment, and training and readiness. It states that it is the exclusive Canadian military and law enforcement distributor for Hornady Law Enforcement duty ammunition, and a Canadian distribution partner for Torraka operational workwear. It says its manufacturing follows NATO STANAG specifications, with AS9100D and AQAP-2110 as quality "pathways". The site gives no equipment, facility or certificate details.

Aerial Vehicle Safety Solutions Inc. was founded in 2017 and develops safety and delivery hardware and software for commercial, public safety, military and government drone operators. Its products include ASTM F3322-based parachute recovery systems for DJI platforms, guided and unguided resupply systems, the Precision Avalanche Management System, and a newer line of drone motors, speed controllers, cameras and ground control stations. It reports selling through more than 70 distribution partners and exporting to many countries. It has federal Innovative Solutions Canada testing contracts and is on the first supplier list of the federal Defence Drone Initiative Marketplace.
operating_name: AVSS - Aerial Vehicle Safety Solutions Inc.

abstract_en: Ballvale Strategy Inc. was created in 2020 by John E. Ball, a former General Dynamics Land Systems Canada programs director. It provides defence and security business consulting. This covers defence requirements, the federal procurement process and Industrial and Technological Benefits, and helps clients engage federal agencies and original equipment manufacturers. The company states that some client support counts as lobbying under the Lobbying Act and that it complies with that Act.

The Barrington Consulting Group has operated since 2004 from its head office in Halifax, Nova Scotia, with offices in New Brunswick, Newfoundland and Labrador and Ontario. It provides strategy and advisory, business transformation, digital services, privacy and information security, project management, applied research and training services. Its defence service line supports defence programs and bids, and the firm states it is Canadian-owned and delivers 100% Canadian Content Value in ITB-eligible work. It names Fleetway Inc. (Integrated Data Environment Program) and Halifax Transit among its clients.

Berwick IT Inc. is a consulting firm led by Flavien Berwick, based in Ottawa. Its published material describes cloud and infrastructure engineering, DevOps, site reliability engineering, cloud architecture and digital sovereignty advisory work. The owner states a specialization in defence and government DevOps. No customers, certifications, headcount or physical facilities are published.

Biiwaabik Contracting Inc. is an Indigenous-owned industrial construction firm based in New Liskeard, Ontario. It states that it serves clients in energy, mining, infrastructure, manufacturing and large-scale industrial development. Its published services include project management, consulting, civil and structural work, health, safety and environment, ironworking, pipe fitting, welding, millwrighting and electrical work. It also states an aim to provide defence-related construction services to the Department of National Defence and the Canadian Armed Forces.

Bioindustrial Innovation Canada (BIC) was founded in 2008 and is based in Sarnia, Ontario. It invests in and advises early-stage bioproduct and sustainable chemistry companies. It also runs cluster and network programs, including COMM SCI, the AgSci cluster project, the Biomass Quality Network Canada and the CONNECT Program for small and medium-sized enterprises. It makes no physical products. It also publishes commentary on dual-use bioeconomy applications for defence and resilience.

Biokinetics and Associates Limited is an Ottawa engineering firm that has worked in human injury biomechanics since 1975. It runs laboratories for ballistics, impact and drone safety, and tests helmets, body armour, body padding, less-lethal munitions and drones against published standards. It also designs and sells its own test devices, such as the Ballistic Load Sensing Headform and the Blunt Trauma Thoracic Rig, and does contract engineering research and development. Its clients include government agencies, manufacturers and individual inventors.

BKS Technical Solutions describes itself as a Canadian application sales engineering company with over 20 years of experience in the aerospace, defence, naval and industrial transportation sectors. It acts as the Canadian sales representative for European, American and Canadian manufacturers ("Principals"), getting their products specified and designed into customer applications. It lists rugged electronics, power, cable management and shock and vibration products by sector. It does not publish manufacturing, certification or facility information.

BlackBerry Limited is a publicly traded Canadian software company headquartered in Waterloo, Ontario, founded in 1984. Its QNX division supplies safety-certified operating systems, hypervisors and development tools for automotive, medical, industrial, aerospace and defence embedded systems. Its Secure Communications division supplies certified voice and messaging encryption (SecuSUITE), endpoint management (UEM) and crisis communications (AtHoc) to governments and regulated industries. It also licenses a patent portfolio of about 6,100 patents and applications.

BluMetric provides environmental geoscience and engineering, site assessment and remediation, industrial hygiene and occupational health and safety, and surveying and GIS services to industrial, mining, government and military clients. Through its WaterTech Canada division in Carp, Ontario, it designs, builds and services reverse osmosis water purification units, shipboard desalination and oily water separation systems, and mobile wastewater treatment plants. It reports contracts with the Department of National Defence, Rheinmetall Canada and Thales Canada, and a supply contract with an unnamed Canadian shipbuilder. It is listed on the TSX Venture Exchange as BLM.

BMT Canada Ltd. (formerly BMT Fleet Technology Ltd.) is an engineering and technical consultancy headquartered in Kanata, Ontario, with offices in Ottawa, Victoria, Calgary and Halifax/Dartmouth. It supports the Royal Canadian Navy and Department of National Defence through engineering, logistics and management support, submarine in-service support and National Shipbuilding Strategy programs. It also works in energy and environment, including a prototype smart microgrid tested in Nova Scotia. BMT Group Ltd., the parent, is owned by an employee benefit trust.

Brotech Precision CNC Inc. has machined parts to customer specifications since 1995 at its plant at 711 Bayview Drive in Barrie, Ontario, with a second site in Owen Sound. It runs 25 CNC machines (including 9-axis mill-turn and 5-axis centres) and 4 CMMs. Its work includes CANDU nuclear components for Bruce Power, landing gear parts for aerospace Tier 1 suppliers, and defence parts such as components for the US Navy CSTRS winch programme supplied through Rolls-Royce. It publishes ISO 9001, AS9100 Rev D, CSA N299.3 and Controlled Goods Program credentials.

Cambrian R&D, established in 2009, is the applied research division of Cambrian College and works with companies on funded projects using college faculty, students and facilities. Its equipment includes a 5-axis CNC machine, waterjet and laser cutters, polymer and metal 3D printers, a handheld 3D scanner, a climatic test chamber and an analytical chemistry lab. The Centre for Smart Mining, an NSERC-supported Technology Access Centre, helps mining technology companies adopt new technology. Recent projects include a lifting system and toboggan for the RufDiamond Fat Truck, a platform the project says could serve defence, mining, forestry and emergency response.

Canada Cyber Weapons Centre Limited operates as Canada Cyber Warfare. Its website describes cyber weapons development, hybrid and multi-domain warfare platforms, cyber and space warfare command centres, an augmented reality military-intelligence system, and training and intelligence operations. It says its clients are intelligence agencies, military and defence bodies, defence companies and government entities, and it does not name them. The site publishes no address, phone number, named staff, certifications or founding year.

Canadore College is a public college of applied arts and technology with three campuses in North Bay, Ontario. Its Aviation Campus has a hangar with fixed and rotary wing aircraft and a simulation wing for aircraft maintenance training. It also has an applied research centre and a cybersecurity program. It is a designated Military-Connected College, and Department of National Defence training contracts appear in federal contract records.

Cantec Systems is an Ottawa company that describes itself as an authorized Canadian Value Added Centre for power products. It supplies lead-acid, nickel-cadmium, nickel-metal hydride and lithium batteries, chargers and inverters, and builds custom battery packs and cables in its Ottawa facility. It also offers load testing, lithium battery testing and certification support, installation, maintenance and a battery recycling program. Public procurement records show Department of National Defence battery supply contracts.

Captec Americas Inc. is the Canadian operation of the UK-headquartered Captec Group, based at 15 Saltsman Drive in Cambridge, Ontario. It engineers, integrates and supports rugged and industrial computers, servers, displays, integrated racks, consoles and subsystems. Defence work includes naval bridge consoles, rugged servers and equipment enclosures. The company states that it works with defence OEMs, system integrators and prime contractors. It also supplies industrial, energy, healthcare, rail and simulation customers.

CCX Technologies Inc. is a 100% Canadian-owned firm, founded in 2017 in Ottawa, that designs and manufactures networking and computing equipment for real-time operational networks used mainly in aerospace and defence. Its products include secure routers, data-bus interfaces (DataPHYs), servers, a tactical console, antennas, software-defined radios and the SystemX operating system with the Falcon avionics intrusion detection system. It also provides a security operations centre, penetration testing and cybersecurity audits, and customized or white-label versions of its hardware and software. It states that it holds Transport Canada Approved Maintenance Organization and Approved Manufacturing Organization status and is CMMC Level 2 compliant.

CFN Consultants was founded in 1983 and is headquartered in Ottawa, with offices in the Atlantic region and on the west coast. Its partners and associates are mainly former senior military officers and public servants. It provides analysis, strategic planning, competitive bid support, socio-economic benefit (ITB, value proposition and Indigenous procurement) planning and contract management for private-sector clients.

Invest Barrie is the Economic Development Department of the City of Barrie, Ontario, with a business and tourism development branch and a Small Business Centre. It offers site selection and development process facilitation, talent recruitment, business retention and expansion, trade missions and tariff and export advisory services. It promotes advanced manufacturing, defence and security, mining supply, health and life sciences, tourism and arts and culture. On May 28, 2026 the Mayor announced a $50 million incentive to attract defence industry investment.

The City of Hamilton is a single-tier municipality in Ontario. Its Economic Development division operates the Invest in Hamilton program, which promotes the city to investors and supports local businesses. Services include municipal grants and loans, the Hamilton Business Centre for small business, Global Hamilton for foreign direct investment, tariff-response information, and business development staff assigned to sectors such as manufacturing, life sciences, agri-food, goods movement, ICT and tourism.

The City of Mississauga is a municipal government in Peel Region, Ontario, incorporated in 1974. Its Economic Development Division, branded Invest Mississauga, is based in City Hall and provides site selection, data analytics, talent and workforce connections, export and supply-chain introductions, and funding and program guidance. It also runs sector programs for advanced manufacturing, defence, life sciences, technology, smart logistics and creative industries. A small-business arm, IDEA Mississauga, supports entrepreneurs.

The Corporation of the City of St. Catharines is a municipal government in the Niagara region of Ontario. Through its economic development department, branded Invest in St. Catharines or TeamSTC, it offers business retention and expansion, investment attraction, relocation support, market research, trade missions and small business advising through the St. Catharines Enterprise Centre. It names manufacturing, agriculture and food and beverage, healthcare, creative industries, tourism and professional and technical services as priority sectors. It does not manufacture or sell products and has no published certifications.

CMI Heavy Industries operates a large manufacturing shop at 2677 Winger Road, Stevensville, Ontario, with 100-ton lifting capacity. Its published services are CNC turning and boring-mill machining, plate fabrication, robotic and submerged-arc welding and cladding, assembly and testing, strip and rebuild, sandblasting and painting, and engineering design. Its published examples cover rolls, shafts, gearboxes, turbine components and crusher parts for steel mills, mining and power generation, and paper mills. FedDev Ontario announced a $1 million Regional Tariff Response Initiative contribution for new heavy machining equipment in July 2026.

Compound Metal Coatings Inc. is a Mississauga, Ontario coating job shop founded in 2001. It plates customer parts with electroless nickel (including PTFE, boron nitride and ceramic composites), immersion gold and PVD/DLC coatings, working with a sister company on PVD. It serves plastic tooling, aerospace, defence and navy, nuclear, oil and gas, automotive, medical, mining and electronics customers. It also offers coating consulting and customized training courses.

The Corporation of the City of Oshawa is a lower-tier municipality in Durham Region, Ontario. Its Oshawa Economic Development team offers site selection assistance, business retention and expansion support, community improvement plan incentives, and tariff-response advocacy. In 2025 the City proposed an integrated National Defence Innovation Corridor linking defence manufacturing, multimodal distribution, R&D, training and border security. It does not manufacture products or sell commercial goods.
operating_name: Corporation of the City of Oshawa

abstract_en: CyberCare Pro provides cybersecurity compliance consulting, implementation, managed security services and training to small and mid-size businesses and non-profits in Ontario, Florida and Texas. Its CMMC and CPCSC Level 1 and Level 2 readiness program is aimed at contractors and sub-contractors in the defence supply chain. Services include risk assessments, penetration testing, virtual CISO (vCISO) services, compliance-as-a-service and a managed security technology stack. The team is made up of named partners and freelance professionals, led by its president, Marguerite Fleming.

CybernetIQ Inc. is an Ottawa-based cybersecurity software developer, incorporated federally in 2009 as Red Tiger Security Ltd. and renamed in 2016. Its flagship product, CLAW (Control Layer Assessment Workstation), combines network and cybersecurity data from multiple tools into one 3D interface for security analysts. The company says CLAW began with a Defence Research and Development Canada grant and has had federal government clients. It also publishes a resiliency risk report and describes consulting and training services.

Dajcor Aluminum Ltd. began operating in Chatham, Ontario in 2010 and opened a second plant in Chavies, Kentucky in 2020. It runs four extrusion presses and offers design support, CNC machining, tube laser cutting, welding, anodizing and painting. Its published markets include automotive and EV, construction, industrial automation, medical, renewable energy, and defence, security and infrastructure. It states a combined workforce of over 300 and ISO 9001:2015 certification.

Donmac Precision Machining Inc. is a Canadian-owned, family-run manufacturer of custom, build-to-print precision machined components from a 12,000 sq ft plant in Foxboro, Ontario. It runs CNC mill-turn and Swiss lathes, in-house inspection and automated assembly cells, and supplies defence primes with ordnance, ordnance assemblies and naval and land-systems components. It also serves aerospace, medical, electronics and fluid power customers, and offers prototype runs and manufacturing consulting. It states ISO 9001:2015 certification since 2009 and AS9100 as in progress.

Doyletech Corporation describes itself as Canada's first innovation consultancy, operating since 1981 and federally incorporated in 1982. It provides strategic and business planning, market research, intellectual property management and technology transfer advice, and economic development and industrial analysis. Its clients include federal and provincial departments and agencies, technology start-ups and established companies. It sells services only and does not manufacture products.

General Dynamics Land Systems–Canada is a London, Ontario operation that has built armoured vehicles since 1977, when it was the General Motors Diesel Division. It designs, manufactures, integrates and sustains light armoured vehicles (LAV II, LAV III, LAV 6.0, LAV 700) and offers the EAGLE tactical vehicle family. Its support services include field technical services, training, supply support and technical publications. It also leads integration and in-service support on the Logistics Vehicle Modernization project. The company states that it employs about 1,700 people and that more than 85 percent of its revenue comes from exports.

The Information and Communications Technology Council (ICTC) is a neutral, not-for-profit organization that began in 1992 as the Software Human Resources Council. It publishes research reports and policy briefs on the digital economy and labour market. It also offers services such as economic impact analysis, strategy development and data analytics. Its employment and skills programs, including work-integrated learning, AI bootcamps and cybersecurity education for students, are delivered under the eTalent Canada banner. It states a team of over 100 experts.

Invest Brampton is the brand of the City of Brampton's Economic Development Office, located inside City Hall. It is organized into investment services, investment attraction, sector management, the Brampton Innovation District and the Brampton Entrepreneur Centre. It runs the Brampton Business Growth Accelerator, a two-year program funded by FedDev Ontario that helps local firms diversify into defence, aerospace, space and advanced manufacturing supply chains. It also runs the Global Business Centre for export support and publishes sector profiles for advanced manufacturing, space, defence and cybersecurity, and other sectors.

Invest WindsorEssex is a not-for-profit organization supported by the City of Windsor and the County of Essex, and it is the lead economic development agency for the region. It works with companies and entrepreneurs on attracting investment, retaining and expanding existing businesses, and starting new ones. Its departments cover automobility and innovation, business retention and expansion, investment attraction, small business and entrepreneurship, and marketing and communications. It also publishes a regional supplier directory called Source WindsorEssex and runs defence supply chain awareness activities for local manufacturers.

London Economic Development Corporation (LEDC) was established in 1998 and is funded by the City of London through a Purchase of Service Agreement. It works with businesses, governments and academic institutions to attract foreign direct investment, retain and expand local employers, and connect companies with talent and sites. It publishes a free business directory of more than 2,000 local businesses and a local procurement search tool. It promotes a London defence and aerospace manufacturing cluster and does not make products itself.

Mitacs Inc. is a federally incorporated not-for-profit with its head office in Vancouver and offices in more than 25 Canadian cities. It runs programs such as Accelerate, Accelerate Entrepreneur, Business Strategy Internship, Mitacs AI Advantage and Globalink, in which partner organizations co-fund paid research placements. It works with nearly 200 post-secondary institutions and is funded by the Government of Canada and provincial and territorial governments. In 2026 it launched an Accelerate Defence and Security call delivered in collaboration with the Department of National Defence.

The Ontario Association of Certified Engineering Technicians and Technologists (OACETT) is a non-profit regulatory body and professional association with over 21,000 members. It confers the C.Tech. and C.E.T. certifications, runs a code of ethics and disciplinary process, and offers continuing professional development and a job board. It is organized into six regions and 27 chapters, and it carries out government relations on behalf of its members. It does not manufacture products.

AeroWR is led by the Region of Waterloo and directed with industry, academic and government partners. It runs an industry roundtable, partners on the Aerospace Accelerator program with the Accelerator Centre and Skywise, and promotes the Region of Waterloo International Airport (YKF) and local suppliers. It does not manufacture products itself; its website lists local aerospace, aviation and defence organizations as its ecosystem.

The Regional Municipality of Niagara is the regional government of 12 local area municipalities, headquartered in Thorold, Ontario. Its Niagara Economic Development team offers investor support, expedited development services, a Foreign Trade Zone point, tariff-response resources and site-selection help. It employs a Defence Sector Program Manager, hosted a Niagara-focused Defence Sector Workshop with the Niagara Industrial Association, and is launching the Thrive Niagara initiative for advanced manufacturing, defence and aerospace, and automotive. It does not manufacture or sell products.

Rogers Cybersecure Catalyst was established in 2018 as a centre of Toronto Metropolitan University. It delivers cybersecurity training, corporate and law enforcement training, a cyber range, and programs for startups and small businesses, as well as policy and research work. It also publishes a defence resource hub with webinars on defence procurement for Canadian small and medium-sized businesses. It publishes no products and no quality certifications.

The Corporation of the City of Peterborough is the municipal government of Peterborough, Ontario, led by a mayor and ten councillors and administered by a Chief Administrative Officer. It operates Peterborough Regional Airport, which hosts more than 20 aviation and aerospace businesses. Its economic development division promotes the aerospace, defence, nuclear, advanced manufacturing and cleantech sectors. It also publishes a tariff-support resource page that links local firms to federal and provincial programs. It does not manufacture products.

abstract_en: Georgian College is a multi-campus Ontario college, established in 1967, with its head office in Barrie. Its Research and Innovation department works with industry and community partners on industrial simulation and prototyping, digital and AI projects, and community data analytics. The Centre of Industrial Simulation and Prototyping is an NSERC-designated Technology Access Centre that offers digital twins, robotics and automation, electromagnetics and acoustics, and energy systems simulation. The college also delivers training to the Canadian Armed Forces and has partnership agreements with CFB Borden and the Royal Canadian Navy.

Niagara College operates campuses in Welland and Niagara-on-the-Lake, Ontario, and publishes that it has more than 10,500 full-time students. Its Research and Innovation division works with small and medium-sized businesses through applied research projects, technical services and course-based projects. WAMIC in Welland offers precision metrology, 3D scanning, reverse engineering, additive manufacturing, engineering design and Industry 4.0 support to automotive, aerospace, agri-food and machinery manufacturers. In 2026 the college launched Defence Systems Engineering Technology programs focused on aerial, terrestrial and marine drones.

The Regional Municipality of York, headquartered in Newmarket, Ontario, has served York Region's nine cities and towns since 1971. Its Economic Strategy team runs the York Link platform and provides site selection, soft landing, talent, government incentive and small business support to companies in or entering the region. In 2026 York Link published a Canadian Defence Market Entry Roadmap and a supplier directory of defence-ready and high-potential manufacturers in the region. The organization is a municipal government and does not manufacture defence products itself.

The University of Guelph's Office of Research supports a research enterprise that the university describes as worth about $201 million. The enterprise covers all eight colleges and the Ontario Agri-Food Innovation Alliance, a partnership with the Government of Ontario that supports 13 research centre sites. The Research Innovation Office manages patenting, licensing and commercialization, and the university offers industry, government and community partners several routes to collaborate. The university is registered in the federal Controlled Goods Program.

The University of Waterloo opened in 1957 and has its main campus at 200 University Avenue West in Waterloo, Ontario, with satellite campuses in Cambridge, Kitchener and Stratford. It reports $286M in research funding in 2024/25 and 1,160+ research partnerships with industry, government agencies and non-profits. Its research units include the Institute for Quantum Computing, the Cybersecurity and Privacy Institute, the Waterloo Institute for Nanotechnology and the Waterloo Institute for Sustainable Aeronautics. It is registered with the Controlled Goods Program and has received Department of National Defence research funding.

Western University was founded in 1878 and is based in London, Ontario. Its Office of Innovation and Strategic Partnerships handles industry, government and community research collaborations, technology transfer and licensing. The university publishes a dual-use research program covering sensing, autonomy, secure communications, advanced materials and energy, and health security. It runs facilities such as Surface Science Western, WindEEE and the Fraunhofer Innovation Platform for Composites Research. It is listed in the federal Controlled Goods Program registry.

Wescam Inc. operates as L3Harris WESCAM, a division of L3Harris Technologies' Integrated Mission Systems segment. It designs and builds the gyro-stabilized MX-Series EO/IR turrets and sighting systems at a 330,000-square-foot facility in Waterdown, Ontario. A Toronto (Don Mills) site makes and coats opto-mechanical lens assemblies. The company also provides maintenance, repair, in-service support and operator training through factory teams and a network of WESCAM Authorized Service Centers. Published Canadian customers include the Royal Canadian Air Force, through the Canadian Commercial Corporation.

Bell Textron Canada Limited is the Canadian operation of Bell, a helicopter manufacturer owned by Textron Inc. Its Mirabel, Quebec site covers design, engineering, composite manufacturing, final assembly, flight testing, certification, customization, paint and aftermarket support for Bell light and medium helicopters. A Calgary, Alberta supply centre distributes spare parts to Canadian operators and to Canadian Forces bases. The company states it holds the Government of Canada in-service support contract for the CH-146 Griffon fleet.

Bombardier Defense was launched in 2022 as an evolution of Bombardier's Specialized Aircraft division and is headquartered in the United States at Wichita, Kansas, within Bombardier Inc. of Dorval, Quebec. It offers turnkey packages covering the design, build, testing and certification of mission-modified Global and Challenger aircraft, as well as engineering support and in-service support. Its aircraft serve intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance, maritime patrol, airborne early warning, medical evacuation and head-of-state transport missions with operators in more than 50 countries. Global aircraft are assembled in the Greater Toronto Area and completed in Greater Montreal.

De Havilland Aircraft of Canada Limited is a Calgary-based aircraft manufacturer founded in 1928 that holds Transport Canada design, manufacturing and maintenance approvals. It builds turboprop and amphibious firefighting aircraft, offers special mission configurations of the Dash 8 and Twin Otter through its De Havilland Defence brand, and supports a fleet it states at over 3,000 aircraft. Its customers named in published news include airlines, the French civil security service and the Royal Canadian Air Force training program, and it is building the De Havilland Field aerospace campus in Wheatland County, Alberta.

Field Aviation Company Inc. trades as Field Aerospace and is the Canadian operating arm of a US-owned aircraft modification group that has operated in Canada since 1947. It engineers, installs, tests and certifies modifications, including special mission and intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (ISR) integration, avionics modernization and VIP interiors, and holds a stated portfolio of more than 130 supplemental type certificates (STCs) on 64 aircraft types. The company filed a notice of intention to make a proposal under the Bankruptcy and Insolvency Act on June 5, 2026, and trade press and court-linked reporting say substantially all of its assets were sold on July 31, 2026, so the record needs close review.

PAL Aerospace, a subsidiary of Exchange Income Corporation, designs, certifies and installs aircraft modifications and supplemental type certificate kits, and holds a Transport Canada Design Approval Organization number. It develops and sells AIMS-ISR and AIMS-C4 mission software through its CarteNav business, and builds operator consoles and equipment racks for special mission aircraft. It also operates contractor-owned surveillance aircraft under its Force Multiplier Program, and provides maintenance, in-service support and aircrew and uncrewed aircraft training. Its published customers include the Netherlands Coastguard, the UK Home Office, Air Greenland and, through SkyAlyne, the Royal Canadian Air Force.

MDS Aero Support Corporation, founded in 1985 and headquartered in Ottawa, designs and delivers full engine and engine component test facilities for aviation, industrial and marine gas turbines. It also supplies special purpose test equipment, the nxDAS data acquisition software, project management, engineering services, and aftermarket support such as calibration, maintenance and spares management. The company describes itself as a Tier 1 supplier to engine manufacturers and maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) firms, with support offices in the UK, Germany, China and India and an icing test site at Thompson, Manitoba.

Cascade Aerospace Inc. is an operating unit of IMP Aerospace & Defence, headquartered at Abbotsford International Airport in British Columbia, with a site at CFB Trenton and an Ottawa business development office. It is a Transport Canada Design Approval Organization and an authorized Lockheed Martin C-130 Service Center and C-130J Heavy Maintenance Center, and it also supports Boeing 737/757 and Bombardier Q400/CRJ and CL-215/415 aircraft. Its on-site shops cover non-destructive testing, sheet metal, composites, interiors, painting and hydraulics, and it supplies Class E package freighter conversion kits for the Q400 and CRJ. Named customers in its own releases include the Royal Canadian Air Force, the U.S. Navy and Marine Corps, the Mexican Air Force and the Bangladesh Air Force.

MHD-ROCKLAND is a Canadian aftermarket supplier of parts and services for legacy fixed-wing aircraft, headquartered in Sainte-Anne-de-Bellevue, Quebec, with sites in Ontario, the United States, Australia and New Zealand. Its Burlington, Ontario unit, MHD-R Tech Ops, repairs, overhauls and manufactures flight control actuators under an exclusive licence from Collins Aerospace for Bombardier CRJ and Fokker regional jets. The company also holds a large P-3 and C-130 parts inventory, owns a propeller repair shop in Washington State, and runs P-3 flight training and flight testing with five P-3C aircraft in Florida. It sells to military and government operators and to commercial operators.

EarthDaily Analytics operates the EarthDaily Constellation, a satellite system that images most of Earth's landmass daily in 22 spectral bands, and processes the imagery into analysis-ready data and analytics products. Its products serve agriculture, mining, forestry, insurance, civil government, and defence and intelligence users, including persistent change detection, tip-and-cue and maritime domain awareness. The company states it was created in 2021 with Antarctica Capital and has since acquired Descartes Labs and SkyForest. In September 2026 it announced a Government of Canada National Master Standing Offer for commercial satellite imagery.

MDA Space is a TSX-listed Canadian company headquartered in Brampton, Ontario, with three business areas: Satellite Systems, Robotics & Space Operations, and Geointelligence. It acts as prime contractor for satellite constellations (Telesat Lightspeed and Globalstar), builds and operates robotic systems including Canadarm2 and Canadarm3, and operates RADARSAT-class radar satellites. It also supplies sensor systems for Royal Canadian Navy ships. In February 2026 it launched 49North, a wholly-owned subsidiary for defence work outside the space domain, headquartered in Ottawa.

Telesat Corporation (Nasdaq and TSX: TSAT) operates a fleet of geostationary satellites and teleports, and sells broadcast, enterprise, government and defence satellite connectivity. Its Telesat Lightspeed low Earth orbit network is being built by MDA Space and includes a Military Ka-band service for the Canadian Armed Forces. Telesat also sells satellite consulting services covering spacecraft procurement, frequency coordination, launch and testing. It has served Canada since 1969 and is headquartered in Ottawa, Ontario.

INKAS Aerospace & Defense is the defence division of the INKAS Group of Companies, headquartered at 3605 Weston Road in Toronto. It designs and builds armoured personnel carriers, MRAP vehicles and tactical vehicles, and develops the Heemar uncrewed ground vehicle, the Anuri counter-UAS interceptor drone and an uncrewed surface vessel. It also offers counter-UAS systems, airport and homeland security solutions, and operator training. The group's armoured-vehicle plant is equipped with laser cutting and bending systems. In 2026 the company announced additional production facilities in Toronto, Charlotte (North Carolina) and Fort Pierce (Florida).

Roshel Inc. is headquartered in Brampton, Ontario. It states that design, metal fabrication, welding, painting, and mechanical and electrical assembly are done in-house. Its product lines are the Senator and Captain armoured vehicles for military and law enforcement use, cash-in-transit vehicles, commercial fleet upfitting and telematics-based fleet management. It also operates a production facility in Shelby Township, Michigan. It has announced partnerships with Daimler Truck, Algoma Steel, Swebor, ST Engineering, OMNIPOL and Leonardo, and it has acquired Centigon of France.

Davie is a shipbuilder and ship repair yard in Lévis, Quebec, which says it has operated since 1825. It builds and converts icebreakers, ferries and naval auxiliary ships, and provides through-life support to the Royal Canadian Navy's surface combatant fleet. It is a partner in the National Shipbuilding Strategy and is owned by Inocea Group. In 2026 it announced Davie Autonomous Inc., an Ontario company to produce uncrewed maritime vessels with Kraken Technology Group.

CMC Electronics is a Montréal-based avionics company that designs and manufactures navigation systems, cockpit systems integration, displays and control panels, avionics computers, and optoelectronics and microelectronics. It serves military helicopters, fighter and trainer aircraft, civil helicopters, air transport and uncrewed aerial systems. It also provides repair, training and documentation support, and operates a second manufacturing site in Sugar Grove, Illinois. The company's own history dates its corporate origin to 1903, and its history page records that it passed from Esterline to TransDigm in 2019.

Evertz Microsystems Ltd. is a Canadian-owned subsidiary of Evertz Technologies Limited (TSX: ET), headquartered in Burlington, Ontario. It designs, engineers and manufactures video and audio infrastructure, software platforms and secure network equipment. Its customers include broadcasters, telecommunications firms, sports venues, universities and government agencies. In 2026 it announced roles in two Canadian defence initiatives, Babcock's Team INSPIRE and Calian's ATHORA platform.

abstract_en: GeoSpectrum Technologies Inc. has specialized in underwater acoustic transducers and systems since 1994. It makes hydrophones, sound projectors, towed and hull-mounted sonars, and the software and winch or handling systems that go with them. It reports in-house pressure and environmental chamber testing and NIST-traceable calibration equipment. Its customers include the Royal Canadian Navy, and it has been named a Preferred Supplier to Vard Marine's Team Vigilance.

Lockheed Martin Canada is headquartered in Ottawa and has facilities in Ottawa, Montreal, Halifax, Calgary and Victoria. It is the prime contractor and combat system integrator for the Halifax-class frigates and the developer of the CMS 330 combat management system, which it has also supplied to New Zealand and Chile. It also provides in-service support, training and simulation, electronic warfare support, uncrewed-systems software and industrial benefits programs for Canadian suppliers.

General Dynamics Mission Systems–Canada is a business of General Dynamics, established in 1948 and headquartered at 1941 Robertson Road, Ottawa, with offices in Dartmouth, Calgary and Sherbrooke. It supplies undersea warfare and sonobuoy processing systems, airborne mission management and training systems, tactical and naval communications, satellite ground systems integration and cyber defence capabilities. It also provides integrated logistics support, field support and in-service support. Named customers include the Department of National Defence, the Royal Canadian Navy, the Government of Panama and the Portuguese Air Force.

AtkinsRéalis Group Inc. is a publicly traded Canadian company whose roots date to 1911 and which operates globally. It offers engineering, advisory, digital, cybersecurity, project delivery, operations and maintenance, and decommissioning services across transportation, nuclear, water, power, industrial, minerals and defence markets. In Canada it is a top-five supplier to Defence Construction Canada and has a presence on most military bases. It also stewards CANDU® nuclear technology through its subsidiary Candu Energy Inc.

EXP (legal name EXP Services Inc. / Les Services EXP Inc.) provides engineering, architecture, design, consulting and project delivery services across buildings, infrastructure, earth and environment, industrial and chemical, digital, climate and operations work. It states that it has more than 4,700 employees and more than 100 offices and laboratories in North America, and that its heritage dates to 1906. It serves public and private clients in transportation, energy, water, healthcare, education, federal and mission critical markets, and in April 2026 it named a Senior Vice President, Canada Defence National to strengthen its work with Defence Construction Canada and the Department of National Defence. It is a services firm and does not publish manufactured products.

Hatch is headquartered in Mississauga, Ontario, and provides engineering, project and construction management, technology development, digital and environmental consulting services. It states a global network of 11,000 professionals and project experience in more than 150 countries. Its work covers mining and metals, energy (including nuclear and renewables) and infrastructure, and it has a defence practice focused on Arctic, aviation, maritime and power infrastructure for the Canadian Armed Forces. It also publishes proprietary technologies and software tools, such as Nsolv, Smelter Optimizer and Hydromantis GPS-X.

Marshall Land Systems is a Canadian-owned defence company with UK origins that designs and delivers deployable and mission-critical infrastructure, integrated vehicle platform solutions and managed support services. Its Ottawa office handles engineering, program management, finance and operations, and its 82,000 sq. ft. Moncton plant produces mission modules for the Canadian Armed Forces' Logistics Vehicle Modernization program and containers for the Royal Netherlands Army. The company states it has more than 600 employees across the UK, Canada and the Netherlands. It was acquired by Flowing River Capital Partners in November 2025.

Raymond EMC makes modular RF shielded enclosures, deployable QuietShelter units, shielded doors and cabinets, and EMC and anechoic chambers, and resells Eurotempest TEMPEST computing equipment. It also relocates, upgrades, tests and maintains shielded enclosures. It sells to government, military, aerospace, automotive, telecommunications, medical and research customers. Its head office is in Ottawa and its production facility is in Vars, Ontario.

CAE Inc. was incorporated in 1947 and is listed on the TSX and NYSE. Its Defense & Security segment is a platform-independent training systems integrator across air, land, maritime, cyber, space and public safety, and it is the prime contractor on the NATO Flying Training in Canada program. The company states about 13,000 employees at about 240 sites in over 40 countries, including more than 4,800 employees in Canada. Defense & Security was 42% of FY2025 revenue and Civil Aviation was 58%.

Calian was incorporated in 1982 and is headquartered in Ottawa, with offices and manufacturing sites across Canada, the United States and Europe. Its Defence & Space work includes C5ISRT systems integration, simulation-based military training for the Canadian Armed Forces and NATO, EMSEC and TEMPEST services, and MIL-STD electronics and cable harness manufacturing. It also supplies health services to the Canadian Armed Forces, IT and cybersecurity services, and nuclear, agricultural-technology and GNSS products. Calian VENTURES is its program for scaling Canadian small and mid-sized defence technology firms.

ITPS Canada operates from London International Airport (CYXU) in Ontario and runs the International Test Pilots School and, as a subsidiary division, the International Tactical Training Centre (ITTC), now based in North Bay. It delivers EASA-approved fixed and rotary wing test pilot and flight test engineer courses, uncrewed aircraft flight test courses, and degree programs approved by the Ontario Ministry of Colleges and Universities. It also supplies contracted flight test personnel and consulting, operates its own fleet of jet trainers, helicopters and the HU-16 Albatross, and is expanding into aircraft sustainment and engineering. Customers named in its own and third-party material include the Royal Canadian Air Force, the Royal Netherlands Air Force, the Royal Malaysian Air Force, the United States Air Force Test Pilot School and Honeywell Aerospace.

Med-Eng has operated since 1981 and is a brand of The Safariland Group, part of Cadre Holdings. It designs and tests personal protective equipment, EOD and search tools, blast dosimeters and vehicle blast attenuation seats, with manufacturing in Pembroke, Ontario and Ogdensburg, New York. It reports customers in approximately 100 countries and territories and runs in-house blast, ballistic and impact test facilities.

Weatherhaven Global Resources Ltd. was founded in British Columbia in 1981 and has its head office in Burnaby, BC. It makes soft-wall shelters, expandable ISO-container shelters (MECC, EHMECC, TRECC, HERCon) and camp support systems, and provides engineering, installation, logistics, repair and overhaul, and in-service support. Its own profile says manufacturing and operations are at its Brockville, Ontario facility. Named customers include the Canadian Department of National Defence, the UK Ministry of Defence, the United Nations and Boeing.
loc_city_list: North Tonawanda, New York, United States

abstract_en: Wuxly, founded in 2015 as a consumer winter-outerwear brand, now operates a defence division that designs and supplies combat and cold-weather uniform systems, load-bearing and carrier systems, and tactical soft goods. It states that it uses a vertically integrated, predominantly Canadian manufacturing model, with cutting and sewing done domestically. It has supplied clothing and soft goods for the Armed Forces of Ukraine and states it is developing smart textiles for soldier biomonitoring with Myant. The company states that its products are made under ISO 9001 and ISO 14001 standards and that it is a certified B Corporation.

Magellan Aerospace Corporation is a publicly traded aerospace company incorporated in Ontario in 1996, with its head office at 3160 Derry Road East, Mississauga. It machines, fabricates, casts and assembles aeroengine and aerostructure parts for civil and military customers, and runs engine and component repair and overhaul. Its specialty products include Black Brant sounding rockets, small satellite buses and avionics, and the Wire Strike Protection System for helicopters. In 2026 it announced a Government of Canada contract for M-72 Light Anti-Tank Weapon production and a teaming agreement with TKMS on heavyweight torpedoes for the Canadian Patrol Submarine Project.
loc_city_list: Long Island, New York, United States

abstract_en: INDAL has operated in Mississauga since its 1951 incorporation as Dominion Aluminum Fabricating Ltd., and Curtiss-Wright acquired it in 2005. Its products include the RAST, ASIST and TC-ASIST helicopter securing and traversing systems, MANTIS aircraft tugs, variable depth sonar and towed array handling systems, and deck tracks, tie-downs and horizon reference systems. It also runs in-house modelling and simulation tools for ship motion and helicopter-deck interface analysis. Recent announced work includes ASIST design services for the Royal Canadian Navy River Class Destroyers, RAST and ASIST supply for the U.S. Navy through the Canadian Commercial Corporation, and a teaming agreement with Hanwha Ocean on towed array handling for the Canadian Patrol Submarine Project.

DEW Engineering and Development ULC is a Canadian defence manufacturer headquartered in Ottawa with a second plant in Miramichi, New Brunswick. It designs, tests and produces armour systems for military and police vehicles, shelters, trailers, heaters, environmental control units and CBRN decontamination systems, and re-roles and supports military vehicles for the Canadian Army. The organization states that it has in-house fabrication, machining, painting, assembly and a ballistic test range, and that its products are ITAR-free.

Babcock Canada is a wholly owned subsidiary of Babcock International Group and has operated in Canada since 2008. It delivers equipment support and in-service support to defence and civil customers across naval, air and land programs. It holds a Transport Canada Approved Maintenance Organization certificate for aircraft maintenance in Winnipeg. It also designs and manufactures mission-based equipment, including weapons handling and launch systems, magazine racks and food and stores lifts for naval ships, and armoured Land Cruiser-based vehicles. Its technology products include the iSupport360 sustainment application, the INSPIRE radio control software and the Babcock Immersive Training Experience.

The Cambridge, Ontario site is a Honeywell space-hardware plant that handles design, machining, plating, assembly, integration, testing and delivery for space missions. It has built instruments for the James Webb Space Telescope and leads the Quantum Encryption and Science Satellite (QEYSSat) mission for the Canadian Space Agency. The site was formerly COM DEV International. The aerospace business of which it is part became an independent, publicly traded company in mid-2026.

Teledyne FLIR is a U.S.-headquartered maker of thermal imaging and uncrewed systems, owned by Teledyne Technologies Incorporated. Its Canadian uncrewed aerial systems unit at 575 Kumpf Drive, Waterloo, Ontario, builds the SkyRanger R70 drone, which Teledyne said Canada's Department of National Defence ordered in 2024 for donation to Ukraine. Trade press also reports that Teledyne FLIR produces ground radars in Laval, Quebec. The unit began as Aeryon Labs Inc., which FLIR Systems acquired in 2019.

Avidrone Aerospace Incorporated says it has designed and built uncrewed aircraft systems since 2007, from small UAVs to rotorcraft over 1,000 lb. It describes itself as the original equipment manufacturer of its aircraft, with in-house airframe design and flight control software. Its fleet covers payloads of 2.3 kg to 227 kg, and it sells to defence and commercial users. Its head office is at the Region of Waterloo International Airport.

Centra Industries Inc. operates from 24 Cherry Blossom Road in Cambridge, Ontario, as a PCC Aerostructures company. It does 3-, 4- and 5-axis machining of aluminum structures up to 12 feet and of titanium, nickel-based and steel alloys up to 80 inches. It also builds metallic assemblies and large floor-jig structural sub-assemblies, and offers in-house CNC programming and tool design. Third-party sources place it in commercial and military airframe programs, and it is owned by Precision Castparts Corp.

SkyWatch Space Applications Inc. is a Kitchener, Ontario company that runs a geospatial data platform made up of the EXPLORE, HUB, MAP, BUILD and CONNECT products. Customers use it to find and purchase imagery from third-party providers, manage it across an organization, and load it into GIS software such as ArcGIS or into their own applications. Satellite and data operators can also use it to distribute their archives. The company has held Canadian Space Agency contracts for research and development in AI and big-data analytics for space systems.

Chartright Air Group began in the late 1980s as an aircraft management firm at Toronto Pearson International Airport. It now offers private jet and helicopter charter, aircraft management, sales and acquisition, a jet membership program called JetClub, and maintenance under Transport Canada approved maintenance organization number 196-92. It operates fixed base operations and hangars at Toronto Pearson, the Region of Waterloo International Airport and Lake Simcoe Regional Airport. In 2025 it announced it would support final production quality checks on Bombardier Global aircraft at its Waterloo facility.

NAVBLUE Inc. is the Waterloo, Ontario arm of NAVBLUE, which Airbus launched in 2016 after acquiring Navtech. It supplies flight planning, crew and operations control, electronic flight bag, aeronautical data and flight procedure design products and services to airlines. In April 2026 Airbus announced that NAVBLUE solutions and Skywise Digital solutions were merged into a single wholly owned subsidiary named Skywise, with about 750 employees worldwide. The navblue.aero website now redirects to the Skywise site.

Spire Global Canada Subsidiary Corp. operates from one office in Cambridge, Ontario, and is an indirect subsidiary of Spire Global, Inc. (NYSE: SPIR). In February 2025 a Government of Canada contract worth up to Can$72 million for the design and development of the WildFireSat constellation was assigned to it, and Spire said it planned to add satellite manufacturing and test equipment at the Cambridge office. Trade press and SEC-filing summaries report that Public Works and Government Services Canada terminated that contract for convenience on April 23, 2026. The parent group sells satellite data, analytics and space services to government and commercial customers, including defence and security users.

Maerospace Corporation is a Waterloo, Ontario company that makes over-the-horizon high frequency surface wave radar (PASE) and AI-driven maritime analytics (TimeCaster) for navies, coast guards and other maritime authorities. It also provides installation, commissioning, training and maintenance of its systems. It obtained the rights to the radar technology in 2019 from Raytheon and Defence Research and Development Canada, and has operated a fourth-generation demonstration installation at Cape Race, Newfoundland since 2023.

Eclipse Automation Inc. was founded in 2001 and is headquartered in Cambridge, Ontario, with other operations in South Carolina, Germany and Hungary. It designs and builds custom automation machines, and offers engineering services, digital twin and vision systems, robotics integration, build-to-print and contract manufacturing, and post-installation support. Its published work includes automated tooling and equipment for CANDU nuclear refurbishment projects and a published page on aerospace and defence automation. In July 2026 it announced a $6 million FedDev Ontario investment delivered through the Regional Tariff Response Initiative and the Regional Defence Investment Initiative.
loc_city_list: Rock Hill, South Carolina, United States

abstract_en: ATS Industrial Automation Inc. is the industrial automation business of ATS Corporation, headquartered in Cambridge, Ontario. It delivers custom automated assembly and test lines, laser welding systems, digital twin and line-control software, and remote tooling for nuclear reactor refurbishment, decommissioning and small modular reactors. It also operates a submerged test facility for nuclear tooling and holds CSA N299.1, CWB W47.1 and ISO 9001 registrations, which it claims on its own site. Its published markets are automotive and EV, grid energy storage, fuel cells, nuclear, consumer and industrial products, aviation component testing and autonomous systems manufacturing.

OTTO sells a line of autonomous mobile robots (OTTO 100, 600, 1200, 1500 and Lifter), along with OTTO Autonomy software, OTTO Fleet Manager, simulation, training and OTTO Care support plans. Its published customers are manufacturers in automotive, consumer goods, food and beverage and general industry. The company is part of Rockwell Automation, Inc. following an acquisition of Clearpath Robotics and OTTO Motors completed in October 2023. A separate Clearpath research division sells uncrewed ground vehicles to research buyers, including a 2022 federal contract with the National Research Council Canada.
operating_name: Rockwell Automation Canada / Clearpath OTTO Motors

abstract_en: YKF has two runways, a NAV Canada control tower, Canada Border Services Agency Airport of Entry service, bonded customs and sufferance warehouse facilities, and two fixed base operators. It is home to 44 businesses covering flight training, aircraft maintenance, charter, ground handling and uncrewed aerial vehicles. The Region of Waterloo supports the airport's aerospace sector through its AeroWR initiative and an Aerospace Accelerator Program.

Waterloo Wellington Flight Centre began as a flying club in 1932. It trains professional and recreational pilots through its Airline Transport Pilot Licence program, self-paced modular courses and a University of Waterloo aviation degree partnership. It also teaches drone (RPAS) courses and runs a Transport Canada written-exam testing site. It operates a Transport Canada Approved Maintenance Organization, and an Aviation Sim Centre with Boeing 737 MAX, Q400 and Airbus A320 simulators that it offers to airlines.

Great Lakes Helicopter Corp. (GLH) runs a helicopter flight school at the Region of Waterloo International Airport and holds registration as a career college under Ontario's Career Colleges Act, 2005. It also provides aerial services such as agricultural spraying, frost control, seeding, forestry support, surveying and LiDAR, and it offers drone services. The group of companies includes Rotor Services Ltd. (an aircraft maintenance organization that also sells Robinson helicopters), heliSIX (tourism and charter), GLH Drones and Heli Theory. Trade press reports that Chad McIntosh acquired the company in October 2025 and that it operates about 20 helicopters.

Flightpath was founded in 2006 at the Waterloo Regional Airport with a single Piper Navajo.
