It now offers private jet charter, empty-leg flights, aircraft management, maintenance oversight, and aircraft acquisition and sales. The company states that it manages 26 aircraft and flies more than 6,100 charter hours a year from bases in Canada and the United States. Its Canadian headquarters is in Cambridge, Ontario, and its U.S. headquarters is in Boca Raton, Florida.

Flite Line Services operates fixed-base operator facilities at CYKF (Breslau, Ontario) and CYXU (London, Ontario), including fuel, de-icing, ground handling and cargo and customs services. Its maintenance arm holds Transport Canada AMO #40-11 for piston and turbine aircraft, avionics, structures, welding and instruments. It is an authorized Garmin dealer that installs glass cockpits, navigators, autopilots and ADS-B equipment. It also offers composite and sheet metal repair, charters, scenic flights and an aircraft rental club.

Mid-Canada Mod Center, operating under Transport Canada AMO 59-97, designs, installs, repairs and services avionics for business, commercial and special mission aircraft. Its engineering arm, Avionics Design Services, develops Supplemental Type Certificates, Technical Standard Order and Repair Design Approval packages, and MC2 builds approved STC kits. It is also Canada's exclusive factory-authorized distributor and repair centre for Gentex helicopter and fixed wing helmets. It operates from Toronto Pearson Airport and Region of Waterloo Airport (Breslau), and was acquired by De Havilland Aircraft of Canada Limited in 2023.

Rotor Services Limited was founded in 1988 and operates as a Transport Canada Approved Maintenance Organization (AMO 51-91) at the Region of Waterloo International Airport. It services Robinson, Bell 206, MD500, AS350 and EC130 helicopters and gyroplanes, including scheduled maintenance, overhauls, inspections and flight testing. It also sells new Robinson R22, R44, R66 and R88 helicopters and helps clients source pre-owned aircraft. It provides aircraft acquisition consulting and aircraft management services. Since a 2025 change of ownership it has been part of the Great Lakes Helicopter group of companies.

Aerotech Aviation provides aircraft maintenance from Hangar 31, 4881 Fountain Street North, at the Region of Waterloo International Airport in Breslau (Woolwich Township), Ontario. The airport's business directory lists it under aircraft maintenance, and the airport's tenant list describes the work as private aircraft maintenance. Its LinkedIn company page describes it as a privately held firm of 2–10 employees. No company website, certifications, named personnel or registry record could be confirmed from usable sources.

Executive Aviation provides above-wing and below-wing ground handling for airlines at airports in Ontario, British Columbia, Saskatchewan and Nova Scotia. It runs FBOs for private and executive aircraft at London, Sault Ste. Marie and Sudbury. It also operates a 15,000 sq. ft. ground support equipment (GSE) repair and refurbishment shop at London International Airport. Its head office is at London International Airport; the Breslau location in the seed record is its ground handling station at the Region of Waterloo International Airport.

Summit Fuel Services operates a fuel service at the Region of Waterloo International Airport (CYKF) in Breslau, Ontario. It publishes 66,000 litres of storage and three mobile Avgas refuellers, and lists 100LL as its fuel product. It also offers ramp, call-out and crew and passenger arrangements, plus rental hangar units on Apron 1. It has won the World Fuels Network Canada Operations Excellence Award in several years. No defence, certification or manufacturing content is published.

Waterloo Warbirds is a volunteer-run group that was formed in 2014 when the owners of several vintage aircraft merged their operations. It flies, maintains and restores a fleet that includes the T-33 Silver Star, de Havilland Vampire, MiG-15, L-29 Delfin and Harvard Mk. 2. It sells passenger flights, supplies airshow displays and flyovers to event organizers, and runs a cadet flight award and veteran-honouring outreach. It states that it receives no external funding or grants and relies on passenger flight revenue and its Ally Program supporters.

Apex Aircraft Sales Ltd. (operating as Apex Aircraft Sales & Brokerage) buys, sells and brokers new and used general aviation aircraft in Canada. It offers consultation, condition assessment advice and expedited aircraft importation. It was appointed Pipistrel's Canadian distributor in October 2023. It is based at the Region of Waterloo International Airport near Breslau, Ontario. It does not publish any manufacturing, maintenance or certification capability.

SkyCare, legally 2080061 Ontario Inc., has served Northern Ontario and Manitoba since 2006 from a head office in Sioux Lookout, Ontario. It flies passenger and cargo charters, and provides air ambulance service to the Province of Ontario under a Standing Offer Agreement managed by Ornge. It also offers private medevac and repatriation flights. It operates a fleet of 20 aircraft from bases in Sioux Lookout, Thunder Bay, Breslau (Kitchener) and Winnipeg area locations, and reports more than 150 employees.

Air Canada is a publicly traded airline headquartered in the Montréal area, and it provides scheduled passenger service, cargo and charter flights. At the Region of Waterloo International Airport (YKF) in Breslau, Ontario, it does not operate its own aircraft. It sells single-itinerary connections to Toronto Pearson using The Landline Company's motorcoaches. The Air Canada media centre announced that service would grow to 12 daily round trips from YKF on June 15, 2026. This record covers Air Canada's YKF presence and the national legal entity behind it, not a separate legal entity.

WestJet is a Canadian low-cost airline whose group includes WestJet Airlines, Sunwing Vacations Group and WestJet Cargo. It serves Kitchener-Waterloo from the Region of Waterloo International Airport (YKF), where it is listed as a scheduled airline, and the airport's site promotes non-stop service to Calgary. WestJet is a passenger air carrier and does not manufacture products. This record covers its YKF presence; the corporate facts come from the parent company's own publications.

Flair Airlines Ltd. operates scheduled low-fare passenger flights across Canada, the United States, Mexico, the Dominican Republic and Jamaica, and has added charter operations. Its published corporate mailing address is at Edmonton International Airport. At YKF it based aircraft and crews from about 2022. It closed its Kitchener-Waterloo crew base on September 3, 2025 and said it would keep flying scheduled service from the airport. In 2026 it launched a vacation packages business, Flair Vacations.

The centre is housed on the University of Waterloo campus and brings together scientists from the University of Waterloo and the National Research Council of Canada (NRC). It conducts research on AI, the Internet of Things and cybersecurity, applied to intelligent logistics and other uses. Its stated focus areas include battery-free touch sensors, neuromorphic movement control, gesture recognition in virtual reality, quantum-safe blockchain for critical infrastructure and automated materials discovery. It also develops the skills of students and early-career researchers.
operating_name: NRC-Waterloo Collaboration on AI, IoT and Cybersecurity

abstract_en: The lab is a CENGN Living Lab Initiative program hosted at the University of Waterloo RoboHub, and Rogers Communications supports it with 5G and LTE connectivity. It combines indoor lab space with an outdoor validation area, a robot and drone fleet available for rental, and access to Waterloo robotics researchers. Startups and scaleups reach it through CENGN Innovation Projects or Adoption Projects that are co-funded under the federal Strategic Response Fund. CENGN announced the partnership on September 26, 2025.
operating_name: CENGN Robotic Connectivity Living Lab at Waterloo RoboHub

abstract_en: Velocity says it has helped founders of more than 500 startups since 2008, with a combined enterprise value of over $40 billion. It runs coaching, programs, events and non-dilutive student awards and grants, and offers 3D printing, laser cutting, electronics, workshop and shared lab space. Its Innovation Arena headquarters is in Kitchener, with additional program offices on the University of Waterloo campus. The startups it supports are listed by sector and include health, industrial and aerospace or military technology companies.

Communitech has operated since 1997 as a member-based organization for Waterloo Region's technology community. It offers membership tiers, founder and leadership programs, AI adoption programs (AI@Work and the Waterloo Region AI Coalition), intellectual property education, events and flexible workspace at the Communitech Hub in downtown Kitchener. It publishes no manufactured products, certifications or defence-specific activity.

The Accelerator Centre (AC) is a not-for-profit organization at the University of Waterloo Research and Technology Park that supports early-stage technology founders. It runs programs including AC:Incubate, AC:Studio, AC:RevLab, AC:Incubate+, AC:Health, the Aerospace Accelerator and the Global Impact Creator, and it leases coworking and office space. It states that it takes no equity and is technology agnostic. It reports more than 400 alumni companies and works with the Region of Waterloo, Skywise and AeroWR on aerospace.

Catalyst137 is a converted former tire warehouse in Kitchener that describes itself as a hub for growth-oriented technology firms, with a focus on Internet of Things (IoT) hardware. It leases offices from 1,000 to 150,000 square feet, runs a co-working space (Catalyst Commons) and hosts events. Its tenant list includes technology firms, BDC, Export Development Canada, NRC IRAP and a University of Waterloo additive manufacturing lab. It is a property and ecosystem operator, not a manufacturer or defence supplier.

The Smart Manufacturing and Advanced Recycling Technologies (SMART) Centre is a Conestoga College applied research centre at 96 Grand Avenue South, Cambridge, Ontario. It operates labs for additive manufacturing, advanced recycling, cybersecurity, electronics and sensors, robotic welding and visualization. It is an NSERC-funded Technology Access Centre that works with industry partners and employs student researchers. Its published work covers mechanical design, prototyping, automation, software and sensor development, not series production.

The Regional Training Centre is a unit of Conestoga College. It delivers Ontario Fire College courses to firefighters from Waterloo, Kitchener, Cambridge, Guelph and elsewhere in Ontario. Courses cover NFPA 1001 Firefighter, pump operations, technical rescue, fire officer, fire investigator, fire and life safety educator, fire instructor, hazardous materials and incident safety officer training. Delivery takes place on a 72-acre training property with a live-fire burn building, propane props and a driver training track. It offers week-long, weekend and evening courses and can run custom courses.

The Institute for Earth and Space Exploration (Western Space) is a research institute of Western University. It brings together 112 members from eight Western faculties for work in planetary science and astronomy, space technology, Earth observation and space and remote health. Projects include student-built CubeSats (Ukpik-1 and Western Skylark), a Canadian Space Agency-funded Integrated Vision System for rover missions, and a Mission Control Facility on campus. It offers funding programs, training and partnership routes for industry, health-care, municipal and non-profit partners.
operating_name: Western University Institute for Earth and Space Exploration

abstract_en: The Centre for Research and Innovation (CRI) is the research and industry-innovation unit of Fanshawe College of Applied Arts and Technology in London, Ontario. It works with small and medium-sized businesses on proof-of-concept development, process development, and product testing and validation, and it acts as the college's liaison to external research funders. Its facilities include the Fanshawe Product Testing lab, which covers thermal, mechanical, vibration, acoustic and electromagnetic compatibility testing, and the CARIB food innovation labs. Its work involves student researchers and is funded in part by NSERC, the Canada Foundation for Innovation and SONAMI.
operating_name: Fanshawe College Centre for Research and Innovation

abstract_en: The McMaster Manufacturing Research Institute (MMRI) is part of McMaster University's Faculty of Engineering and operates labs in machining systems, metal forming, polymer processing, thermal processing and materials property assessment. It works with manufacturers on tooling selection, tool path development, process parameters, process monitoring, prototype development and process scale-up. It also runs an industrial training program and graduate research. Its facility is at McMaster Innovation Park, 230 Longwood Road South, Hamilton.

IDEAWORKS was founded in 2008 and runs several research centres, including the Additive Manufacturing Innovation Centre (AMIC), the Uncrewed and Remote Sensing Innovation Centre (URSIC), the Energy & Power Innovation Centre (EPIC) and an Industrial Internet of Things lab. AMIC operates metal and polymer 3D printing systems and a RAPID Lab for low-volume production of 5 to 500+ units. Clients keep ownership of their intellectual property, and each project employs at least one student research assistant. Funding comes from federal and provincial programs such as CFI, NSERC and the Ontario Centres of Innovation.

Innovation Factory is a not-for-profit business accelerator serving Hamilton, Halton, Brant and Norfolk, funded by the Government of Ontario. It offers venture advisory, workshops, pitch competitions, intellectual property programming and investment readiness support, and takes no equity in its clients. It hosts the Centre for Integrated Transportation and Mobility (CITM) for smart transportation innovators and the Synapse life science program. It amalgamated with Haltech on April 1, 2024.

Bioenterprise Canada, which calls itself Canada’s Food & Agri-Tech Engine, is a not-for-profit organization headquartered in Guelph, Ontario, with regional offices in Atlantic Canada, Quebec, Manitoba and Alberta. It connects food and agri-tech innovators with industry experts, innovation advisors, partners and investors. It also delivers government-funded programs such as the Clean Agri-Tech Accelerator, the OAFRI Commercialization Stream and the Grow Ontario Accelerator Hub. It does not manufacture products.

MaRS Discovery District is a registered charity that operates the MaRS Centre and MaRS Waterfront in Toronto, supporting more than 1,200 science and technology ventures in health, climate and other sectors. It provides venture services, advisory support and connections to capital, customers and talent, and leases office, lab and event space to about 120 tenants through its Innovation Hubs division. Its venture capital arm, MaRS IAF, invests in seed-stage startups. In 2026 it announced a partnership with Vimy Forge to build a capital pipeline for early-stage defence and dual-use companies.

Vector Institute launched in 2017 with funding from the Government of Canada, the Government of Ontario and industry sponsors, in partnership with the University of Toronto. It supports research in machine learning and deep learning, runs scholarships and internships, and offers engineering support, training and collaborative programs to enterprises, startups, health providers and public sector bodies. It does not make physical products and no defence-specific work is published on its site.

DAIR is a federally incorporated not-for-profit whose members include Bombardier, de Havilland Aircraft of Canada, MHI Canada Aerospace, Safran, Siemens and several Ontario universities and colleges. It runs the DAIR Green Fund, the Supplier Development Initiative, the Defence Readiness Program, the Innovation Network, DAIR Upskill and DAIR Digital Manufacturing. It is building a physical hub at the former Downsview airport site in Toronto, with labs and equipment that partners can access. It does not manufacture aerospace products itself.

UTIAS is a research and graduate-teaching unit of the University of Toronto's Faculty of Applied Science and Engineering. It operates laboratories in aerodynamics and propulsion, aircraft flight, space systems, structures and optimization, robotics and plasma-materials physics. It also hosts the Centre for Aerial Robotics Research and Education and the Centre for Research in Sustainable Aviation. Its faculty collaborate with industry partners including Bombardier and Safran on projects such as aircraft noise reduction.
operating_name: University of Toronto Institute for Aerospace Studies

abstract_en: DualUseTech.ca is a consortium based in Waterloo, Ontario, facilitated by the Accelerator Centre, Communitech, AERO WR, the Region of Waterloo and Waterloo EDC. It publishes a directory of 50 member technology companies organized under the Government of Canada's Key Industrial Capabilities, a regional directory of 10 manufacturers, and a quantum defence subcommittee. Buyers describe an operational problem and the consortium connects them to relevant Canadian capabilities.

Nuvation Energy, based in Waterloo, Ontario, makes configurable battery management systems (G4, G5 and G5 Plus) and a Multi-Stack Controller for stationary energy storage up to 1500 V DC. It also offers battery energy storage system (BESS) design, BMS design, and testing and certification support. The company says it designs its products in Canada and the USA, manufactures them in Canada, and is owned by US and Canadian citizens and residents. It lists utility-scale, commercial and industrial, microgrid, marine, mobile and defence applications.

Ontario Die International Inc. is a family-owned maker of cutting dies, founded in 1923 and based at 235 Gage Avenue in Kitchener, Ontario. It states that it has manufacturing facilities in Canada, the United States, Mexico and the Czech Republic. Its products include steel rule dies, clicker (Viking) dies, DieVerse reconfigurable tooling, DieVac vacuum cutting systems, the DieTrackRT die-tracking system and Super Dumbbell specimen cutters. It cuts fabric, leather, foam, plastic, rubber and composite parts, and its published supplier awards are mostly from automotive seating customers.

Ansys Canada Ltd. operates a Waterloo, Ontario research and development office, which the organization says employs 160 people, and also lists offices in Vancouver and Montreal. The Ansys group sells multiphysics engineering simulation software (fluids, structures, electronics, optics) to aerospace, defence, space, automotive, energy and healthcare customers. Waterloo's simulation roots are the TASCflow and CFX computational fluid dynamics tools. Federal contract records show the entity supplying Ansys software licences and maintenance to Defence R&D Canada and other federal departments.

KA Imaging is a University of Waterloo spin-off founded in 2015. It makes spectral and high-resolution X-ray detectors and systems under the Reveal, BrillianSe, Sight and inCiTe names. Its SpectralDR dual-energy technology captures multiple images from one exposure. It sells into hospitals, veterinary clinics, industrial inspection and quality control, and security and EOD teams, and it has supported a medical X-ray experiment in space.

BizLink elocab Ltd. is the Kitchener, Ontario operation of the BizLink Group and sister company to BizLink elocab GmbH in Germany. It designs and makes custom round, flat, hybrid and high-performance flex cables, and builds complete cable assemblies with connectors and overmoulding, including in cleanroom conditions. It also offers prototyping and engineering support. It markets to semiconductor, industrial automation, laboratory diagnostics, rail and marine customers, and the elocab site carries land and naval defence application pages.

EXO Insights Corp. is a Waterloo, Ontario company that builds the BioTwin® human-performance platform. The platform combines eye-tracking glasses, position tracking, physiological sensors, drone-based terrain scanning, mixed-reality scenarios and 2D and 3D replay analytics. The company states it is a 15-person firm. It says it delivered two transactions to a Tier 1 prime under a Victoria-class in-service support industrial and technological benefits (ITB) obligation in 2020–21. Earlier work was industrial safety training for nuclear and mining customers.

XL Tool Inc. is a tool and die and custom machine shop in Kitchener, Ontario that builds progressive, compound, transfer and other stamping dies, jigs and fixtures, and machines parts to customer print. The company states it works to ISO 9001:2015 and follows N285 and N299 standards for nuclear components. It publishes an equipment list that includes 3-, 4- and 5-axis CNC mills, wire EDM, CNC lathes, grinders, a CMM and tryout presses of up to 800 tons. In July 2026 the federal government announced FedDev Ontario funding of up to $1 million toward a project of more than $4 million that supports the company's entry into defence and aerospace markets.

Pegasus Aeronautics Corporation was started by University of Waterloo engineers and makes lightweight gas-electric range extenders and direct-drive engines for UAVs. It lists in-house electrical design, PCB prototyping, mechanical design, CNC machining and engine test chambers. It also offers the GM-15 Sentinel, a 25 kg hybrid UAV that is powered by its GE70 unit.

7D Kinematic Metrology owns the iGPS technology, an indoor positioning system in which networked infrared laser transmitters let several sensors and probes be tracked at the same time across a factory. The company develops, assembles and tests the system in Cambridge, Ontario, with an applications R&D site in Saint-Hubert, Quebec. It sells to aerospace, shipbuilding, rail, automotive and heavy-industry manufacturers and states that its solutions are not currently ITAR-controlled.

OpenText, incorporated in 1991 as a University of Waterloo spin-off, publishes information management, content management, cybersecurity, data analytics and AI software. It sells these products and related professional, managed, support and learning services to enterprise and public-sector customers, including defence and intelligence agencies. It is listed on the TSX and NASDAQ, and its head office is in Waterloo, Ontario. It states that it has more than 20,000 employees and operates in 180 countries.

Watsec Cyber Risk Management is based in Waterloo, Ontario. It offers a risk assessment method it calls Intelligent Cyber Resilience, which covers both technology and human exposures. Published services include gap assessments against the CyberSecure Canada standard, privacy audits for PIPEDA, MFIPPA and GDPR, and dark web credential monitoring delivered with a partner. Trade press and a government-linked presentation list Watsec as an accredited CyberSecure Canada certification body.

ETAS Embedded Systems Canada Inc. was established in Waterloo, Ontario in June 2016 as the Canadian site of ETAS, a wholly owned subsidiary of Robert Bosch GmbH. The site provides safety and security solutions for embedded and automotive systems, originally under the ESCRYPT brand and now under the ETAS brand. It integrated the Waterloo cryptography company TrustPoint Innovation Technologies and has supplied connected-vehicle security work to Transport Canada. Its stated customers are automakers, automotive suppliers and engineering service providers.

NCC Group was founded in 1999 and is headquartered in Manchester, United Kingdom. It states that it has over 2,000 colleagues worldwide. It sells technical assurance and penetration testing, digital forensics and incident response, managed detection and response, consulting and implementation, and threat intelligence services. It lists a Waterloo, Ontario office among its North American locations and serves public sector, financial, telecommunications, transport, energy, manufacturing and health clients.

GeoMate Inc. is a Waterloo, Ontario software and data company founded in 2019. Its Compact HD Map product is built from aerial and satellite imagery and sold as map data for autonomous fleets, municipalities and consultants. Its RealSimE platform produces simulation-ready 3D environments for ADAS and autonomous driving validation. Named customers include Magna New Mobility, May Mobility, Gatik, AFL Global and GHD, and it has worked with the City of Kitchener.

Precision Resource Canada, Ltd. has operated in Cambridge, Ontario since 1986 as part of Precision Resource, a privately held group headquartered in Shelton, Connecticut. The Cambridge site produces fineblanked metal stampings and assemblies, and its Technical Center develops fineblanking processes and builds the group's fineblanking tools. The group also offers precision machining, metal additive manufacturing, finishing and fuel cell bipolar plates, and serves automotive, aerospace, medical, heavy-duty, electronics and defence markets. The Canadian site holds Intertek-issued IATF 16949 and ISO 14001 certificates.

Data Perceptions Inc. is an IT consulting firm headquartered in Waterloo, Ontario. It publishes services in technology strategy and transformation, cybersecurity planning and implementation, data analytics and AI readiness, integrated project management, and Microsoft 365-based modern workplace deployment. It says it serves clients across Canada and internationally through a global partner network and a talent network of independent consultants. Its named clients and testimonials include a public library, a financial and higher-education audience, and a testimonial referring to defence, intelligence and maritime awareness work.

eSentire Inc. is a cybersecurity services company founded in 2001 and operating its lead security operations centre in Waterloo, Ontario, with a second centre in Cork, Ireland. It sells managed detection and response, digital forensics and incident response, and exposure management and penetration testing services, built on its own Atlas platform and its Threat Response Unit. Its published customers include a law firm, a private equity firm, a software company and a sporting goods manufacturer, and it also sells through channel partners. The company states it holds ISO/IEC 27001 and SOC 2 certification and PCI DSS compliance, and no defence customers or programs are named on its site.

Arctic Wolf Networks, Inc. is headquartered in Eden Prairie, Minnesota, and operates in Canada through its wholly owned subsidiary Arctic Wolf Networks Canada, Inc. It sells security operations services built on the Aurora Superintelligence Platform and delivered by security teams, and it reports serving more than 10,000 organizations in sectors such as healthcare, manufacturing, government and education. Its Waterloo, Ontario office has been its main research and development site and is home to its first security operations centre.

Magnet Forensics sells software and extraction products that acquire, analyze and report on digital evidence from mobile devices, computers, cloud sources, vehicles and media. Its product line includes Magnet Axiom, Magnet Axiom Cyber, Magnet Graykey, Magnet Verakey, Magnet Review, Magnet Verify, Magnet Griffeye and the Magnet One cloud platform. Its customers are police and federal agencies, military and intelligence users, and corporate investigation teams. The company was founded in 2011 and joined with Grayshift in 2023 under the Magnet Forensics name. It is owned by the private equity firm Thoma Bravo.

McAfee describes itself as a worldwide online protection company. It sells subscription antivirus, identity theft protection, scam detection, VPN and mobile security products to individuals and families. The Canadian entity, McAfee Canada ULC, is listed at a Waterloo, Ontario address in a Government of Canada lobbyist registration. A Waterloo economic development body describes the Waterloo team as software developers focused on research and development.

AppLogic Networks, formerly Sandvine, sells software for network traffic classification, application quality-of-experience scoring, traffic management and analytics. Its customers are communication service providers, enterprises, managed service providers and governments. The company says it is now software-only. It has a Waterloo, Ontario office and also lists offices in the United States, Sweden, India, Japan, Malaysia and the United Arab Emirates. It describes itself as based in the US and says it sells only in democratic jurisdictions after a 2024–2025 restructuring.
loc_city_list: Dubai Media City, United Arab Emirates

abstract_en: Sera4 Ltd. is a Canadian technology company headquartered in Waterloo, Ontario, that holds patents for keyless access management. Its Teleporte platform combines Teleporte Cloud, the Teleporte Mobile app for Android and iOS, and Teleporte Embedded hardware, including the AP3 padlock and AX5 door controller. Customers named on its site include telecom tower operators, utilities, a rail operator, a county government and retail organizations in the Americas, Africa and Asia. It states that it is ISO 27001:2022 certified.

Symantec's enterprise security products are now part of Broadcom Inc. and sold under the Symantec brand, including Endpoint Security Complete, Cloud Secure Web Gateway, Data Loss Prevention and Messaging Gateway. Broadcom's contact page lists an office at 609 Kumpf Drive in Waterloo, Ontario, but does not say which division works there. Canadian federal buyers, including Shared Services Canada, the Department of National Defence and NATO, have issued CanadaBuys notices for Symantec support and licences. The Canadian legal entity previously registered with the federal lobbyists registry was Symantec (Canada) Corporation, a subsidiary of Symantec Corporation.

IBM Canada Limited is headquartered in Markham, Ontario, with its own software labs, a defence and intelligence centre in Ottawa, and a semiconductor packaging plant in Bromont, Quebec. It sells technology products and services (AI, automation, cybersecurity, hybrid cloud, quantum, consulting and systems integration) to Canadian public- and private-sector clients. Federal contract records show in-service support and ERP work for the Department of National Defence. The organization states a 2025 expansion of its defence offering, including a secure collaboration centre in Ottawa and an AI model built with Janes. Its Waterloo Region presence is documented only by a 2017 innovation incubator at the Communitech Data Hub and a municipal business directory listing.

Anyon Systems Inc. was founded in Montréal in 2014 and says it designs, manufactures and integrates the main subsystems of a superconducting quantum computer in-house. Its products are the Qube and Hudson quantum computing platforms and the open-source Snowflurry software library. It delivered a gate-based quantum computer to Defence Research and Development Canada (DRDC) in 2021 and a 24-qubit system (MonarQ) to Calcul Québec. It lists a research office in Waterloo, Ontario, and a Montréal head office in Saint-Laurent.

evolutionQ was founded in 2015 and is based in the Kitchener-Waterloo area of Ontario, with a separately incorporated European office in Aachen, Germany. It sells the Basejump platform, which includes BasejumpSKI for symmetric key infrastructure combined with post-quantum cryptography, and BasejumpQDN for managing quantum key distribution networks. It also provides quantum risk assessments, quantum roadmap and strategy work, and executive workshops. Its published work includes a Bank of Canada research project, a Canadian Space Agency-funded satellite QKD project, and network deployments with telecom partners in Europe and Quebec.

High Q Technologies Inc. is a University of Waterloo spin-off, headquartered in Waterloo, Ontario, that makes quantum-enabled EPR spectroscopy instruments for structural biology and drug discovery. Its FATHOM spectrometer uses superconducting resonators and quantum-control pulse techniques. It also runs a sample measurement service from its applications lab and works with contract research organizations. It is backed by Quantum Valley Investments and received up to $3.75 million from FedDev Ontario's Regional Quantum Initiative.

Keysight Technologies Canada Inc. sells, supports and services the electronic test and measurement instruments and software of its U.S. parent, Keysight Technologies, Inc. Its head office is in Mississauga, Ontario, with service sites in Kanata, Saint-Laurent and Calgary and a quantum engineering presence in Kitchener, in Waterloo Region. Its published offering includes electronic warfare, radar, satellite and secure communications test solutions, as well as quantum control and error-diagnostic software. It is registered in the Controlled Goods Program and its Canadian sites are listed on the parent's ISO 9001 certificate.

QEYnet was founded in 2016 and is working toward a global quantum key distribution network delivered by microsatellites. It has delivered a free-space QKD system to the National Research Council of Canada and holds a Canadian Space Agency contribution to demonstrate its Quantum Receiver in orbit. Its development and qualification work was funded in part by the Department of National Defence's IDEaS program. The company is small and describes a founding team of spacecraft engineers and quantum communication experts, with QKD expertise from the University of Waterloo's Institute for Quantum Computing.

Open Quantum Design (OQD) is a not-for-profit that publishes open-source designs for a trapped-ion quantum computer, covering hardware, middleware control and top-level programming interfaces. The technology was developed by University of Waterloo researchers at the Institute for Quantum Computing and Perimeter Institute's Quantum Intelligence Lab. OQD runs a paid community-participation model, coordinates working groups on GitHub, and offers to build a quantum computer for a participant's team for training and prototyping. It has named Xanadu, the University of Waterloo, Unitary Foundation and Haiqu as founding partners, and SDT Quantum of Korea as a hardware manufacturing partner.

Cognitive Systems Corp. is a privately held technology company in Waterloo, Ontario, founded in 2014. It develops WiFi Motion, a software stack that senses motion and presence from wireless signals and runs on chipsets, routers and access points. It licenses the technology to chipset makers and service-provider platforms, and in 2026 launched Caregiver by Cognitive for home care agencies. It describes itself as a pioneer in "Spatial Intelligence" and reports 400+ patents. No defence customers or defence programs are published.

ABRO Manufacturing Inc. operates from a unit at 1601 Victoria St N in Kitchener, Ontario. It machines complex, tight-tolerance parts, including multi-axis and mill-turn work, and says it is aiming to supply the Canadian space and aerospace sectors. It also provides CNC applications support, DFMA support and strategic procurement. In a job posting it says it is preparing for AS9100 certification. The organization describes itself as a new, small team.

AXIBO INC is a Cambridge, Ontario robotics company founded by McMaster University engineering graduates. It sells camera motion-control systems with AI subject tracking and Unreal Engine virtual-production support, and names Netflix and Apple as customers. In 2025 it announced a $12 million round to launch Axibo AI, a division building humanoid robot platforms that it says are designed and made in Canada. It states that it designs, prototypes, manufactures, tests and ships its robots in-house.

Canadian Strategic Missions Corporation (CSMC) describes itself as a space and defence company developing dual-use technologies. Its subsidiary CSMC Nuclear is developing the LEUNR micro-reactor and the POLAR-1, ORCA-1 and JAY-1 reactor concepts for remote, defence, research and lunar applications. Its subsidiary CSMC Labs does research and development in quantum sensing, robotics, nano-materials, electrochemistry, industrial automation and space systems. The company was founded in 2020 as the Canadian Space Mining Corporation and has received funding from federal and provincial programs, including DND IDEaS, FedDev Ontario, NGen and the Canadian Space Agency.

ENVGO Inc. is a Waterloo, Ontario marine technology company founded in 2021 by engineers who previously built Aeryon Labs. It integrates hydrofoils, electric and hybrid powertrains, and AI-based autonomy into one vessel platform. Its products are the XV2 micro-USV, which it markets to defence, coast guard and port security users, and the NV1 electric hydrofoil boat for recreational and commercial use. In 2026 it announced an expansion into defence and public safety and an MOU with Open Ocean Robotics.

H2nanO designs nanomaterial-enabled water treatment technologies for the energy and mining sectors. SolarPass is a sunlight-driven oxidation process for contaminated water, Oasis is a passive enhanced-evaporation system for brine and water disposal, and Stratus is a modular low-energy thermal distillation system for high-salinity water. The company reports a 2025 pilot of SolarPass at Imperial Oil's Kearl oil sands mine site. It is headquartered in Kitchener, Ontario, with a western Canada office in Acheson, Alberta.

Intelline Inc. is a Waterloo, Ontario startup that develops CAVIE modules, a patented opposed-piston linear engine that it says is fuel-agnostic and stackable from 50 kW to 2 MW. It offers the power as an energy-as-a-service subscription covering equipment, installation, maintenance and fuel management. The website lists applications in data centres, marine, defence, hybrid vehicles, construction, mining, remote communities and manufacturing. The company says it expects to deploy CAVIE generator systems to its network from 2028. A separate Intelline Works brand sells machined engine parts for performance vehicles.

Quantum Valley Ideas Laboratories (Ideas Lab, QVIL) is an independent research laboratory in Waterloo, Ontario, founded in 2016. It takes quantum sensing ideas to commercial-ready prototypes for commercial and defence applications, then licenses the IP or spins out companies such as WaveRyde Instruments. Its facilities include optics labs, clean fabrication space, additive and subtractive manufacturing, electronics labs and radio frequency testing with a 3 m anechoic chamber rated above 110 GHz. It has stated funding or collaboration from DRDC, DARPA, NRC, NSERC, Mitacs, FedDev Ontario and the Government of Ontario.

TensorOne Inc. is a Kitchener, Ontario company developing counter-UAS systems that combine AI software, acoustic sensors and interceptor drones. It received a National Defence contribution under the IDEaS Innovation Networks program for a Drone Against Drone Interceptor concept. The company is a member of the Waterloo Dual-Use Technology Consortium and has signed an MOU with Volt Carbon Technologies and Solid Ultrabattery to test batteries and carbon materials on its UAS platforms. Its own website is a single landing page with limited detail.

Biomiq Inc. is a Canadian medical device company based in Kitchener, Ontario. It markets BIHOCL-brand hypochlorous acid products for wound care and eye care, along with the PureGel nano-hydrogel, the JetOx jet lavage kit and UV Smart UV-C disinfection devices. In May 2024 it assumed national wound care contracts held by Sterasure Inc., which continues to manufacture BIHOCL products for it in Kitchener. Its published markets are Canadian health care institutions and clinicians, and it donated wound care product to Ukrainian hospitals in 2024.

NAV CANADA owns and operates Canada's civil air navigation service from a network of area control centres, control towers, flight service stations, maintenance centres and flight information centres. It publishes aeronautical information, and it develops and maintains navigation aids and air traffic management technology. At YKF in Breslau, Ontario, it staffs a control tower that opened in June 2017 and replaced a 1969 structure. Its customers are airlines, business aviation and cargo operators, air charters, helicopter operators and general aviation owners.

COPA Flight 26, also called the Breslau Flyers, is a local flight of the Canadian Owners and Pilots Association. It meets on the second Tuesday of each month from September to June, in person and on Zoom, with guest speakers on aviation topics. It holds fly-outs and community events such as Discover Aviation free introductory flights, and it publishes a members' newsletter. Membership is open to pilots and non-pilots for a $30 annual fee.
operating_name: Canadian Owners and Pilots Association Flight 26

abstract_en: The Recreational Aircraft Association Canada represents amateur-built and non-certified aircraft builders and pilots in dealings with Transport Canada, MD-RA Inspection Services and other government bodies. It publishes the bi-monthly Recreational Flyer magazine and posts technical articles and safety notices on its website. It supports local chapters across Canada, including a Kitchener-Waterloo chapter that meets at the Waterloo airport (CYKF), and says it provides $5 million of insurance coverage for all RAA events at no charge. It is run by volunteers, and members pay annual or life fees.

The chapter was chartered in May 2014 and is part of the East Canada Section of The Ninety-Nines. It holds monthly meetings, social and educational events, scholarship information sessions and tours of aviation facilities such as NAV Canada control towers. It takes part in the Girls Can Fly event hosted by Waterloo Wellington Flight Centre. It says it has over 35 members, including student pilots, recreational pilots and professional commercial pilots. It does not make or sell products and has no commercial capabilities.

CATSA was established on April 1, 2002 under the CATSA Act and is accountable to Parliament through the Minister of Transport. Its mandated activities are pre-board screening, hold baggage screening, non-passenger screening and management of the restricted area identity card system. It buys and deploys screening equipment and contracts frontline screening officers from private firms; GardaWorld Security Screening Inc. holds the Central Region (Ontario) contract. At YKF, CATSA operates the pre-board checkpoint and an inline hold baggage screening system in the airport terminal.
operating_name: Canada Air Transport Security Authority at YKF

abstract_en: The Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) is the federal agency responsible for integrated border services. It administers the legislation that governs the admissibility of people and goods into and out of Canada. The Breslau office, listed in the CBSA directory as Kitchener-Waterloo International Airport (Region of) (401), provides air traveller and commercial services at the Region of Waterloo International Airport. This is a government service delivery site. It is not a manufacturer or a supplier of products.
operating_name: Canada Border Services Agency at YKF

abstract_en: The Transportation Safety Board of Canada (TSB) was created by an Act of Parliament in 1990 to advance safety in air, marine, pipeline and rail transportation. It is headquartered in Gatineau, Quebec, has an engineering laboratory in Ottawa, and has investigators in eight regional offices. Its Region of Waterloo International Airport (YKF) presence in Breslau, Ontario, is known only from the airport's business directory, which lists the TSB under government agencies with the TSB's national toll-free number. The TSB does not make or sell products.
operating_name: Transportation Safety Board of Canada at YKF

abstract_en: Transport Canada is a federal government department headquartered in Ottawa, with regional headquarters including one in North York, Ontario. Its published programs include the Airports Capital Assistance Program, which provided funding to the Region of Waterloo International Airport in Breslau, Ontario, in 2021 and 2023. No Transport Canada office, plant or facility in Breslau was found, so the seed label "Transport Canada at YKF" appears to describe the department's funding relationship with the airport rather than a separate organization. The record is therefore built for the department as a whole.

NV Piping Systems Inc. has operated in Cambridge, Ontario since 2007 and fabricates stainless steel, duplex and nickel-alloy pressure piping and pressure vessel internals. Its services include non-destructive examination to ASME B31.1 and B31.3, passivation, mechanical polishing and electropolishing, glass bead-blasting and plasma nitriding. It supplies industrial and municipal customers in water treatment, semiconductor, pharmaceutical, food and beverage, oil and gas, power and pulp and paper. It holds TSSA Certificates of Authorization for shop fabrication of ASME B31.1 power piping and ASME B31.3 process piping.

Qorsa Corp is a Waterloo, Ontario technology company that sells two software platforms: CasQade, a cryptographic-agility and post-quantum security framework, and AtlasAI, an AI data-ingestion and analytics platform. It says it was built from CivicAtlas (launched 2019) and Quantum Secure Solutions (acquired in May 2025). It runs Qorsa Labs, an applied research division with a research relationship with the University of Waterloo. In October 2025 it reported a CasQade demonstration at NATO's SHINE event.

Trylon TSF Inc. runs a 70,000 sq ft steel fabrication plant in Elmira, Ontario. The plant has beam and angle lines, a 1000-ton press, plasma and laser cutting, robotic welding, galvanizing and a paint booth. The company also provides structural engineering, LiDAR and BIM services, field construction (including helicopter-assisted tower erection), and fibre engineering in the United States. Its customers are mainly telecom carriers, tower companies, utilities and mining operators in Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Germany and Romania. It also lists defence and radar support structures as a product line.

Fuchs Lubricants Canada Ltd. is the Canadian company of the FUCHS lubricant group and sells automotive, industrial, grease, metal processing and special application lubricants under brands such as TITAN, CASSIDA, RENOLIN and RENOLIT. It operates production sites in Cambridge, Ontario and Langley, British Columbia, and warehouses in Alberta, Saskatchewan and Manitoba. In August 2025 it opened a new Eastern Canada warehouse and office building in Cambridge. Federal contract records show standing-offer awards from the Department of National Defence for packaged oils and lubricants for the Canadian Armed Forces.

Fastenal Canada, Ltd. is a business-to-business distributor of industrial and construction supplies. It operates from a distribution centre at 900 Wabanaki Drive in Kitchener, Ontario, and says it has more than 200 locations in Canada. It offers inventory management and supply chain services to manufacturers, government agencies and school boards, and it holds a federal standing offer for hand tools and an OECM supplier agreement. The parent company, Fastenal Company, markets defence and aerospace supply programs; the evidence for Canada-specific defence supply is thin.

EverBond Interface Technologies Inc. is a startup founded in 2018 out of the University of Waterloo. It develops a reactive coating that is applied to fabrics and neutralizes toxic chemicals on contact, as an alternative to PFAS-based protective treatments. The company reports Innovate Solutions Canada and Mitacs grants totalling over $1M, a published PCT patent (December 2023), technology licensed to private industry, and a paid collaboration with an industry leader. It is working toward commercialization, and no production facility or certification is published.

Valley Blades Limited designs, manufactures and distributes blades, cutting edges, ground engaging tools (G.E.T.), wear parts and accessories for construction, mining and snow plow equipment. It operates a plant and head office in Waterloo, Ontario and a manufacturing and distribution facility in Edmonton, Alberta. Its published process technology includes CNC machining, robotics, heat treating, casting and forging, and it states ISO 9001 registration. Its products include the patented PolarFlex segmented snow plow blade and the Grader-Link grader blade system.

Firan Technology Group (FTG) operates two units. FTG Circuits makes rigid, HDI, RF, thermal management and rigid-flex printed circuit boards. FTG Aerospace designs and builds illuminated cockpit panels, keyboards, cursor control devices and avionics assemblies, and also covers the FLYHT airborne communications and weather-sensor business in Calgary, which it acquired in December 2024. FTG has plants in Ontario, Alberta, California, Virginia, Massachusetts and Minnesota, a joint venture and a subsidiary in Tianjin, China, and a new aerospace facility in Hyderabad, India. Its shares trade on the TSX as FTG.

Horizon Aircraft is a publicly traded Canadian aerospace original equipment manufacturer headquartered in Lindsay, Ontario. It states that it was co-founded in 2013 and is developing the Cavorite X7 for civil and defence missions such as medevac, search and rescue, cargo and surveillance. It has flown large-scale prototypes and has named suppliers for the fuselage, wings, engine and flight controls of the full-scale aircraft. It published no quality certifications, equipment lists or machining capability on the pages reviewed.

Langtry Blast Technologies Inc. (LBTI) manufactures air blast, wheel blast, suction blast, robotic and hybrid blast machines, plus media reclaim modules and dust collectors, at its Burlington, Ontario plant. It also provides controls programming, preventative maintenance, retrofits, aftermarket parts and operator training for new and existing equipment. The company says it serves the aerospace, automotive, medical, mining and commercial sectors. It lists ISO 9001:2015 and Canadian Welding Bureau certification.

Letar Inc. operates a machine shop at 40 Courtland Avenue in Concord (Vaughan), Ontario. It runs more than 26 CNC machines for 3-, 4- and 5-axis milling and turning, and it also offers sheet metal bending, hardware-installation assembly, in-house CMM inspection and concurrent engineering. Its published approvals include Bombardier, De Havilland and L3Harris, and its published certifications are AS9100D, ISO 9001:2015, Controlled Goods Program and ITAR registration. The company also makes housings and heatsinks for telecommunications equipment, including a rugged first-responder radio device.

Malleum, which operates under the legal name Magnari Inc. and was formerly known as Red Canari, is a research-led cybersecurity firm headquartered in Ottawa. It offers strategy and advisory, risk and compliance, enterprise, application and hardware security assessments, adversarial emulation, and a managed IT and security program called MalleumOne. It states that it serves aerospace, defence, aviation, government, finance, energy and other sectors. It also has offices in Montréal, Delaware and Newcastle upon Tyne.
loc_city_list: Newcastle upon Tyne, England, United Kingdom

abstract_en: Shimco, founded in 1985, makes shims and small precision parts in batches of one to several thousand pieces at its Cambridge, Ontario plant, with in-house milling, turning, shearing, light assembly and Nadcap-accredited chemical processing. It supplies aerospace OEMs, Tier 1 suppliers and maintenance-repair-overhaul customers and states it is registered under the Canadian Controlled Goods Program and the Joint Certification Program. It is building a second plant in Casablanca, Morocco. The company announced in May 2026 that it was acquired by Avantus Aerospace.

Velatron Technologies has operated in Kitchener, Ontario since 1945, when it was founded as S.G. Smallwood Inc. It designs and builds custom transformers, inductors and windings of up to 100 kVA, and also offers reverse engineering, build-to-print work and wound-component repair. It works from an 18,000 sq. ft plant with in-house winding, encapsulation, machining and automated electrical test equipment. It states AS9100D and ISO 9001:2015 certification and is listed in the Controlled Goods Program registry. It supplies aerospace, space, defence, medical, energy and industrial customers.

NORTAC Defence Limited was founded in 2010 and is based in Ottawa, Ontario. It designs hardware and software for beyond-line-of-sight tracking, messaging and situational awareness for military and civil agencies. Its TITAN BY NORTAC platform combines data from satellite short burst data, LTE, radio and other sources into one common operating picture. It states that it supplies tracking and messaging services to Canadian government agencies and that the platform is in use by civil agencies such as police, border control and first responders.

Connect Tech Inc. is a hardware design and manufacturing company in Guelph, Ontario, founded in 1985. It makes rugged embedded computing products, including carrier boards, edge AI systems and peripheral cards. It builds them in an in-house SMT manufacturing facility and offers custom design when off-the-shelf products do not fit. Its markets include aerospace and defence, robotics, industrial automation, mining and agriculture. HEICO Corporation acquired 89.99% of the company in 2020.

Safran Landing Systems Canada Inc. is a wholly owned Canadian subsidiary of Safran Landing Systems SA of France. Its Ajax, Ontario site designs and develops fully integrated landing gear systems, makes components, and assembles and delivers shipsets to North American customers, including Boeing and Bombardier. Its Mirabel, Quebec site produces main landing gear components for Airbus and Boeing and operates special processes such as HVOF coating and zinc-nickel plating. The company holds AS9100D certification and Nadcap accreditations, and is registered in the Controlled Goods Program.

The Oakville site is an RTX business of Collins Aerospace and has operated since 1984. It lists machining, material finishing and assembly, a design, engineering and test lab, and customer support as its focus areas. Published sources name Airbus, Boeing, Bombardier and Gulfstream as customers of the plant. The plant's legal entity appears in federal contract records as Goodrich Aerospace Canada Ltd.

The Toronto-area site is operated as Magtron Aerospace Inc. within Héroux-Devtek, a Longueuil, Quebec landing gear company. It publishes four capabilities: precision machining, vacuum brazing and bonding, electronic chassis manufacturing and complex precision assemblies. In 2009 it won a multi-year contract from Noranco Inc. to braze, heat treat and test avionic housings for the F-35, and in 2010 it passed a Nadcap audit in heat treatment and aluminum vacuum brazing. Héroux-Devtek was acquired by an affiliate of Platinum Equity in February 2025.

Cyclone Manufacturing Inc. is a vertically integrated aerospace supplier. It offers 3- to 5-axis CNC machining, sheet metal fabrication, tube bending and welding, structural assembly, and in-house heat treatment, shot peening, NDT, anodizing and painting. It operates plants in Mississauga and Milton, Ontario, and in Kraśnik, Poland. Its published customers include Boeing, Airbus, Bombardier, Embraer and Lockheed Martin. It holds AS9100D and several Nadcap accreditations, and it is part of the Mubea Aviation group.

Dishon Limited machines and grinds complex components and assemblies from aluminum, stainless steel, Inconel, nickel alloys and titanium. It runs more than 60 machines in Vaughan, Ontario, and a second machining facility in Orlando, Florida. Its work goes into landing gear, engine, aerostructure and fluid-system parts and into space and satellite programs. It describes itself as a Tier 2 supplier to Tier 1 customers and states that it is an AS9100 and ISO 9001 facility registered with the Controlled Goods Program.

Kongsberg Geospatial Ltd. is an Ottawa software company founded in 1992 as Gallium Visual Systems and a wholly owned subsidiary of Kongsberg Defence & Aerospace since 2006. Its TerraLens SDK is used by defence systems integrators to display live sensor data in naval, land, air defence and airborne surveillance systems. It also makes IRIS ground control and airspace visualization software for uncrewed systems, plus THEIA airport surface awareness and MIDAS sensor data exploitation. It provides HMI and UX development and software development services for command and control displays.

Thales Canada Inc. has its head office in the Ottawa (Kanata) area and operates 13 locations in five provinces. It describes itself as a prime contractor and systems integrator for the Department of National Defence, and as the provider of in-service support for Royal Canadian Navy vessels. It designs and manufactures thermal-imaging optronics in Saint-Laurent, Quebec, and operates research and technology centres in Montreal and Fredericton. It also serves civil aviation, public safety, border protection and cybersecurity customers.

Pratt & Whitney Canada Corp. designs and builds gas turbine aircraft engines, including the PT6 family and the PW300 and PW800 turbofans, and is part of Pratt & Whitney, an RTX business. Its Mississauga site is described in trade press as the location for turbofan research and development and for PW300 assembly and testing. An Ontario environmental approval describes the site as a jet engine testing and assembly facility with test engine cells and a paint booth, and a production limit of 1,200 engines a year. Head office is in Longueuil, Quebec. This record covers the Mississauga site, and company-level facts are noted as such.

Ontario Drive & Gear Limited (ODG) was founded in Kitchener in 1962 and is now based in New Hamburg, Ontario. Its Gear division makes custom gears, shafts and assembled, tested gearboxes in a high-mix, low-volume job shop, with in-house design, inspection and metallurgical testing. Its Vehicle division builds ARGO amphibious all-terrain vehicles, and ARGO's Space, Robotics and Defence Division developed the J8 Atlas unmanned ground vehicle, which Defence Research and Development Canada tested under a Build in Canada Innovation Program contract. The company states that ARGO uses about 15 percent of its manufacturing capacity and that 85 percent of its work is for other customers.
loc_city_list: Thief River Falls, Minnesota, United States

abstract_en: Burloak Technologies Inc. prints metal parts by laser and electron beam powder bed fusion and directed energy deposition. It supplies aerospace, space, defence and energy customers from one site in Oakville, Ontario. The same site also does heat treatment, CNC machining, materials testing and inspection. According to its parent's May 2026 release, the business was sold by Samuel, Son & Co., Limited to i3D Manufacturing, a division of BTX Precision.

Celestica Inc. is incorporated in Ontario and trades on the TSX and NYSE. Its Canadian sites are the Toronto head office and a Newmarket, Ontario operation that houses an electronics testing lab and a microelectronics cleanroom lab. It offers design, printed circuit board and box-build assembly, cable and harness work, environmental and vibration testing, repair and overhaul, and obsolescence management for aerospace and defence customers. Its Atrenne unit in Massachusetts makes ruggedized embedded computing systems.

Diamond Aircraft Industries Inc. (Diamond Canada) has built composite aircraft in London, Ontario since 1992. Its London plant assembles the DA20, DA40, DA42 and DA62 families and does contract composite work for other aircraft makers. It also supplies trainers to military and civilian flight schools and special mission platforms for surveillance. Diamond Canada is owned by the Chinese group Wanfeng Aviation and is a sister company to Diamond Aircraft Industries GmbH in Austria.

Liburdi Engineering Limited is the corporate entity of the Liburdi Group of Companies. The group was founded in 1979 and is based at 400 Highway 6 North, Dundas, Ontario. The group publishes four lines of business: gas turbine repair and engineering services, vision-based automated welding systems, orbital welding systems, and code construction welding services. It lists ISO 9001, AS9100, Transport Canada Approved Maintenance Organization status, Nadcap and Controlled Goods registration among its certifications.

C-COM Satellite Systems Inc. was established in 1997 and is headquartered in Ottawa, Ontario. It states that it has shipped over 11,000 iNetVu driveaway, flyaway, manpack and fixed motorized antenna systems to more than 100 countries through a dealer network of 600+ partners. It names military and government as its largest market, and also serves oil and gas, telecom backhaul, broadcast, public safety and education. It is developing an electronically steered Ka-band phased array antenna with the University of Waterloo and an 8-channel beamformer integrated circuit.

Kepler Communications Inc. was incorporated in 2015 and is headquartered in Toronto, with a U.S. subsidiary in Sterling, Virginia. It states that it has launched 33 satellites, including a 10-satellite optical relay tranche launched in January 2026, and that it builds satellites in an in-house production facility. Customers and programs named in its releases include the European Space Agency (ESA), Defence Research and Development Canada (DRDC), the Canadian Space Agency (CSA), the U.S. Space Development Agency (SDA) and NorthStar Earth & Space. The company's published markets are Earth observation, space domain awareness, intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (ISR), and defence.

Founded in 1992, NANOWAVE Technologies Inc. is vertically integrated, covering RFIC design, thin film manufacturing, CNC machining, circuit card assembly, automated hybrid microwave assembly, and system integration and test. It occupies about 50,000 sq. ft. of engineering and manufacturing space in Etobicoke, including Class 100 to 10,000 clean rooms. Its stated products include solid-state power amplifiers, low noise amplifiers, sources and converters, filters, space RF payload equipment and transportable weather radar. It reports AS9100D and ISO 9001:2015 certification and registration in the Controlled Goods Program.

Gastops, incorporated federally as GasTOPS LTD. in 1979, makes the MetalSCAN, ChipCHECK and FluidSIGHT condition monitoring products used on military and commercial aircraft engines, wind turbines, gas turbines and marine engines. It also runs an aerospace component MRO facility and a fluid, filter and chip debris laboratory, and offers modelling, simulation and digital twin engineering. It has offices in Ottawa, Dartmouth (Nova Scotia) and Huntsville (Alabama). Its customers include Pratt & Whitney, Pratt & Whitney Canada, the Royal Canadian Air Force and wind turbine manufacturers.

Allen-Vanguard is an Ottawa-headquartered developer of vehicle-based, man-portable and fixed-site electronic countermeasure (ECM) systems, counter-drone effectors and RF decoy equipment for armed forces, public safety and security agencies. It also provides threat-analysis waveform development, field service representatives, depot-level repair and vehicle integration, with a second engineering site in Tewkesbury, United Kingdom. Court records show that the company and its UK subsidiary were placed into receivership on September 1, 2026, and that the court approved a sale transaction on September 25, 2026.

Sinclair Technologies was founded in Toronto in 1951 and now operates from Aurora, Ontario, as a division of Norsat International Inc., a subsidiary of Hytera Communications. It designs and manufactures antennas, RF signal conditioning products and communication shelters for public safety, transportation, utilities, natural resources and in-building networks. It also offers system engineering, test equipment calibration and product training. Its quality system is certified to ISO 9001:2015, and Government of Canada records show antenna contracts with National Defence.

Electrovaya Inc. is an Ontario-incorporated lithium-ion battery developer and manufacturer headquartered in Mississauga, with a cell and battery plant under development in Jamestown, New York. It states that material handling accounts for over 95% of its sales over the last three years. It also supplies high-voltage battery systems for defence, robotics, airport ground support equipment and stationary storage. It reports ISO 9001 certification since 2022, UL 2580 listings on many battery systems, and a solid-state battery research program at Electrovaya Labs.

Ranovus Inc. is an Ottawa (Kanata) company founded in 2012. It develops the ODIN optical infrastructure platform, a chip that combines silicon photonics with drivers and amplifiers, for AI and machine-learning data centres. Trade press reports that it tests and assembles its products at its Hines Road plant, and it has announced a manufacturing collaboration with Jabil. It runs a Defence and Government Business Unit and is a named participant in a DARPA contract with Cerebras Systems.

Christie Digital Systems Canada Inc. is the Kitchener, Ontario engineering and manufacturing arm of Christie, a visual technologies company that is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Ushio, Inc. of Japan. It designs and manufactures projection and display products under an ISO 9001:2015 certificate covering the design and manufacture of audiovisual solutions. Its published simulation offering covers multi-projector display integration for flight, military, ship bridge, vehicle, medical and air traffic control training. Most of its output is exported, mainly to the United States, Asia and Europe.

Fidus Systems Inc. was founded in 2001 and is headquartered in Kanata (Ottawa), Ontario. It has design centres in Ottawa, Kitchener and Fremont, California. It provides turnkey and staff-augmentation embedded design services to customers in aerospace and defence, communications, semiconductor, medical, industrial and computing markets. It also sells a small line of FMC mezzanine cards. It is registered in the Controlled Goods Program, and Catchment Capital took a majority stake in 2025.

Arnprior Aerospace Inc. was established in Arnprior, Ontario in 1954 and is wholly owned by American Industrial Acquisition Corporation (AIAC). It combines sheet metal fabrication, 3-axis and 5-axis machining, heat treatment, chemical processing, paint and assembly, mostly to customer-furnished designs. Its Arnprior plant closed on March 6, 2024 and its equipment was auctioned in October 2024. The company's website, brochure and 2026 U.S. federal contractor registration still show it operating from Portland, Oregon and Chihuahua, Mexico, with a head office address in Arnprior.

The Ottawa Research Centre (ORC) is one of the research centres of Defence Research and Development Canada (DRDC), part of the Department of National Defence. It states that it began in 1941 and has been a centre for electromagnetic sciences research since the early 1970s. Its published capabilities cover cyber operations, communications and radar electronic warfare, space domain awareness, radar for ISR and C2, space RF intelligence, continental defence modelling, position, navigation and timing, and defence communications. It conducts research and advice for the Canadian Armed Forces and does not publish products, certifications or a plant equipment list.
operating_name: Defence Research and Development Canada (DRDC) — Ottawa

abstract_en: Cohere Inc. was founded in Toronto in 2019 and builds foundation language models (Command, Embed, Rerank, Parse, Transcribe) and the North and Compass AI platforms. It offers cloud, private-cloud, on-premises and dedicated Cohere-managed deployments. Its customers and partners include the Government of Canada, Bell Cyber, Thales Canada (Royal Canadian Navy in-service support), and TKMS (submarine research and prototyping). Cohere publishes its own research through Cohere Labs.

Xanadu designs photonic quantum computing hardware, including the Borealis and Aurora systems, and publishes PennyLane, an open-source quantum programming framework. It runs a 48,000 sq ft headquarters with a nanophotonic facility in Toronto and a photonic packaging facility that it says is open to external academic and industry users. It has research and funding relationships with Canadian and U.S. defence and science programs, and it has announced a 158,000 sq ft manufacturing facility called Inception in Etobicoke. It had 264 employees at December 31, 2025.

Promation was founded in 1995 and describes itself as a privately owned Canadian corporation. It works in-house from concept engineering through machining, welding, assembly, testing and commissioning of custom systems. Its nuclear work includes CANDU refurbishment tooling, fuel handling, waste handling and hot-cell equipment, built under CSA N285.0 and N299.1 quality programs. It also runs internal R&D labs and university research partnerships in additive manufacturing, vision and robotics.

BWXT Canada Ltd. is the Canadian commercial nuclear business of BWX Technologies, Inc., headquartered in Cambridge, Ontario, with plants and operations across Ontario. It states it has supplied more than 300 CANDU and pressurized water reactor steam generators and operates a nuclear clean room for component assembly. It also makes CANDU fuel and fuel channel components through BWXT Nuclear Energy Canada and provides inspection, maintenance and engineering services in the field. Its customers named in public releases include Ontario Power Generation, Bruce Power and GE Hitachi Nuclear Energy.

Carleton University, in Ottawa, Ontario, offers degree programs through five faculties and reports $155.4 M in sponsored research funding for 2024-2025. Its engineering labs include wind tunnels, rotorcraft test facilities, a nanofabrication cleanroom, and autonomous vehicle and 5G labs. Industry and Partnership Services and the Office of the Vice-President (Research, Innovation and International) manage partnerships with companies such as Ericsson, Ross Video, March Networks, IBM and BlackBerry QNX. The university states that it is registered in good standing with the Controlled Goods Directorate, and its Centre for Security, Intelligence and Defence Studies is headquarters of the Canadian Defence and Security Network.

The Royal Military College of Canada (RMC) was founded in 1876 and is part of the Canadian Defence Academy. It offers undergraduate and graduate programs in arts, science and engineering. RMC states that it is a leader in defence research and operates on-campus facilities that include a nuclear reactor, wind tunnels, an anechoic chamber, an ammunition lab and a cyber lab. Some of its research is sensitive or classified.

Toronto Metropolitan University (TMU) is a public university at 350 Victoria Street, Toronto. Its Faculty of Engineering and Architectural Science publishes more than 130 labs and facilities, including aerospace test facilities, wind tunnels, a casting research centre and robotics labs. Zone Learning runs incubators on and off campus, and the Rogers Cybersecure Catalyst runs cybersecurity training and a defence-readiness stream for small and medium-sized businesses. Industry and government partners work with researchers through the Office of the Vice-President, Research and Innovation.

The Downsview Aerospace Campus (the Bombardier Centre for Aerospace and Aviation) is part of Centennial College of Applied Arts and Technology. It opened in 2019 in renovated de Havilland Canada buildings at Downsview Park. It houses the School of Transportation's aviation programs and the School of Engineering Technology and Applied Science's aerospace manufacturing programs. Centennial Innovates, the college's applied research department, runs industry research projects, including the Landing Gear Innovation Lab with Safran Landing Systems. The campus is part of the Downsview Aerospace Innovation & Research (DAIR) hub.

Invest Ottawa is the lead economic development agency for knowledge-based industries in Canada's Capital and was established by the City of Ottawa in 2012. It runs entrepreneurship and technology-company programs, global expansion and foreign direct investment services, and talent programs. It operates Bayview Yards, its headquarters and innovation hub, and Area X.O, a test and R&D complex for smart mobility, connectivity, autonomy and defence technologies that is a NATO DIANA test centre. It also leads the Ottawa–Gatineau Defence Innovation Hub strategy together with the City of Ottawa and Ville de Gatineau.

L-SPARK Corporation, headquartered in Kanata (Ottawa), Ontario, says it was founded in 2014 and supports high-growth startups and scale-ups. It currently runs corporate-partner accelerator programs with TELUS (Sovereign AI) and Mitel (unified communications). It also hosts the SaaS North conference. It employs a Director of Military, Defence and Dual-Use Technologies, and a trade-press report describes a planned dual-use defence accelerator at concept stage.

Area X.O is a gated test and demonstration site that evolved from the Ottawa L5 Connected and Autonomous Vehicle Test Facility, launched in May 2019, and is founded and managed by Invest Ottawa. It offers a 16 km test track, private 4G/5G networks, plug-and-play sensors, a command centre, autonomous shuttles and drones, and engineering, training and compliance-readiness support. It serves smart mobility, communications, agriculture, defence and security, and smart-city users. It was named a NATO DIANA test centre in March 2024.

Kinectrics is a Toronto-based lifecycle services company that works for nuclear operators and electric utilities, with licensed nuclear facilities, high-voltage and high-current labs, and materials labs. It also runs an in-house machine shop and makes products such as nuclear PPE and conductor inspection tools. The company says it has more than 1,300 staff and 19 locations in 7 countries. BWX Technologies completed its acquisition of Kinectrics' parent company in May 2025.

Algoma Steel Inc. is the operating company of Algoma Steel Group Inc. It makes steel at its Sault Ste. Marie works and sells sheet and plate to the automotive, construction, energy, infrastructure, manufacturing, transportation, marine and defence markets. Its Plate Mill, in-plant heat-treating facility and Direct Strip Production Complex make plate, abrasion-resistant and armour grades, and hot-rolled sheet. In 2026 it announced a joint venture with Roshel Inc. and a memorandum of understanding with Hanwha Ocean, both aimed at Canadian defence supply.

Stelco makes hot-rolled, cold-rolled and galvanized or galvannealed steel sheet, as well as pig iron ingots, for automotive, construction and energy customers in Canada and the United States. Lake Erie Works in Nanticoke has a blast furnace, basic oxygen steelmaking, slab casting and a hot strip mill. Hamilton Works in Hamilton has cold rolling and continuous galvanizing lines. Cleveland-Cliffs acquired the company on November 1, 2024. In late September 2026, trade press reported that Stelco would indefinitely idle its Hamilton cold-rolled and coated operations and concentrate production at Lake Erie Works.

Ciena Canada operates Ciena's largest research and development centre in Ottawa, where it designs coherent optical networking hardware and software for network operators and cloud providers. Ciena Corporation, a U.S. parent, publishes the company's website and quality program, and no separate Ciena Canada site was found. Ciena says its products are made by third-party contract manufacturers, including some with facilities in Canada. No Canadian defence contracts, Controlled Goods registration or Canadian-specific certificates were found.

The Ontario Aerospace Council (OAC) was established in 1993 and describes itself as the voice and principal advocate for Ontario's aerospace industry. It says its members represent over 70% of Ontario's aerospace employment base, across all tiers (OEMs, Tier 1–4 suppliers, UAS/UAV, MRO, ground-based infrastructure and space), and that colleges and universities are also members. It works with industry, academia, governments and associations on technology adoption, supply chain readiness, skills development and training, and it publishes a capabilities directory of members. It makes no products and holds no published manufacturing equipment.

ABC Technologies was founded in Toronto in 1974 and supplies plastic components and systems to light vehicle manufacturers. It runs injection moulding, blow moulding, extrusion, robotic painting and assembly, with in-house tooling, machine building, material compounding, design and testing. It was taken private in 2023 and bought TI Fluid Systems in April 2025. The combined business is being rebranded TI Automotive and is headquartered in Auburn Hills, Michigan.

Accuride Canada Inc. operated a light and heavy truck wheel production facility at 31 Firestone Boulevard in London, Ontario, and made blanks, single steel wheels and dual steel wheels. It was a wholly owned subsidiary of Accuride Corporation, and about two-thirds of its sales were to affiliated companies. The company obtained CCAA protection on October 10, 2024, and the plant shut down at the end of January 2025. The monitor's file was still open at the latest update (July 2026).

AMD's Canadian operations are rooted in Markham, Ontario, and began with its 2006 acquisition of ATI Technologies, which was founded in Ontario in 1985. AMD says its Canadian workforce numbers over 2,500 and works on graphics processor (GPU) programming, machine learning algorithms and GPU-accelerated high-performance computing software. The Markham site takes on university interns and co-op students each year. In March 2026 AMD and the University of Toronto announced a joint AI and computing research lab.

Applanix Corporation develops, manufactures, sells and supports the Applanix POS family of GNSS-aided inertial systems, OEM GNSS-inertial boards for drone payloads, and POSPac post-processing software. It was founded in 1991 and has been part of Trimble since 2003. Research, product development, production, calibration, customer support, sales and marketing are all carried out at its Richmond Hill head office. Published markets are mobile mapping, hydrographic survey, vehicle automation and mining.

Applied Brain Research (ABR) spun out of the University of Waterloo's Centre for Theoretical Neuroscience and has worked on brain-inspired, low-power AI since 2012. It publishes streaming speech-to-text and text-to-speech models and a software development kit (SDK). It also has the TSP1 state space accelerator chip, which is designed to run these models on battery-powered devices without a cloud connection. Its stated application areas are augmented reality glasses, wearables, smart home appliances, robotics, medical devices and automotive.
