No defence customers, certifications or manufacturing facilities are published.

Assent (legal name Assent Compliance Inc.) is a private company headquartered at 525 Coventry Road in Ottawa. It sells the Assent Network and Assent Sustainability Platform, along with advisory, supplier engagement and program management services, to manufacturers and distributors. It publishes an Aerospace & Defense industry page and names Boeing, Honeywell, Rolls-Royce and General Electric among its customers. On July 9, 2026 it completed its first acquisition, IPOINT of Reutlingen, Germany.

Atlantis Systems Corp. was the parent of Atlantis Systems International Inc. at 1 Kenview Boulevard, Brampton, Ontario. It designed and delivered maintenance trainers, flight training devices and a naval tactics trainer for military and civil aircraft customers. In 2007 it acquired the Eduplus division of Tecsult Inc. and entered training delivery, which became its largest revenue generator. Bluedrop acquired it in 2013 and merged it into Bluedrop Training & Simulation Inc. in Halifax, Nova Scotia.

ATS Corporation is a publicly traded Canadian automation company founded in 1978 as a special-purpose machine builder. It provides pre-automation engineering, custom and repeat automation systems, standard automation platforms, test solutions, digital tools and after-sale service. Its Canadian operations are centred in Cambridge, Ontario, where its Industrial Automation business designs automated tooling for nuclear refurbishment, decommissioning and new-build projects. The company reports more than 7,000 employees at over 65 manufacturing facilities worldwide.

Avidbots was founded in 2014 and has its head office in Kitchener, Ontario. It builds fully autonomous commercial floor-cleaning robots for airports, warehouses, manufacturing sites, retail, education and healthcare facilities. It says it designs and builds the robots and their proprietary autonomy software, and that it produces them at a Kitchener-Waterloo plant. It reports ISO 9001 and ISO/IEC 27001 certification from BSI Group Inc. and has offices in the United States, India, Colombia and elsewhere.

Babcock & Wilcox Canada Corp. (B&W Canada) is a subsidiary of Babcock & Wilcox Enterprises, Inc. of Akron, Ohio. It publishes contract awards for boiler equipment supply and installation, low-NOx burners, and power plant maintenance in Ontario, New Brunswick, Alberta and Newfoundland and Labrador. Its head office is at 75 Savage Drive, Cambridge, Ontario, and it lists regional operations in Saint John and Edmonton. The affiliated Babcock & Wilcox FPS, Inc. combustion equipment business is in Dartmouth, Nova Scotia.

BAE Systems (Canada) Inc. is the Canadian corporate entity of BAE Systems plc, with offices in Ottawa and Dartmouth, Nova Scotia. It states that it provides design, manufacture, integration and support services for the Canadian Armed Forces across the maritime, land, air, space and digital domains. Its published Canadian work includes the Type 26-based River-class destroyer design, Hawk jet trainers, M777 howitzers and hybrid-electric bus propulsion. Most listed products are built by other BAE Systems group companies in the UK, Sweden, Australia and the U.S.

Bailey Metal Products Limited was founded in 1950 by Sam Bailey and is based in Concord, Ontario. It makes structural and drywall steel framing, drywall trims, clips and connectors, COMSLAB composite floor systems, TotalJoist floor joists and roofing products, and sells through dealers, distributors and retailers. The company says it has over 700 employees and 13 locations in Ontario, Quebec, Alberta and British Columbia. It joined Saint-Gobain in June 2024 and continues to operate under the Bailey brand. No defence or aerospace work is published.

Boart Longyear Canada operates from Ontario as part of the global Boart Longyear group, which is headquartered in Salt Lake City, Utah. The group's Canadian sites include a products office and coring manufacturing site in North Bay, a regional office and percussive manufacturing site in Mississauga, and drilling-services offices and warehouses in Haileybury and Calgary. The group designs, manufactures and sells surface and underground drill rigs, coring and top-hammer tooling and down-hole instrumentation, and runs drilling services for mining customers. The Canadian entity's own legal name, headcount and current certification status are not published on the pages reviewed.

The centre is a 750,000 sq ft campus that opened in May 2024 and replaced Bombardier's Downsview plant. It assembles the Global 5500, 6500, 7500 and 8000 from large structural components made in-house and by suppliers. Its flight-test hangar and engine-run booth are on site, and aircraft are then flown to Montréal for interior completion. The Government of Canada has ordered the Global 6500 built here for the Royal Canadian Air Force, and Saab uses Global airframes for its GlobalEye surveillance aircraft.

Bosch Rexroth Canada Corp. is headquartered in Welland, Ontario, where it engineers and builds custom integrated hydraulic systems and manifold blocks. It sells and services drive and control technology for factory automation, mobile machinery and industrial applications through branches across Canada, and runs a Customer Experience Centre in Burlington, Ontario. It states that its components are used in defence applications such as weapon systems, radar, stabilization systems and simulators, and it offers technical training through the Bosch Rexroth Academy.

The Port Hope Conversion Facility is a Cameco Corporation operation that receives uranium trioxide from Cameco's Blind River Refinery. It converts the trioxide to uranium hexafluoride (UF6) for light water reactor fuel and to uranium dioxide (UO2) powder for CANDU fuel. Cameco describes it as Canada's only uranium conversion facility, with uranium-related products made on the site since 1935. It operates under a Class IB nuclear fuel facility operating licence from the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission and employs 409 people as of December 31, 2025.

CME traces its history to 1871 and operates under an Act of Parliament charter granted in 1902, with the legal name Alliance of Manufacturers & Exporters Canada. It combines policy advocacy with member programs, including Lean and leadership training, peer councils, workforce development, technology adoption support, a members-only B2B sourcing portal and Made Safe health and safety services. In 2026 it launched CME Defence to help small and mid-sized manufacturers enter defence supply chains. It publishes offices in Ottawa, Toronto, Winnipeg, Montréal and other provincial centres.

Cistel Technology Inc. was founded in 1995 by Nishith Goel and is based in Ottawa, Ontario. It lists four service lines: staffing services, modern business solutions, IT security and risk management, and managed services. It sells to Government of Canada and private sector clients, and its contract history on CanadaBuys includes standing-offer work under a PSPC solutions-based informatics vehicle. It also reinvests part of its revenue in research with Canadian universities in power electronics, networking, cybersecurity and natural language processing.

Conestoga College is a public college headquartered at the Doon campus in Kitchener, Ontario, with campuses in Cambridge, Waterloo and other Waterloo Region cities. Its Research, Innovation & Entrepreneurship unit runs applied research centres and labs, including the SMART Centre, which is an NSERC-designated Technology Access Centre. The SMART Centre offers robotics and automation, 3D printing and scanning, electronics prototyping, machine vision, software and cybersecurity services to small and medium-sized businesses. No defence-specific products, certifications or registry entries were found.

Hydrogenics Corporation is a Mississauga, Ontario developer of hydrogen electrolyzers and fuel cell systems that Cummins Inc. acquired in 2019. Its Mississauga facility assembles PEM cell stacks for the HyLYZER 500 and 1000 electrolyzer systems and supports hydrogen research and development. In February 2026 Cummins announced it would stop new electrolyzer sales, and in April 2026 Alstom acquired Cummins' rail hydrogen fuel cell activities. Cummins told Railway Gazette International that the sale included the Hydrogenics entity, so current ownership and operations need review.

Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is a Crown corporation created in 1951 under the Defence Production Act. It acts for National Defence and the Canadian Armed Forces by procuring and managing infrastructure, real property and environmental projects. Its work includes tendering and awarding about 2,000 contracts a year, on-site contract management, environmental science and engineering services, and project and program management. It is not a manufacturer and does not publish production equipment or processes.

Dejero was founded in 2008 and is headquartered in Waterloo, Ontario, with U.S. and U.K. offices. Its products include the EnGo mobile transmitters, GateWay and TITAN routers, WayPoint receivers, CuePoint return servers and the Control management platform, all built on its patented Smart Blending Technology. It states that it serves broadcast, media production, public safety, enterprise and government and defence customers, and that Dejero Control holds FedRAMP Moderate authorization. It reports ISO 9001:2015 certification and 142 patents (100 issued, 42 pending).

DENSO Manufacturing Canada, Inc. (DMCN) is a wholly owned subsidiary of DENSO Corporation that operates a single-building thermal manufacturing campus on 43 acres at 900 Southgate Drive, Guelph, Ontario. It makes HVAC units, radiators, condensers, engine fans and engine cooling modules for DENSO's North American automaker customers. The company states more than 700 team members in 2026 and lists IATF 16949, ISO 9001 and ISO 14001 certificates on its page. No defence products, named customers or equipment lists are published.

The Descartes Systems Group Inc. develops and operates software-as-a-service applications and a messaging network for shippers, carriers, freight forwarders, customs brokers and logistics service providers. Its products cover customs filing, export compliance and denied-party screening, transportation management, fleet routing and telematics, ecommerce fulfilment and EDI connectivity. It is publicly traded on the TSX and Nasdaq. Its published defence link is export compliance software used by a U.S. defence-industry compliance provider.

The site at 461 Front Road in Kingston, Ontario is the Kingston Technology Centre (KTC), operated by the legal entity EIDCA Specialty Products Company. It was a DuPont site until DuPont's electronics business was spun off as Qnity Electronics on November 1, 2025. Qnity describes it as its centre of excellence for process development and scale-up. Its federal pollutant-release filing describes the site as mainly research and development with some small-scale manufacturing, and reports 74 full-time-equivalent employees.

Epiroc Canada Inc. is headquartered in Mississauga, Ontario, with branches across Canada and a main equipment and electrification site in Lively (Greater Sudbury), Ontario. Its published portfolio covers drill rigs, loaders and trucks, raiseboring equipment, rock drilling tools, battery-electric conversion, automation and digital solutions, and parts and services. A remanufacturing centre in Lively rebuilds mining equipment components. Its drilling tools plant in Langley, British Columbia, is scheduled to close by the first quarter of 2027.

Ericsson Canada Inc. has operated in Canada since 1953 and has head office in Mississauga, Ontario. It provides 5G network products and services to Bell, Rogers, TELUS and other service providers, and private network solutions to utilities and mines. Its R&D centres in Ottawa and Montreal work on 5G Advanced, 6G, Cloud RAN, AI and quantum technologies. In May 2026 it announced a partnership with the Government of Canada to build a 5G test network for defence and public safety users.

F&P Mfg., Inc. is a subsidiary of Ftech Inc. of Japan, with its main plant in Tottenham, Ontario. It states that it produces more than 58 million component parts a year, with stamping, hydroforming, robotic welding, e-coat paint and modular assembly done in-house. It publishes an IATF 16949:2016 certificate issued by SGS. It also runs a die shop and a QA test lab. It is listed as a supplier to Honda and General Motors through supplier awards.

Fanshawe College of Applied Arts and Technology is a comprehensive college with campuses in London, Simcoe, St. Thomas and Woodstock. Its Norton Wolf School of Aerospace, Information and Defence Technologies trains aircraft maintenance and avionics technicians from an airport hangar in London, and in October 2026 the college was announced as the delivery partner for RCAF aviation maintenance training at CFB Borden. Its Centre for Research and Innovation offers applied research for industry, and the Fanshawe Product Testing lab offers electrical, environmental, mechanical and acoustic testing.

Field Aviation Company Inc. (Field Canada) designs, integrates, tests and certifies structural, avionics and mission-system modifications for government and commercial aircraft, including Challenger and Dash 8 special mission platforms. It has operated in Canada since 1947 and is part of the U.S.-owned Field Aerospace group. Its Calgary parts-manufacturing business was sold to De Havilland Canada in 2024. It filed notices of intention to make a proposal on June 5, 2026, and its assets were sold to De Havilland Canada and PAL Aerospace on July 31, 2026. The entity continues only to finish a Challenger modification for Draken Europe and export the aircraft.

Field Effect Software Inc. was incorporated federally in 2016 and has its head office in Ottawa, with offices in the United States, United Kingdom and Australia. It builds its own managed detection and response platform covering endpoint, network, cloud and DNS, backed by a 24x7 security operations centre. It also offers digital forensics and incident response, incident response readiness planning and cybersecurity assessments. It sells through managed service providers, value-added resellers and carrier partners such as TELUS.

Flying Colours Corp. is based at Peterborough Airport in Ontario and has facilities in St. Louis, Missouri and, as of 2019, Singapore. It maintains, refurbishes, paints and modifies business aircraft, and it has done special mission conversions such as multi-mission Dash 8-400 interiors and CRJ700 modifications. Flexjet acquired the company in August 2023, and its website now operates under the Flexjet Technical Services brand.

Fortinet Technologies (Canada) ULC is the Canadian operating entity of the cybersecurity vendor Fortinet, Inc. It runs a research and development and FortiGuard threat-intelligence centre in Burnaby, British Columbia, plus offices in Ottawa and Calgary. It sells firewalls, secure networking, security operations software and subscription services, and it runs the Fortinet Training Institute programs. Shared Services Canada has selected it to secure federal enterprise internet and IT infrastructure.

Frontier Lithium Inc. is headquartered in Val Caron (Greater Sudbury), Ontario, and has not yet started commercial production. It holds the PAK, Spark and Bolt spodumene deposits north of Red Lake and operates the project through a joint venture in which Mitsubishi Corporation holds 7.5%. It has produced spodumene concentrate and battery-quality lithium hydroxide monohydrate at sample and mini-pilot scale, and it plans a lithium conversion facility on Mission Island in Thunder Bay.

abstract_en: Galaxia is a Halifax-based Canadian space technology company founded in 2020. It sells MissionOne, a turnkey service covering spacecraft design, manufacturing, integration, launch and operations. It also makes the Onyx Edge onboard compute system and offers Virtual Satellite-as-a-Service (VSaS). Published work includes a Defence Research and Development Canada (DRDC) tactical satellite contract and an autonomous flight safety system for Maritime Launch Services.

Gedex, legally Gedex Systems Inc., says it was incorporated in 1999 and is a private company developing earth-imaging technology for resource discovery. Its HD-AGG gravity gradiometer, GeoMIM isolation platform and inversion algorithms were built for airborne exploration surveys, and it has named De Beers and Noble Mineral Exploration as users. The company entered Companies' Creditors Arrangement Act (CCAA) protection in August 2019 and most of its assets were sold to FCMI Parent Co. that November. The current website (gedex.ca) shows activity in 2022 to 2024, including the purchase of a survey aircraft, but the current operating entity is not confirmed.

The Whitby mill operates under Gerdau Ameristeel Corporation, a subsidiary of Brazil-based Gerdau S.A. and part of Gerdau Long Steel North America. It melts scrap in an electric arc furnace, casts billets and hot-rolls them in a bar mill and a structural steel mill. It also runs an on-site scrap shredder and non-ferrous scrap separation. The mill's own published certificate list shows ISO 9001, ISO 14001 and ABS facility approval, and the CWB lists a W47.1 welding certification for the site.

Sudbury Integrated Nickel Operations (Sudbury INO) is Glencore's nickel mining, milling and smelting complex in the Sudbury basin. It includes the Fraser Mine, the Strathcona Mill, the Sudbury Smelter and the Onaping Depth project at Craig Mine. The smelter treats concentrate from Sudbury and Raglan Mine, as well as third-party concentrates and secondary materials. The nickel matte it produces is shipped through Quebec City to Glencore's Nikkelverk refinery in Norway.

The plant at 570 Glendale Avenue opened in 1952 and covers about 2 million square feet. GM publishes the Gen 5 V8 engine as its current product, and other GM and chamber listings add the GF6 transmission and a V6 engine. In April 2026 GM Canada announced a C$691 million investment so the plant can build the sixth-generation V-8 engine. Its output ships to GM assembly plants worldwide.

HARD-LINE was founded in 1996 in the Sudbury area and is headquartered in Dowling, Ontario. It designs and builds radio remote controls, the TeleOp tele-remote system, camera systems, proximity detection, network infrastructure and remote-controlled low-profile loaders, mainly for underground mining. In July 2023 it was acquired by Hexagon AB and became part of Hexagon's Mining division. No defence customers or defence products are published.

Honeywell Aerospace is an aerospace and defence supplier whose Canadian operations are centred on Mississauga, Ontario, with a space products site in Cambridge, Ontario and a repair and overhaul site at Slemon Park, Prince Edward Island. Its Canadian work includes electric power and thermal management systems, satellite communications payloads, space science instruments and fuel control unit repair. Customers named in public sources include the Department of National Defence and the Canadian Space Agency. Honeywell Aerospace Inc. became an independent public company on June 29, 2026.

Husky Technologies, founded in 1953, builds plastic injection moulding systems, PET preform and closure moulds, hot runner systems, mould controllers and integrated turnkey systems for beverage, food and consumer packaging and for medical applications. It supports customers in more than 140 countries through service, parts, remote monitoring and training offerings. Its head office and primary manufacturing site are in Bolton, Ontario, with additional manufacturing in the United States, Luxembourg, Switzerland, India and China. Since January 2026 it has been a wholly owned subsidiary of GPGI, Inc. (NYSE: GPGI).

Founded in 2002 at the University of Waterloo, the Institute for Quantum Computing (IQC) is headquartered in the Mike & Ophelia Lazaridis Quantum-Nano Centre. It brings together faculty from the Faculties of Engineering, Mathematics and Science in 17 research groups, and offers Master's and PhD programs in quantum information. It hosts quantum research laboratories and gives academic, industry and government users access to the Quantum-Nano Fabrication and Characterization facility. IQC leads the science team for the Canadian Space Agency's QEYSSat quantum encryption satellite mission, and it lists 20 spin-off companies.

Kinaxis was founded in Ottawa in 1984 as Cadence Computer Corporation and has been listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange since 2014. It sells Maestro (formerly RapidResponse) on a subscription basis to manufacturers and distributors in industries that include aerospace and defence, automotive, life sciences and industrial manufacturing. It also provides professional services, customer support, training and certification, and works through a network of system integrator, cloud and solution-extension partners.

KSR International Inc. is a Tier 1 automotive supplier that says it was founded in 1948 in Ridgetown, Ontario, and it has plants in North America, Europe and Asia. Its products are fixed, adjustable and electronic pedal modules, e-brake and e-clutch (by-wire) systems, and inductive and Hall effect sensors. It states that it holds more than 50 U.S. patents and does in-house testing. Angstrom Automotive Group of Southfield, Michigan acquired it in July 2025, according to trade press.

Kuntz Electroplating Inc. (KEI) has operated in Kitchener, Ontario since 1948 and describes itself as a Tier 1 and Tier 2 supplier of plated and powder-coated components. Its single plant runs automated copper-nickel-chrome plating lines, a powder coating plant, a Type II anodizing line and robotic polishing cells, supported by in-house quality control and process chemistry laboratories. It also offers sub-assembly, packaging, logistics and supply chain management for die castings, forgings, stampings and extrusions. Its 2025 corporate overview lists military and nuclear applications among its work, but names no defence customers.

LAVAL Tool & Mould Ltd. was founded in 1975 and builds, repairs and services medium to large compression and injection moulds, with prototype tooling. Its Innovations Division offers tool sampling and compression moulding production on hydraulic presses of 250 to 2,500 tons. The company states that it is registered under the Controlled Goods Program and with ITAR, and that it supplies military, automotive, heavy truck and other customers. It publishes ISO 9001:2015 and IATF 16949 certificates on its website.

DRS Technologies Canada Ltd. is the Canadian subsidiary of Leonardo DRS, Inc. and is headquartered in Kanata (Ottawa), Ontario. It makes the SHINCOM shipboard communications system, infrared search and track and other sensor systems, deployable flight recorders and emergency locator beacons. It also provides turnkey and build-to-print electronics manufacturing for defence, space and aerospace customers. Its Pivotal Power division in Bedford, Nova Scotia, makes military-specification power conversion equipment and uninterruptible power supplies.

Lumentum is a U.S.-headquartered, publicly traded maker of optical and photonic components and systems for cloud and AI data centres, telecommunications networks, industrial lasers and 3D sensing. Its Canadian operating entity, Lumentum Ottawa ULC, is at 61 Bill Leathem Drive in Ottawa. The company's ISO 9001 certificate lists that site as performing design, development, product line management, operations engineering, quality, customer service, sales and lab operations. Lumentum also publishes a government, aerospace and defence product line of pump lasers, photodiodes, modulators and tunable laser assemblies.

The Haley division has operated in Renfrew County since 1952 and makes large, complex magnesium and aluminum sand castings such as engine inlet, fan and intermediate cases, accessory gearbox housings, APU gearboxes and helicopter transmission housings. It uses 3D sand printing, automated pouring, CNC finishing, digital radiography and 3D scanning. Castings are machined and assembled at other Magellan sites. Magellan publishes long-term supply agreements with Pratt & Whitney Canada, Pratt & Whitney and Collins Aerospace that cover Haley-produced castings.

Mansour Mining Technologies Inc. (MMTI) was established in Sudbury, Ontario in 1976 as Mansour Mining Inc. It made ground support solutions, smelter hardware, rock drilling tools, mine ventilation products and custom fabricated products at an ISO 9001 manufacturing facility in Sudbury, with sales and service offices in Quebec, Saskatchewan and Mexico. Local news reports that it was acquired in October 2019 and has since operated as DSI Underground Canada, which is part of Sandvik. The former website, mansourmining.com, now redirects to Sandvik's ground support page.

Martello Technologies Group Inc. (TSXV: MTLO) develops and sells monitoring software. Its products are Vantage DX, a SaaS platform for Microsoft 365 and Teams, and Mitel Performance Analytics (MPA), which Mitel sells to its customers and partners. In October 2025 the company moved Vantage DX to End of Sale status and refocused on the Mitel business and AI-based IT monitoring. It is headquartered in Kanata (Ottawa), Ontario, and has operating subsidiaries in the United States, France, the Netherlands and Switzerland. Nothing published indicates defence or manufacturing activity.

Mitel develops and sells hybrid (cloud, on-premises and hosted) business communications platforms, including MiVoice Business, OpenScape Voice, MiCollab and Mitel CX, together with desk devices and professional services. Its website lists a Government & Defense industry page and a critical-communications offering for government, public safety and emergency response. It completed a financial restructuring on June 20, 2025. Its Ottawa (Kanata) office is the only North American location listed in the excerpt of the company's locations page that was readable.

Mold-Masters was founded in 1963 and says it was the first company to make hot runners exclusively. Its global headquarters is at 233 Armstrong Avenue, Georgetown, Ontario. The company sells hot runners, controllers, auxiliary injection units, co-injection systems and aftermarket services (MasterCARE) to moulders and mould makers in automotive, medical, packaging, consumer goods and electronics markets. It is an operating company of Hillenbrand, Inc., which Lone Star Funds acquired in February 2026.

Nanometrics is a privately owned Canadian company with two business units: Seismic Instruments and Systems, and Seismic Monitoring Services. It supplies instruments and networks to scientific institutions, universities and government agencies, and turnkey monitoring and data analysis to oil and gas, mining, carbon sequestration and critical infrastructure operators. Its published customers include Natural Resources Canada, the United States Geological Survey and the U.S. Air Force Technical Applications Center.

The National Research Council of Canada (NRC) operates 12 research centres and a business unit, with facilities in 24 locations across Canada and about 4,505 full-time equivalent staff. It works with industry, academia and the Department of National Defence on projects such as aircraft structural life extension, wind-tunnel and ice-tank testing, military vehicle digital twins, quantum security and drone and counter-drone development. It also runs the NRC Industrial Research Assistance Program (NRC IRAP), which gives advice and funding to small and medium-sized businesses, and it hosts five NATO DIANA test centres. Its Metrology Research Centre provides measurement services and certified reference materials.

Nemak of Canada Corporation operated the Windsor Aluminum Plant and the Nemak Engineering Centre on G.N. Booth Drive in Windsor, Ontario. The plant cast aluminum engine blocks and cylinder heads for automotive customers, including General Motors and Shanghai General Motors. In 2019 Nemak announced it would end manufacturing in Windsor by mid-2020. A union dispute followed. The current Nemak group website lists no Canadian location, so current activity is unconfirmed.

Nordion supplies industrial-grade and medical-grade Cobalt-60 sealed sources and designs, builds and services gamma irradiation systems. It operates a CNSC-licensed Class 1B nuclear substance processing facility in Ottawa (Kanata) and an ISO/IEC 17025 accredited dosimetry laboratory. It also provides source transport containers and logistics, irradiator upgrades, sample irradiation, modelling and radiation safety training. Its customers are gamma sterilization and food irradiation operators, and it is a subsidiary of Sotera Health.

The centre in Kennesaw, Georgia opened in 2012 as the hub for Novelis research and development in the beverage can, automotive and specialty aluminum markets. It houses materials development and testing laboratories and beverage can-making lines. Novelis Inc. is incorporated federally in Canada, is a subsidiary of Hindalco Industries Limited, and operates a rolling plant in Kingston, Ontario. The Kennesaw centre itself is outside Canada.
operating_name: Novelis Global Research and Technology Centre

abstract_en: OVIN is the Government of Ontario's flagship initiative for the automotive and mobility sector. It is led by the Ontario Centre of Innovation (OCI) and delivers R&D co-investment, talent development, technology pilot and demonstration zones, incubators, global market-entry support and a network of nine Regional Technology Development Sites. It supports connected and autonomous, electric, charging, semiconductor and hardware technologies. In October 2026 it added a funding stream for defence, dual-use and space technologies.

Optiwave Systems Inc. was founded in 1994 in Ottawa and develops photonic design automation software, including OptiSystem, OptiFDTD, OptiBPM, OptiFiber, OptiGrating, OptiMode, OptiSPICE, OptiInstrument and OptiOmega. It states that its software has been licensed to more than 1,000 corporations and universities in over 70 countries. It also provides software training, custom engineering design services and a cloud simulation service. It publishes a defence communications applications page and has collaborated with the National Research Council of Canada and the University of Ottawa on free-space optical link simulation.

OTTO Motors makes a line of autonomous mobile robots (OTTO 100, 600, 1200, 1500 and Lifter) with its own navigation software (OTTO Autonomy) and a fleet-management platform (OTTO Fleet Manager). It also offers support plans, operator and technician training, and facility simulation. Its published markets are automotive, consumer packaged goods, food and beverage, and other manufacturing. Rockwell Automation acquired Clearpath Robotics and OTTO Motors in October 2023, and OTTO now trades as OTTO by Rockwell Automation.

The input name, Patriot One Technologies, is the former name of Xtract One Technologies Inc., a Toronto-headquartered company listed on the TSX. It sells the SmartGateway and Xtract One Gateway screening systems and the Xtract One View security management platform. These use proprietary AI and sensors to detect firearms, knives and other prohibited items without stopping people at the entrance. Its published markets are mostly civilian. Its former subsidiary-led work included contracts with Canada's Department of National Defence in 2020 and 2021.

Peraso Inc. designs mmWave baseband and RF integrated circuits, phased-array antenna modules, and firmware and software. It reports that it has developed mmWave technology since 2008. It sells to wireless internet service provider equipment makers, and it has announced military drone communications and identification-friend-or-foe design wins. It owns no fabrication, packaging or production test facility, and it relies on third-party vendors to manufacture, package, assemble and test its products. The record covers the Peraso group: Peraso Inc. (Delaware, San Jose) with its Canadian head office in Toronto and a research site in Markham.

Peraton Canada was established in 2017 and is now Arcfield Canada Corp. It is headquartered in Calgary and supports the Canadian Armed Forces and the Royal Canadian Air Force on the CF-18 fleet, with supply chain management, engineering solutions, and maintenance, repair and overhaul of avionics and automated test equipment. It works from a Calgary repair and engineering facility and from warehouses at Cold Lake, Alberta and Bagotville, Quebec. It holds DND Technical Airworthiness accreditations and states ISO 9001:2015 and AS9100D certification.

Polycorp Ltd. was founded in 1996 and is headquartered at 33 York Street West, Elora, Ontario. It develops rubber and other elastomer compounds and makes moulded and extruded components, protective linings and wear systems from them. It publishes an engineering services group, an ISO 9001:2015 quality management system claim and a defence and aerospace product line covering seals, vibration isolation and insulation. It is majority owned by Arsenal Capital Partners and acquired Burke Industries (San Jose, California) in 2025 and Iron Horse Engineering in 2026.

Rail-Veyor Technologies Global Inc. (Railveyor, RVTG) sells a haulage system made of stationary electric drive stations, light-rail track, steel rail cars and proprietary automation software. It engineers each installation to the customer's site, oversees installation and commissioning, and supports the system after handover. Installations are published for mines in Quebec, Missouri, Kazakhstan and South Africa, and for a petroleum coke line in South America. The head office and a test facility are in Sudbury, Ontario, and an engineering Tech Center is in Houghton, Michigan.

Raytheon ELCAN Optical Technologies is the Midland, Ontario optics business of Raytheon Canada Limited, which is owned by RTX. It makes optical and electro-optical sub-systems for missile guidance, cockpit displays, space imaging and high-energy laser systems, and the ELCAN Specter line of weapon sights. In-house work includes optical design, fabrication, thin film coating, diamond point turning, assembly, alignment and test. Recent contracts include Specter DR sights for NATO Support and Procurement Agency (NSPA) customers and the German Armed Forces.

Redpath Canada Limited operates from North Bay, Ontario as the Americas operational management arm of the Redpath Group, which was founded in 1962. It provides shaft sinking, mine development, mass excavation, production mining, raiseboring, mechanized raise mining, underground construction, production drilling and in-house engineering. It also designs and supplies the Redbore family of raise drills. Its Canadian project work includes Hudbay's 777 Mine, the BHP Jansen potash shafts, Glencore's Raglan Mine and the Éléonore Mine.

Rock Tech Lithium is developing lithium converters that would turn spodumene and recycled-battery lithium into battery-grade lithium hydroxide and carbonate. It also owns the Georgia Lake spodumene project near Beardmore, Ontario. The Guben converter in Germany is fully permitted but not yet built. The Red Rock converter in Ontario is at the feasibility stage. The company reports 16 employees (2 in Canada and 14 in Germany) as of December 31, 2025.

Ross Video is a privately held Canadian company headquartered in Iroquois, Ontario, with an R&D campus in Ottawa. It designs and builds hardware and software for live production, including switchers, routing and signal processing, graphics, camera motion systems and media workflow. It manufactures electronics in-house on surface mount lines at Iroquois and sells to customers in more than 121 countries. It also operates a mobile production services unit and a creative services group.

Sault College is a publicly funded Ontario college that opened in 1965 as the Ontario Vocational Centre. It offers diploma, degree, certificate, apprenticeship and continuing education programs, including aviation, engineering technology and skilled trades. Its Applied Research Office carries out funded projects with Sault Ste. Marie companies, using robotics and automation labs, faculty and students. The college also operates a flight training hangar at the Sault Ste. Marie Airport and sells customized corporate training.

Sciencetech Inc. has designed and manufactured optical spectroscopy instruments and solar simulators in Canada since 1985. Its product lines include xenon arc light sources, solar simulators, monochromators, far-infrared (terahertz) systems, quantum efficiency and photovoltaic testing equipment, and custom-built instruments. It sells mainly to research institutions, space agencies and universities through direct sales and a network of international representatives. It received Canadian Space Agency support to build a laser-ablation spectrometer prototype for planetary exploration.

Seneca Polytechnic (legally Seneca College of Applied Arts and Technology) is an Ontario public college with campuses in Toronto, King City and Peterborough. It offers degree, diploma, certificate and graduate programs, customized corporate training, and an aviation school with flight simulators and a flight-training campus at Peterborough Airport. Seneca Applied Research is the single point of access for industry partners and runs three applied research centres, covering life sciences and cosmetic science, artificial intelligence, and health and social innovation. Its HELIX incubator supports student, graduate, employee and community start-ups.

Sherritt International Corporation refines nickel and cobalt at Fort Saskatchewan, Alberta, from mixed sulphide produced at the Moa joint venture in Cuba. It also operates a fertilizer, ammonia and sulphuric acid site at Fort Saskatchewan and holds a one-third interest in Energas, a Cuban power generator. Its Technologies group develops and licenses pressure-leach and related hydrometallurgical processes and is advancing a nickel and cobalt sulphate project for battery supply chains. Trade press reported in June 2026 that the Fort Saskatchewan refinery was shut down after its Cuban feed ran out.
loc_city_list: Varadero, Boca de Jaruco and Puerto Escondido, Cuba

abstract_en: The Peterborough plant at 1954 Technology Drive makes level, weighing and process protection instruments under the Siemens SITRANS name and the legacy Milltronics brand. It also assembles flow, pressure, temperature and valve positioner products. Siemens Canada acquired Milltronics Ltd. in 2000. In June 2025 Siemens announced it would wind down Peterborough manufacturing by September 2027 and move it to its Concord, Ontario plant. Product management and research and development teams for the Measurement Intelligence business will stay in Peterborough.

Sky Harbour Aircraft Refinishing, Goderich, Ontario, described itself as offering aircraft maintenance, modifications, interiors and painting for corporate aircraft, general aviation aircraft and warbirds. The town of Goderich's airport history says the business became internationally known for painting warbirds and peaked at over 100 employees. The same town source says it closed in 2009, and the company website still online carries a 2008 copyright notice. The record is therefore treated as dormant, pending a registry check.

Skyjack was formed in 1985 and has been part of Linamar Corporation since 2002. It makes mobile elevating work platforms and telehandlers, sold mainly to equipment rental companies. Its Guelph plants carry CWB certification for fusion welding of steel, and it has added plants in Mexico, China and Hungary since 2022. Operator and service training, technical manuals and the ELEVATE telematics system accompany the machines.

Skyway Canada Limited is a Toronto-headquartered contractor that has served industrial and commercial construction and maintenance clients since 1967, with branches from British Columbia to Nova Scotia. It adds insulation, rope access, fireproofing, coatings and abatement to a scaffolding and shoring base, and sells scaffold materials through an online store. It also runs a proprietary digital project management platform, Skytrax, which it reports as SOC 2 Type 2 certified. It works with Indigenous communities through several joint ventures.

Solace Power Inc. is a deep-tech company in Mount Pearl, Newfoundland and Labrador. It designs wireless power and data transfer technology that removes wire harnesses, connectors and slip rings. Its aerospace and defence work includes repeat contracts with Boeing, and it is setting up a surface mount technology (SMT) production facility. It also sells through-glass modules for telecommunications and serves automotive and industrial customers.

Space Canada was announced on March 3, 2022 as a national association for Canada's space sector, led by CEO Brian Gallant. It advocates for the sector to federal decision-makers, including for a National Space Council, and publishes policy reports such as one on connecting the space sector to national defence. It runs annual events, including Space Day on the Hill, a Parliamentary Reception and the SpaceBound conference. Its member page lists about 100 logos across founding members, members and associate members, including satellite operators, launch firms, Earth observation companies, universities and investors.

SFL was founded in 1998 at UTIAS in Toronto to build the MOST microsatellite, and it grew into a developer of satellite platforms from 3 to 500 kg. It designed its own onboard computers, radios, power systems and attitude control, and it tested satellites at its Microsatellite Science and Technology Centre. Its customers included HawkEye 360, GHGSat, the Norwegian Space Agency, NASA and Canada's Department of National Defence. The university's SFL site now states that satellite manufacturing is closing and that it is not accepting new clients, and it refers clients to SFL Missions Inc.

Brampton Assembly Plant has 2.95 million square feet of floor space on 269 acres at 2000 Williams Parkway East, Brampton, Ontario. The attached Brampton Satellite Stamping Plant makes inner and outer body stampings. Production of the Chrysler 300, Dodge Charger and Dodge Challenger ended in December 2023. Retooling for the Jeep Compass was paused in February 2025, and Stellantis lists the plant as on operational pause. In September 2026 Stellantis signed a memorandum of understanding with Roshel, a Canadian armoured vehicle maker, on a potential sale of the plant.

The Windsor Assembly Plant opened in 1928 and has built minivans since 1983. It occupies 4.4 million square feet on 177 acres at 2199 Chrysler Centre, Windsor. Current products are the Chrysler Pacifica, the Chrysler Grand Caravan (Canadian market only), the Dodge Charger Daytona and the Dodge Charger SIXPACK. Press reports put the workforce at over 6,000 after a third shift was added in early 2026. The plant is a Tier 1 vehicle-assembly site rather than a defence supplier, and it faces U.S. tariff pressure that has idled it repeatedly.

SYMX.AI, formerly Symboticware, sells X.Machines, X.Parts, X.Connect, X Tires and X Inspect for fleet monitoring, predictive maintenance and site connectivity. Its customers named on its website include Agnico Eagle, Vale, Glencore and Epiroc. The company's website now has a defence page describing adaptation of the platform to military fleet readiness. It is headquartered in Greater Sudbury, Ontario, with offices in Calgary, Toronto, Chicago, Elko and Gurgaon.

The Waterloo, Ontario operation is the former Aeryon Labs, a small-drone maker founded in 2007 and acquired by FLIR Systems in 2019. It is now part of Teledyne FLIR Defense within Teledyne Technologies. Its SkyRanger R70 is built in Waterloo and carries sensor payloads of up to 3.5 kg. In February 2024 Canada's Department of National Defence announced a purchase of more than 800 R70 systems, valued at over CAD$95 million, for donation to Ukraine.

Teledyne Lumenera is the trade name of Lumenera Corporation of Ottawa, Ontario. It develops cameras and camera software for industrial, scientific, life science and aerial imaging applications. It also provides custom and OEM design services that range from private-labelled enclosures to made-to-spec camera designs. Teledyne Technologies acquired the business from Roper Technologies in February 2019, and it is now listed as part of Teledyne Vision Solutions.

Tenstorrent is a computing company that designs AI processors, accelerator cards and systems, and an open-source software stack to run them. It also licenses RISC-V CPU and AI core designs to other chip makers. The company was founded in Toronto in 2016 and now lists its headquarters in the United States, with its Canadian engineering office in Toronto. It states that it relies on ISO 9001-certified manufacturing partners rather than operating its own plant.

Terradyne Armored Vehicles Inc. of Newmarket, Ontario designs, builds and supports the Gurkha LAPV, MPV, RPV and CIV armoured vehicles. It was launched in 2011 as a Magna International business unit and became an independent company in 2014. It says design and manufacturing are done in-house, with roughly 50 employees and about 100 vehicles built per year. Vehicles are sold directly or through dealers to law enforcement, military and civilian customers in Canada, the United States, Europe and the Middle East.

Thoth Technology Inc. (ThothX) was founded in 2001 and is based in Ontario. It makes Argus infrared spectrometers and Aurora infrared line-scan cameras for small satellites and uncrewed aircraft, and it offers thermal vacuum and vibration testing of space hardware. It operates the Algonquin Radio Observatory, including the Earthfence geostationary-orbit radar used for space domain awareness. In September 2025 MDA Space announced a Department of National Defence standing offer for space situational awareness that it will deliver in partnership with ThothX Group.

Tigercat Industries is a privately owned Canadian manufacturer headquartered in Brantford, Ontario, founded in 1992. It makes forestry equipment under the Tigercat and TCi brands, along with industrial carriers, mulchers, grinders and chippers. It fabricates steel structures and cabs in-house and makes its own axles, transmissions and gearboxes. It reports 2,000 employees, twelve southern Ontario locations, and machines in over 40 countries.

TS Tech Canada Inc. makes automobile seats at 17855 Leslie Street in Newmarket, Ontario, and has operated there since 1996. Its Ontario air-emissions approval covers welding, seat assembly and laboratory analysis, with a permitted production limit of up to 1,500,000 seat frames per year. Trade press has reported that it supplies seats for the Honda Civic and CR-V assembled at Honda's Alliston plant. The company belongs to the TS Tech group, whose parent is TS Tech Co., Ltd. of Japan.

The University of Ottawa describes itself as among the top five Canadian universities for research intensity and as the largest English-French bilingual university in the world. It operates from its main campus in Ottawa and a Kanata North campus in Canada's largest technology park. It publishes research strengths relevant to defence, security and aerospace, including quantum technologies, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, semiconductors, secure communications and energetic materials. It offers industry access to shared facilities such as the NanoFab cleanroom facility, the uOttawa-IBM Cyber Range and its core facilities, and it supports commercialization through Innovation Support Services.

The association was founded in 2003 and represents entrepreneurs, businesses, students, academia, industry and government working in remotely piloted aircraft systems. It was rebranded from Unmanned Systems Canada / Systèmes Télécommandés Canada to Aerial Evolution Association of Canada. It organizes an annual national conference and exhibition, a national student UAS competition, the Flight Safety Action Team and its National RPAS Safety Management System, webinars and scholarships. It does not manufacture products and publishes no equipment, certifications or customer list.

Untether AI was founded in Toronto in 2018 and designed at-memory compute AI inference chips (runAI200, speedAI240), tsunAImi and speedAI accelerator cards, and the imAIgine software development kit. On June 6, 2025 it announced a transaction with AMD under which it stopped supplying or supporting its speedAI products and imAIgine SDK, and its engineering team went to AMD. On October 15, 2025 it filed an assignment in bankruptcy, and PricewaterhouseCoopers Inc. was appointed trustee. The company website is still online but the company no longer sells or supports its products.

Vale Canada Sudbury Operations has five underground mines and one open-pit mine, plus the Clarabelle Mill, the Copper Cliff Smelter Complex and the Copper Cliff Nickel Refinery. The refinery makes high-purity nickel pellets and powders, and the mill produces a copper concentrate that is rich in platinum group metals. The operation is part of Vale Base Metals and the legal entity is Vale Canada Limited. The organization says it employs more than 4,000 people directly in Sudbury.

The Port Colborne Refinery is an operation of Vale Canada Limited (Vale Base Metals) on Lake Erie, started in 1918. It has three production areas: a cobalt refinery, a precious metals refinery and nickel processing. Cobalt and precious metals feed come from Vale's Sudbury-area operations, and the precious metals refinery also handles toll materials from third parties. The site employs about 200 people according to Vale Base Metals' current operations page.

Ventra Group Co. is a Nova Scotia unlimited liability company licensed in Ontario, with its Ontario registered office in Windsor. With its Canadian affiliates, it designs, manufactures, sells and services stamped, welded, hydroformed, injection-moulded and painted components for passenger vehicles and light trucks, and says it is a Tier 1 supplier to automakers. It operates plants under the Ventra Plastics and Flex-N-Gate names in Windsor, Tecumseh, Tottenham, Bradford and Peterborough, plus the Flex-Ion Battery Innovation Centre in Windsor. The Canadian affiliate group reports more than 4,000 associates at 11 production and design facilities in Ontario.

Waabi was founded in 2021 by Raquel Urtasun and is headquartered in Toronto, with teams in San Francisco, Dallas, Phoenix and Pittsburgh. It develops the Waabi Driver, an end-to-end AI driving system, and tests it with Waabi World, a neural simulator, and Mixed Reality Testing on a closed course. The Waabi Driver is integrated into the Volvo VNL Autonomous truck, and customer freight operations began on the Dallas–Houston corridor in October 2026. In January 2026 Waabi announced a Series C round and a robotaxi partnership with Uber.

Wescast Industries Inc. is an automotive Tier 1 supplier of cast iron and stainless steel exhaust manifolds, turbocharger housings and integrated turbo-manifolds for passenger cars and light trucks. Its website lists casting and machining facilities in Ontario, Michigan, Hungary and China, and a Technical Development Centre for design, prototyping and testing. The company has been a wholly-owned subsidiary of China-based Sichuan Bohong Industry Co. Ltd. since 2013. Trade press and union statements report that the Wingham, Ontario foundry ceased operations in July 2023.

Western University was founded in 1878 and operates a main campus at 1151 Richmond Street in London, Ontario. It runs core research facilities used by industry and other researchers, including the WindEEE Dome wind-testing chamber, the Fraunhofer Innovation Platform for Composites Research and the ISO/IEC 17025-accredited Surface Science Western laboratory. Western Research Parks hosts industry tenants next to these facilities. In 2026 the university signed agreements on defence and dual-use research with TKMS and Dalhousie University.

Windsor Mold Group, operating as WMG Technologies, has two divisions: Tooling Solutions, which builds complex injection moulds, and Molded Products, which runs medium- to large-tonnage injection moulding. It has sites in Ontario, the United States and Mexico, and says it has operated since 1972. ABC Technologies Holdings Inc. completed its acquisition of the group in March 2023.

22 Wing is at Canadian Forces Base North Bay, Ontario, under the operational command of 1 Canadian Air Division. It hosts the Canadian Air Defence Sector, which monitors air traffic approaching North America in support of NORAD, and the Sector Air Operations Centre. 21 Aerospace Control and Warning Squadron staffs the operations floor and the Sensor System Operations Centre, while 51 Squadron trains wing personnel. United States Air Force members of Detachment 2, First Air Force, are co-located at the wing.
operating_name: 22 Wing North Bay / CFB North Bay

abstract_en: 8 Wing is located at CFB Trenton and is under the operational command of 1 Canadian Air Division. The Wing Commander is also the base commander and is responsible for base administrative, operational and logistical support. The wing's squadrons fly CC-130J Hercules, CC-177 Globemaster III, CC-150 Polaris and CH-146 Griffon aircraft. The base hosts lodger units including the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre Trenton and the Canadian Army Advanced Warfare Centre. An $850 million infrastructure program is underway to prepare the base for the CC-330 Husky tanker transport fleet.

A-Line Precision Tool Ltd. operates from a single free-standing plant at 155 Sun Pac Boulevard in Brampton, Ontario, under the trade name A-Line Aerospace. It publishes 4- and 5-axis CNC milling, CNC turning, wire EDM, waterjet cutting, CNC sheet metal bending, assembly and in-house quality inspection. A sister company, A-Line Processing Inc., shares the site and offers non-destructive testing, chemical processing and coating. A-Line Precision publishes AS9100D / ISO 9001:2015 registration and a Controlled Goods Program registration.

A.T.G. Industries Inc. operates from a 25,000 sq. ft. facility at 760 Industrielle Street in Rockland, Ontario. It machines customer-designed parts using 3-, 4- and 5-axis CNC milling and Swiss-type turning, and verifies them by CMM inspection. In-house finishing includes chemical films, anodizing, passivation, liquid painting and electrostatic powder coating. The company publishes AS9100D, ISO 9001:2015, Nadcap (chemical processing) and Controlled Goods Program certificates for aerospace and other industries.

ABS Machining Inc. says it was established in 1971 and offers large and production CNC machining, heavy fabrication, robotic and specialty welding including Inconel cladding, and complex mechanical assemblies. It reports six plants, more than 50 overhead cranes with lift capacities up to 160 tons, and a large fleet of boring mills and vertical turning lathes. It serves original equipment manufacturers in the energy, mining, steel, locomotive, pulp and paper, and power transmission industries. It also states that it is ISO 9001:2015 certified and N299.3 certified.

Accumetal Manufacturing Inc. was started in 2002 when it bought the assets of a Stratford metal fabricator, and it now operates a 60,000 sq ft plant on two shifts with over 80 employees. It cuts, forms, machines, welds (manual and robotic), paints and assembles components such as ladders, platforms, battery boxes, handrails, sandboxes and cab and undercarriage parts. It states that it is ISO 9001:2015 registered, CWB certified and registered with the Controlled Goods Program, and it serves defence OEMs, military fire training contractors, mining and rail OEMs and a recycling equipment maker. In March 2025 FedDev Ontario announced support of $1,557,430 for the company's production scale-up.

Acentury Inc. was founded in 2011 and is headquartered in Richmond Hill, Ontario. It sells software that automates wireless network testing and deployment, and Radiocomm hardware (passive RF components, RF jumper cables, cryogenic cables and fibre cables) to mobile network operators, network equipment vendors and cable operators. Its subsidiary SynMatrix Technologies develops RF filter design software that integrates with Ansys HFSS. The company says its RF work supports both defence and civilian applications and it has attended CANSEC and Eurosatory, but it names no defence customers.

ACF Associates Inc., founded in 2006, provides performance management, data processing and analysis, visualization and application development, modelling and simulation, and in-service support program services. Its stated customers include the Department of National Defence, the Royal Canadian Air Force, Boeing and several Canadian aerospace firms. It markets an Integrated Performance-Based Management System (IPBMS). It operates as a virtual workplace with staff working remotely across Canada, and is owned by The Loomex Group.

AECOM Canada ULC serves transportation, water, buildings, energy, environmental, industrial and government clients from offices across Canada. It publishes that it employs about 3,500 professionals in 28 offices and that its Canadian legacy began in 1911. In May 2026 it announced the top-ranked position on Defence Construction Canada's National Architecture & Engineering Source List, supporting Department of National Defence infrastructure. It also operates geotechnical materials-testing laboratories in Calgary, Toronto and Winnipeg.

Arcfield Canada Corp. is headquartered in Calgary, Alberta, and describes itself as Canada's only prime contractor for fighter platform avionics sustainment. It holds the Department of National Defence CF-18 avionics in-service support contract (up to $211.6 million CAD over a firm five-year period announced in March 2024). It also manages CF-18 supply chain operations through warehouses at Cold Lake, Alberta, and La Baie (Bagotville), Quebec. It is an affiliate of the U.S. defence services firm Arcfield and has a business development office in Ottawa.

Bempro Global Group Inc. has operated since 1984 from 18 Chelsea Lane, Brampton, Ontario, and is the parent of three operating companies. BMP Metals is the manufacturing arm, with laser and punch cutting, press brake forming, CWB-certified welding, CNC machining, conveyor paint lines, 3D plastic printing and mechanical and electrical assembly. CableTalk Systems designs and distributes communication enclosures, and ClimateWorx International designs and builds precision air conditioning units. BMP Metals states that it supplies telecommunications, medical, transportation, energy and military and naval customers, among others.

Brannon Steel is a family-owned Brampton, Ontario company founded in 1968 that processes carbon steel plate and structural sections into parts to customer print. It operates plasma, oxy-fuel and laser cutting, beveling, press brake forming, plate and structural rolling, flattening, light machining and finishing across three buildings totalling over 200,000 sq. ft. It supplies construction, forestry, mining, rail, energy and other equipment makers and fabricators across North America, and its site lists defence among the industries served. It publishes an ISO 9001 certificate and states ISO 14001 registration.

CFB Kingston is a Canadian Armed Forces base in Kingston, Ontario. Its stated mission is to provide support services to 46 lodger units so they can focus on their primary missions. It supports training schools and institutions, including the Royal Military College of Canada, the Canadian Forces School of Military Intelligence and the Canadian Forces School of Communications and Electronics. It also hosts operational and support units such as 21 Electronic Warfare Regiment, 1 Wing Kingston and the Canadian Forces Crypto Maintenance Unit. It is a government installation and does not manufacture products.
operating_name: Canadian Forces Base Kingston (incl. Schools of Communications and Electronics and Military Intelligence)

abstract_en: DAVWIRE was founded in 2003 and operates from a 40,000 square foot facility at 1180 Wilton Grove Road in London, Ontario. It does build-to-print production of cable assemblies, wire harnesses, electrical wiring interconnection systems and box builds, backed by in-house engineering, a quality assurance testing laboratory and a research laboratory for high-voltage polymers. It holds AS9100 D / ISO 9001:2015 registration and supplies De Havilland Aircraft of Canada programs and Canada's Department of National Defence.

The Toronto Research Centre (TRC) is DRDC's centre for human-centric science and technology in the defence and security environment. It researches warfighter and system effectiveness, warfighter performance and health, and operations in the information environment for the Canadian Armed Forces. It shares a site with the Canadian Forces Environmental Medicine Establishment (CFEME), and the two have experimentation facilities that include environmental, diving and hypobaric chambers, a human bio-analysis lab and a human-rated centrifuge. DRDC partners with industry, academia, other departments and allies through collaborative research and funding programs.
operating_name: Defence Research and Development Canada – Toronto Research Centre

abstract_en: DEFSEC Technologies Inc. (formerly KWESST Micro Systems Inc.) is headquartered in Kanata North, Ottawa. It develops Team Awareness Kit (TAK)-integrated systems for the dismounted soldier, including the Tactical Digital Fires System, the BLISS laser sensor and the Phantom electromagnetic-spectrum system. For public safety it offers the cloud-hosted Lightning situational awareness platform and the ARWEN and PARA SHOT less-lethal product lines. It also performs software engineering work for the Canadian Department of National Defence as a subcontractor.

Emergent Solutions Inc. develops AIoT edge-compute and communications hardware and software for remote and harsh environments. Its published products are the EGU1000 edge compute platform, the EBR100 multi-radio UHF broadband platform and the CMS-iO central management system. It lists oil and gas, mining, electric and water utilities, smart agriculture, telecom, and defence and public safety as target markets. A Markham economic development article describes the systems as developed for both civilian and defence customers.

Ensil Inc. operates from Markham, Ontario, and works with an affiliate, Ensil Technical Services Inc., in Niagara Falls, New York. It repairs circuit boards at component level, reverse engineers obsolete assemblies, and supports prototype and low-volume electronics manufacturing. Its published defence work includes radar, radio, power-supply and RF assemblies. The company lists ISO 9001:2015, Controlled Goods, ITAR and JCP credentials and the CAGE codes L1679 (Canada) and 52GG4 (United States).
loc_city_list: Niagara Falls, New York, United States

abstract_en: FBT Inc. was founded in 1945 as F-B Tool & Die Limited and became FBT Inc. in 2009. It machines and grinds precision components from hard-to-machine materials such as Inconel, titanium, stainless steel, carbide and ceramic. It also designs and builds progressive, draw, compound and forming dies and runs metal stamping presses up to 275 tons. The company states it is certified to ISO 9001:2015 and publishes a Controlled Goods certificate, and it received a FedDev Ontario contribution in 2023 for advanced manufacturing equipment.

FedNor is a federal agency headquartered in Sudbury, Ontario. It began as a branch of Industry Canada in 1987 and became a standalone agency in August 2021. It delivers the Northern Ontario Development Program, Regional Economic Growth through Innovation, the Community Futures Program, the Economic Development Initiative, the Regional Tariff Response Initiative and the Regional Defence Investment Initiative. It makes no products. Its output is funding, program delivery and advice to Northern Ontario firms and organizations.
operating_name: Federal Economic Development Agency for Northern Ontario (FedNor)

abstract_en: Formic AI Ltd. was founded in 2021 and is headquartered in Toronto. It develops the Formic Engine and the Boreal Governance Layer, which retrieve answers from a customer's documents using a knowledge graph rather than generative inference. Deployment can be in the cloud, on a local network or on-premises. The company states that its users include federal regulators, defence bodies, law firms and technology platform partners, and it reports three patent applications covering the underlying methods.

4th Canadian Division Support Base Petawawa, commonly called Garrison Petawawa, supports the units located on the base. These include 2 Canadian Mechanized Brigade Group, the Canadian Special Operations Regiment, 1 Canadian Field Hospital and two aviation squadrons. It falls under the 4th Canadian Division Support Group, which delivers personnel, operations, technical, engineering, signals, corporate, environment and safety services. It manages ranges and training areas and is a government operation, not a manufacturer.
operating_name: Garrison Petawawa (4th Canadian Division Support Base Petawawa)

abstract_en: Hepburn Engineering Inc. designs and supplies hoists, winches, drives, controls and software for mines, and underway replenishment-at-sea stations and receiving-ship equipment for navies. It provides repair, upgrade, spare parts, installation and training for both lines. It has supplied the Royal Canadian Navy's Joint Support Ships through Seaspan Shipyards and the Republic of Korea Navy's AOE-II vessels through Hanwha Ocean.

HFI Pyrotechnics Inc. (formerly Hands Fireworks) traces its origins to 1873 and now focuses exclusively on specialty pyrotechnics for defence and security customers. Its products include marine location markers, smoke grenades and markers, simulated projectile and grenade training devices, and related signalling items. The company says it is a strategic source and centre of excellence for pyrotechnics under Canada's Munitions Supply Program. It operates a licensed production and test site in Edwardsburgh Cardinal Township, Ontario, and announced a $120 million expansion of that site in July 2026.

Horstman Canada Inc. was formed in 2023 by amalgamating General Kinetics Engineering Corporation (acquired by the RENK Group) with Horstman Systems Inc. It makes suspension dampers, Hydrostruts and semi-active damping and ride height systems, and offers vehicle modelling and simulation. Its products are fitted to programs such as Stryker, Bradley and FMTV. It is the Canadian business unit of the Horstman Group, which also has units in the UK and the US.

Hybrid Power Solutions Inc. was founded in 2015 and sells fuel-free portable power packs (Batt Pack series), the Spark Cube, and the TERRA 166 kVA mobile battery microgrid, along with custom battery and energy storage systems. It is listed on the Canadian Securities Exchange as HPSS. The company reports defence-related activity, including a Canadian defence distribution partnership, an order for U.S. Air Force drone support through a U.S. distributor, and a European defence purchase order. It also received up to $2.25 million in federal funding (FedDev Ontario) for manufacturing capacity at its Etobicoke facility.

IMP Aerospace & Defence is a business unit of IMP Group Limited, headquartered in Enfield, Nova Scotia. Its Trenton, Ontario site is a maintenance and modification facility on CFB Trenton. The company says that site does periodic maintenance, restores stored aircraft to service and installs the avionics upgrade on the RCAF Snowbirds' CT-114 Tutor fleet. It also supports the CC-130J Hercules there, and the CH-149 Cormorant helicopter returns to Trenton under the Cormorant Mid-Life Upgrade. The wider group offers fleet management, aircraft maintenance, overhaul and modification, engineering under its own design approval, and manufacturing of aerostructures and wire harnesses.

ITPS (Canada) Ltd. operates the International Test Pilots School (ITPS) in London, Ontario, and the International Tactical Training Centre (ITTC) in North Bay, Ontario. The school was established in the U.K. in 1986 and has operated in Canada since 2001. It runs fixed and rotary wing test pilot and flight test engineer courses, uncrewed aircraft system test courses, and Master of Science programs approved by the Ontario Ministry of Colleges and Universities. It operates a fleet of about 30 aircraft, including L-39, L-29 and Hawker Hunter jets and helicopters, and offers flight test consulting. It reports a new engineering division for maintenance, repair and overhaul, in-house L-39 avionics upgrades, and a variable stability aircraft called ACE. Customers include the Royal Canadian Air Force and allied air forces, usually contracted through the Canadian Commercial Corporation.
operating_name: International Test Pilots School Canada (ITPS Canada)

abstract_en: IPG Photonics (Canada) Inc. is the Kingston, Ontario subsidiary of IPG Photonics Corporation, formed when Laser Depth Dynamics was acquired in December 2017. It develops and manufactures the LDD line of weld monitors, which use Inline Coherent Imaging to measure weld penetration depth and weld geometry as the weld is made. The company says the products are designed and built in-house and are used mainly in automotive and e-mobility laser welding. The Kingston group is IPG's centre for weld process monitoring.

J-Squared Technologies Inc. was incorporated in January 1990 and is headquartered in Kanata, Ontario. It designs rugged embedded computing hardware for military, mining, rail, energy and edge AI uses, and distributes third-party electronics. Its services include maintenance, repair and overhaul, in-service support, product lifecycle management, and testing through its ESL Labs unit in Dartmouth, Nova Scotia. In May 2026 it opened a 26,000 sq. ft. Kanata facility with a large-format nuclear EMP test capability and secure storage.

JPOM was founded in 2007 and describes itself as an independent technical, lobby and business consultancy. Its services cover proposal planning and authoring, capture strategy, contract award support, offset planning, government relations, partnership building, mergers and acquisitions, and navigation of public funding channels. Its team is spread across Canada, with advisors in the United States, Europe, Africa and the Middle East. It makes no physical products and publishes no equipment or facility lists.

Metex Heat Treating Ltd. processes customer-supplied metal parts in Brampton, Ontario, using continuous and batch furnaces, induction hardening cells and nitriding equipment. It states that it runs 24 hours a day, seven days a week, and has an on-site metallurgy team and an ISO/IEC 17025 accredited laboratory. The company states that it is certified to IATF 16949, and its published work is aimed mainly at automotive customers. It also states AMS 2759 capability and acquired Exactatherm Ltd, an aerospace and tool steel heat treater, in 2024.

North Simcoe Tool & Manufacturing was established in 1973 and operates from 381 William St in Midland, Ontario. It specializes in fixtures, gauges, prototyping, production tooling and small-run production machining. It states that its customers are in the automotive, aircraft, defence, aerospace, medical and food products industries. It publishes an ISO 9001:2015 surveillance audit result (June 2022) and a Controlled Goods Program registration notice (December 2016).

Northwest Protection Services Ltd. is a Toronto security company that says it has operated for over 30 years. It supplies licensed guards for events, retail, condominiums, film studios and construction sites, and it runs remote monitoring and CCTV services. It is expanding into cybersecurity by offering threat-exposure, data-protection and secure-transfer products from its partner Autnhive. It also operates a security guard licence training academy and a gig-based guard staffing and payroll platform.

Nuformex Inc. was spun off from the manufacturing division of Transformix Engineering Inc. and operates from 1150 Gardiners Road in Kingston, Ontario. It offers turning, milling, grinding, CMM inspection, drafting and CAD/CAM programming, with build-to-print and reverse-engineering work and production runs of 1 to 1000 parts. It publishes a tolerance of +/-0.0005 inch and offers inventory stock arrangements. It serves advanced manufacturing, energy, life sciences, consumer goods and other sectors, and is listed by Invest Kingston among defence and security suppliers.

Paradigm Shift Technologies Inc. was founded in 1995 and has its head office and coating facility in Toronto, Ontario. It develops and applies its proprietary Electro-magnetically enhanced Physical Vapor Deposition (EPVD®) process to bores from 5 mm to 500 mm in diameter. Its work centres on weapon-system barrels and aircraft components, and it also supplies CoatAlloy™ coatings for petrochemical furnace tubes. It works through research and development, engineering and equipment-construction projects, and licenses coating procedures to clients as technical data packages.

Pylon Electronics Inc. calibrates and repairs test and measurement instruments for aerospace, military, automotive, telecommunications and manufacturing customers. Its calibration labs are in British Columbia, Alberta, Ontario and Nova Scotia, with a technical sales office in Quebec. It also runs an Instrument Manufacturing Division in Ottawa that makes radon and thoron monitors, detectors and sources. It holds a Department of National Defence calibration contract and says it is registered in the Controlled Goods Program.

Qoherent develops machine learning applications for software-defined radio, which it calls radio inference applications. Its products include the RIA Toolkit, RIA Hub and RIA RAN. Its services include RF machine learning prototypes, custom RF datasets, open-source 5G network testing and deployment, and SDR support and testbed development. It states that its work has supported space agencies and defence research organizations, and that it has delivered projects co-funded by the European Space Agency and supported by the Canadian Space Agency.

The Naval Handling business of Rolls-Royce Canada Limited operated a Centre of Excellence in Peterborough, Ontario that designs and builds launch-and-recovery systems, sonar towing and handling systems and winches. Its Mission Bay Handling System is supplied to Canada's River-class destroyer, the UK Type 26 and the Australian Hunter-class programs. Rolls-Royce completed the sale of its Naval Propulsors business to Fairbanks Morse Defense in July 2025, and the sale of the Naval Handling business to the same buyer was reported as closed in July 2026.

Scentroid has operated since 2007 and says it ships to more than 45 countries. Its catalogue covers olfactometers, chemical analyzers with 60+ sensor options, sampling equipment, drone and vehicle-based monitors, and the SIMS3 software platform. It also provides environmental consulting, equipment rentals and odour training. A Scentroid Defence division, launched on its site in 2026, offers CBRNE detection products (TR9+ Sentry, TR10 Warden, GV2000 quadrupedal robot) and AI sensor-fusion platforms. The company states that it holds ISO 9001:2015 certification.

Sphyrna Security was founded in 2000 by Alan Magar. It began as a professional services firm for the Government of Canada and became a cybersecurity vendor. Its NGXS unidirectional gateways, adaptive gateway and data diodes are designed in-house at Sphyrna Labs and manufactured in Canada. Its Verity GRC software supports a managed governance, risk and compliance service. It serves government, defence and intelligence, nuclear energy, utilities and data centre customers.

Teledyne DALSA is a subsidiary of Teledyne Technologies Incorporated, headquartered in Waterloo, Ontario, with a MEMS and semiconductor foundry in Bromont, Quebec and R&D in Montreal. It states that it was established in 1980 and has about 1,000 employees worldwide. It sells imaging components and systems into machine vision, medical, aerospace, defence and security, scientific and transportation markets, and offers custom detector and MEMS development. It describes its defence technology as ITAR-free and subject to Canadian export controls.

The organization delivers provincially funded Ontario Small Business Advisory Centre programs, including free consultations, Starter Company Plus and Summer Company. It also delivers Succession Ontario, the local Foodpreneur Advantage seminars and, since 2026, the Northern Ontario Defence Opportunities program, which funds Northern Ontario SMEs preparing to enter the defence supply chain. It is part of the Small Business Centres Ontario network and does not make products.
operating_name: The Business Centre Nipissing Parry Sound

abstract_en: The Lake Superior Scottish Regiment (LSSR) is a Primary Reserve infantry unit in Thunder Bay, Ontario, and part of 38 Canadian Brigade Group. Its stated task is to augment Canada's military with trained infantry soldiers. It is a military unit, not a commercial supplier. It publishes no manufacturing, product or certification information, only its role, training schedule, trades and issued weapons and vehicles.

Thunder Bay Aviation Ltd. was incorporated in March 1987 and focused on the DHC-6 Twin Otter from 1989. It states that it holds STC, PDA and PMA approvals for over 300 parts and stocks over 500 line items of Twin Otter replacement parts. It is a Transport Canada approved maintenance organization with manufacturing, maintenance and distribution approvals, and it states EASA Part-145 maintenance. Its products include control cables, door handles, fuel caps, seats, cabin interiors, tools and ground power units.

Tron Motors Inc. is a Canadian systems engineering company that combines sensing (radar, optical, RF), edge intelligence, precision motion, propulsion and power electronics. Its flagship Counter-UAS platform, including the Northern Dome high power laser concept, is stated to be in development, with validation activity at Area X.O in Ottawa. It also offers custom BLDC motor and inverter design, gimbals and turrets, and robotics and edge-AI engineering. The company's own pages label each offering as in development, integration capability or available capability.

Turris Communications Ltd. provided two-way radio, SCADA monitoring, fleet management communications and emergency services infrastructure through 12 service centres across Canada. BearCom Group, Inc. acquired the company in September 2018, and the tower sites and other Turris Group entities were excluded from the sale. An Alberta registry index lists the Turris entity as amalgamated into BearCom Canada Corp. The company's own website named an Ottawa head office, and a federal contract record shows a Department of National Defence award.

Visual Defence Inc. is a Richmond Hill, Ontario software and systems integration company. Its current flagship, CITYROVER, is a smartphone- and camera-based AI application that detects road deficiencies for municipalities.
