The company also publishes a physical security product line: the 3C command and control (PSIM) software, video management and storage software, the SecurEye blast-resistant camera and the DMS door access software. Its project logos include airports, transit agencies, universities and national security bodies, and it has one Department of National Defence contract on record.
loc_city_list: New York City, New York, United States
Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia; Abidjan, Ivory Coast; Istanbul, Turkey; Hanoi, Vietnam; Mumbai and Ahmedabad, India

abstract_en: The Peterborough plant was acquired by Woodward, Inc. from Safran Electronics & Defense in July 2025 and is Woodward's only Canadian facility. It produces specialized electromechanical systems for aviation, and Ontario's air-emissions approval describes it as an aircraft control board manufacturing facility. Woodward announced in July 2026 that it will move production to Krakow, Poland, and engineering support to Krakow and Sofia, Bulgaria, ending operations in Peterborough by August 31, 2027. About 165 employees are affected.
operating_name: Woodward Inc. – Peterborough facility (former Safran Electronics & Defense Canada site)

abstract_en: Founded in 1986 as an aerospace and defence research and development firm, A.U.G. Signals Ltd. works in target detection, classification and tracking, image registration, sensor fusion and change detection. It sells TRITON Intelligent Water Surveillance, AirSENCE air monitors and radar-based traffic and animal detection systems. It also does remote sensing and AI-based crop analytics, and has held Canadian defence research contracts. It publishes an ISO 9001:2015 certification for its water monitoring systems and is listed in the Controlled Goods Program registry.

Accipiter Radar Technologies Inc. develops avian, drone-detection (C-UAS), beyond visual line of sight detect-and-avoid and maritime domain awareness radar systems, together with its Radar Intelligence Network software platform. It sells to airports, military airfields, ports, energy producers, law enforcement and border agencies, and also offers subscription surveillance services, installation, training and technical support. The company says it began in 1994 and has an operating office in Orchard Park, New York. Its Canadian entity holds a Controlled Goods Program registration.
loc_city_list: Orchard Park, New York, United States

abstract_en: AirShare, Inc. is an Ottawa-based Canadian corporation that designs and makes counter-uncrewed-aircraft interceptor missiles and the launch and command systems that go with them. The interceptors deploy a countermeasure cloud that entangles drone propellers, and the missile bodies can be 3D printed. The company publishes its products as launcher systems and command and control elements. It reports a contract with Canadian special forces and has a U.S. regional entity, AirShare Systems, Inc.

Allient London (formerly FPH Group Inc.) is the structural and lightweighting composites Technology Unit of Allient Inc., which acquired FPH in 2022. The London plant offers engineering, rapid prototyping, composite mould design and build, waterjet cutting, painting and production of composite, electrical, hydraulic and mechanical subassemblies for defence OEMs. It also offers electric direct drive motors, wire harnesses and battery management systems for military vehicle electrification. FPH Group Inc. is listed in the Controlled Goods Program registry.

Alps Welding Limited has operated since 1974 from a 90,000-square-foot fabrication facility at 400 New Huntington Road in Woodbridge (Vaughan), Ontario. It builds pressure vessels, heat exchangers, tanks, stacks and modular skid packages for engineering, procurement and construction firms (EPCs), equipment designers and end users in oil and gas, power generation, water treatment, chemical, steel and mining. It holds ASME Section VIII "U" and National Board "R" authorizations, TSSA authorizations, CWB W47.1 certification and ISO 9001:2015 registration, and offers mechanical design support for the equipment it fabricates.

Anvil Intelligence Inc., operating as ANVIL, develops a data-fusion and knowledge management platform that ingests multi-source data, enriches it with AI and exposes it through mission applications. It reports deployments with Canadian defence and security organizations and interoperability testing with NATO allies and Ukraine. It is headquartered in Ottawa's ByWard Market and describes itself as 100% Canadian-owned.

Arctic Horizons Inc. develops three unmanned aircraft platforms: Piglet (Class 3 tilt-rotor), Peregrine (Class 2 loitering system deployed from containers) and Stictia (nano class). It also develops ground-control, fleet-awareness and ballistics-solver software. The company was incorporated federally in 2020 and is headquartered in Ottawa, with a Norwegian presence at Hønefoss. In 2024 it announced a $2.1 million Piglet trial contract with a law enforcement agency through Innovative Solutions Canada.

CAE Defence & Security Canada is run from a regional office at 350 Legget Drive in Ottawa (Kanata) and is part of CAE Inc., which is headquartered in Saint-Laurent, Quebec. It describes itself as a training systems integrator. Its work covers training centres and services, simulation products, systems engineering and integration, and mission and operations support across air, land, maritime, space and cyber domains. Published Canadian programs include NATO Flying Training in Canada, the Future Aircrew Training program (through the SkyAlyne joint venture), the Remotely Piloted Aircraft System program, and CF-18 and CH-148 Cyclone support.

Founded in 2015 by leaders from large Canadian corporations, the Canadian Cyber Threat Exchange (CCTX) provides members with threat feeds, intelligence reports, threat calls, symposiums and a peer network. Membership is open to organizations incorporated in Canada across all sectors and sizes, and is priced in tiers. CCTX also leads the Ontario Cybersecurity Excellence Initiative with Rogers Cybersecure Catalyst and runs the Canadian Anti-Scam Coalition.

CFB Borden opened in 1916 as Camp Borden and now trains an average of 20,000 military personnel a year. The base is home to the Military Personnel Generation Training Group and its schools, including logistics, fire and CBRN, chaplain and training development centres, as well as lodger units such as the RCEME School, the RCAF Academy and 400 Tactical Helicopter Squadron. It publishes a Business Development Office route through which other governments and the public may request access to some training programs and physical assets. It does not manufacture products or sell to industry.
operating_name: Canadian Forces Base Borden (Department of National Defence)

abstract_en: Convergence Design Services, formerly Blue Systems, says it has been designing products since 1990. It embeds engineers in client programs from concept through verification, validation and production support, designing to MIL-STD, DO-160, DO-254 and space standards. It operates an EMI/EMC chamber, an anechoic chamber, environmental chambers and 3D scanning and printing equipment at its Arnprior site, which it describes as a Controlled Goods Program site. In 2026 it launched its own products, the MIL-V crewed and uncrewed ground platform and the Arctic OWL Edge-AI sensing family, and announced $5 million in backing from Lordon Mayo Corporation.

CounterCrisis Tech develops and hosts IC4W, a real-time incident command platform built on the Microsoft stack with Esri ArcGIS integration. It also offers an IMS/ICS technology gap analysis, technology advisory services and a fixed-scope implementation program called IC4W Rapid Launch. It is the developer of the Ground Search and Rescue Incident Command System (GSAR ICS) funded by Public Safety Canada, and it has delivered an event coordination system for the Canadian Red Cross. Its published customers and use cases are mainly emergency management, search and rescue, and public safety, with national defence and border security listed as additional use cases.

CryptoMill Cybersecurity Solutions, a Toronto-based Canadian company, develops encryption software that protects data at rest, in use and when shared. Its products include Circles of Trust, Blaze, Vanishh (self-destructing email) and SEAhawk (full-disk and removable-media encryption). It names defence and government among its target users, holds patents assigned to CryptoMill Inc., and appears in federal contract disclosures with National Defence, Shared Services Canada and Statistics Canada.

Dominion Dynamics was founded in 2025 and is headquartered in Kanata, Ontario. It builds AuraNet, a software platform that fuses sensor, signals and reporting data into a common operating picture. AuraNet was fielded with the Canadian Rangers during Operation NANOOK-NUNALIVUT. The company is also developing Dominion Scout, an uncrewed aircraft meant to fly alongside crewed fighters, and AuraSim, a simulation environment for testing autonomy. It operates a 25,000-square-foot manufacturing facility in Kanata and has qualified as a supplier in four streams of the Defence Drone Initiative Marketplace.

Field Effect Software Inc. is headquartered in Ottawa, Ontario. It builds its own managed detection and response (MDR) platform covering endpoints, networks, cloud and AI use, and backs it with a 24/7 security operations centre. It also provides incident response, incident response readiness and cybersecurity assessment services, and a simulation-based Cyber Range training platform. It sells directly and through MSP and VAR channel partners to small and medium-sized organizations in Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom and Australia.

GameStrat Inc. is an Ottawa software company founded in 2015 by University of Ottawa students. Its core product delivers synchronized video clips from several camera angles to coaches' iPads in seconds without relying on cloud servers or WiFi. It sells this to football programs, mostly in the United States, and also to lacrosse teams. A separate tactical offering sends synchronized multi-camera replay to multiple tablets on an offline, closed network for special operations, SWAT, law enforcement and force-on-force training.

GSNetworks says it has supplied custom cable assemblies, harnesses and electromechanical assemblies since 1978. Its products include wire harnesses, ribbon, coax/RF, fibre optic and network cable assemblies, built mainly to customer print. It serves military, aerospace, telecom/satcom/RF, medical, commercial and transportation customers. Artaflex Ottawa Inc. acquired it in December 2022, and the company says it continues to operate as a stand-alone entity.

H2 Analytics Inc. is an Ottawa-based software and professional-services company serving military, national security, law enforcement and humanitarian clients. Its product is the Exercise Architect Suite (EASE), which is used to build and manage intelligence-driven training exercises. It also delivers custom exercise development and delivery, intelligence courseware, C4ISR data integration, mapping and GIS support, and TAK training, server deployment and plugin development. Published sources show work for the Canadian Army, and the company has received federal repayable funding for the next phase of EASE.

International Custom Products Inc., which uses the name ICP and the web address icpdefense.com, has operated since 1985 from a 67,000 sq ft facility at 49 Howden Rd in Toronto. It cuts, stitches, heat-seals and welds engineered textiles, and it offers design, prototyping and production. Its products include parachutes and drogue chutes, harnesses, cargo netting, rifle and ammunition cases, propellant bags, shelters, and logistics bags and holsters. It states ISO 9001:2015 certification and Controlled Goods Program registration. Argyle Capital Partners invested in the company in 2024.

JGW Machine Limited states that it was founded in 1953. It operates from a 100,000 square foot facility in Princeton, Ontario and ships fabricated and machined metal components across North America. Its published services include engineering and design, prototyping, CNC machining, laser cutting, fabrication, welding, metal spinning, powder coating and contract assembly. Its published equipment list includes Okuma machining centres and lathes, a 6 kW Amada fibre laser, Motoman welding robots and a 600-foot powder coat line. The company says it serves transportation and automotive, medical devices, automation and robotics, industrial machinery, energy and agriculture customers, and it lists military among its machining markets.

Kelluu Canada Ltd. is the Canadian subsidiary of Kelluu, a Finnish company founded in 2018 that builds autonomous, hydrogen-powered, lighter-than-air airships at its own factory in Joensuu, Finland. Kelluu sells the data from the airships as a service rather than selling the airships. The Ottawa office is located at Area X.O and was established in summer 2026. Kelluu says the subsidiary has been named a qualified supplier under Canada's Defence Drone Initiative through to the end of July 2031.

Wescam Inc. operates as L3Harris WESCAM, a division of L3Harris Technologies, and is headquartered in a 330,000-square-foot facility at 50 Leavitt Boulevard in Waterdown, Ontario. The facility houses research and development, engineering, assembly and service for the MX-Series turrets (MX-8 to MX-25 and their designating, land and maritime variants). L3Harris reports MX-Series systems active in over 87 countries on more than 260 platform types. Customers named in published material include the Royal Canadian Air Force (through the Canadian Commercial Corporation), the U.S. Army, Airbus and General Atomics Aeronautical Systems. WESCAM also offers a global maintenance and repair network, field service, and operator training and simulation.

Larus Technologies Corporation, founded in 1995 and based in Ottawa, develops the Total::Insight, Total::Perception, Total::Vision and Total::Foresight software products. These products fuse sensor and other data, run simulations and generate predictive analytics for intelligence, surveillance and maritime domain awareness. Its published customers include the Royal Canadian Navy and the Department of National Defence, and it has also taken on public safety and consumer packaged goods work. The company also provides software engineering consulting, mainly in command, control and intelligence (C4ISR) systems.

Metropolitan Technologies develops decentralized connectivity, IoT/OT cybersecurity and data mesh software, plus a rugged edge gateway, for sensors and other assets in critical infrastructure and battlefield networks. Its three products connect edge devices, protect data with two layers of quantum-safe encryption, and route data peer-to-peer under zero trust access controls. The company is based in Ottawa and was founded in 2022 by Daly Brown and Nick Foubert. CAE has invested in it and partnered with it, and it has reported a pilot with the City of Ottawa and ongoing projects with Thales.

Militex Coatings operates a 100,000 square foot plant in London, Ontario that opened in 1990. It applies liquid and powder coatings, including chemical agent resistant coatings (CARC), after in-house cleaning, blasting and chemical pretreatment, and it also assembles, marks and tests the finished parts. It has supplied armoured vehicle production for General Dynamics Land Systems and serves aerospace, rail, power generation and communications customers.

NP Aerospace is an armour manufacturer and vehicle systems integrator serving defence, law enforcement and security customers. Its Canadian operation in London, Ontario assembles composite armour and integrates vehicles, and it leads the Department of National Defence Land Equipment Program engineering support contract. The Coventry (UK) sites make composite armour and run an ISO/IEC 17025 UKAS-accredited ballistic laboratory with live-fire ranges, and also run the vehicle systems and spares business. In 2026 it acquired Iten Defense of Ashtabula, Ohio, which makes opaque and transparent armour.

Pleora Technologies Inc. is headquartered in Kanata (Ottawa), Ontario and was founded in 2000. It supplies GigE Vision and USB3 Vision hardware, software and professional services to camera makers, system integrators and device designers in industrial automation, medical imaging, and security and defence. Its defence offering includes retrofit frame grabbers and the RuggedCONNECT Smart Video Switcher for vehicle situational awareness. Its ISO 9001:2015 certificate from BSI covers design, manufacture, distribution and support of its products.

Quantropi Inc. was founded in Ottawa in 2018 and develops post-quantum asymmetric and symmetric encryption, quantum random number generation and digital quantum key distribution. Its QiSpace platform has three product families, MASQ, QEEP and SEQUR, and the company also holds patents and publishes research on its own cryptographic methods. It describes its work as dual-use. Published activity includes a quantum-secure link between NATO DIANA sites, a key-distribution solution with Nokia, and distribution of HIMERA tactical radios. Quantropi has announced a merger with Mandeville Ventures that would take it public on the TSX Venture Exchange.

Raytheon Canada Limited is a federally incorporated Canadian subsidiary of Raytheon Company (RTX) that works as a prime contractor to the Department of National Defence. It provides over-the-horizon radar, integrates and sustains naval weapon and sensor systems such as the Phalanx close-in weapon system and the Naval Remote Weapon Stations, and delivers repair, overhaul and logistics support for air, land and sea platforms. It operates facilities in Calgary, Renfrew and Waterloo, with its registered office in Ottawa. It also takes part in the Canadian CATE cyber assessment, training and experimentation centres with the University of Calgary and ENFOCOM.

TACTIQL Inc. is a veteran-founded Canadian defence technology company in Ottawa. Its FULCRUM platform processes full-motion video and metadata from crewed and uncrewed ISR sensors to MISB 0601 and STANAG 4609, and it runs on soldier-portable devices, field servers or the secure cloud. The company reports sales to the Canadian Army, Navy and Joint Forces, partners with Calian and Kongsberg Geospatial, and is in Phase 2 of the NATO DIANA accelerator. It is registered in the Controlled Goods Program.

Uncrewed Systems Inc. is a Kitchener, Ontario firm that sells and integrates RMUS (Utah) Raven and ARMUS drones and the U-Core ground control software from Unmanned Systems Poland. It describes a three-node model: GO-TO AI electronics made in Kraków, platform design by RMUS, and Canadian assembly, adaptation and R&D in Kitchener. It also offers counter-UAS threat assessment and integration advice, and operator training through the RMUS Hub and in-person courses. Its stated clients are defence procurement offices, public safety agencies and critical infrastructure operators.

Volatus Aerospace Inc. (TSX: FLT) is the former Drone Delivery Canada Corp. It supplies tactical ISR and counter-UAS capability, heavy-lift cargo drones, aerial inspection and mapping services, and drone pilot training. It operates a 53,000 sq ft manufacturing and systems integration facility in Mirabel, Québec, and an Operations Control Centre in Vaughan, Ontario. In September 2026 it announced a five-year Government of Canada contract to supply tactical ISR uncrewed aircraft systems to the Canadian Armed Forces. It also reported delivering an initial ISR training drone fleet to an unnamed NATO partner.

Zighra Inc. is an Ottawa-based software company that describes itself as a Canadian defence AI company. Its products are IntentHunter (Counter-UAS intent inference), GenesysInsights (GNSS interference detection), and SilentEdge and DeepSense xAI (continuous behavioural-biometric authentication and identity threat detection). Federal departments have tested its products through Innovative Solutions Canada contracts. These include the Royal Canadian Navy, the Canadian Coast Guard, Shared Services Canada and the Department of National Defence.

Abuma Manufacturing was founded in 1980 and operates from a 100,000-square-foot facility at 531 Admiral Drive, London, Ontario. It fabricates, welds and assembles parts from customer drawings, using laser cutting, waterjet cutting, CNC bending, CNC milling and turning, and robotic welding. It serves defence, nuclear and clean energy, environmental, food and industrial customers. It has been vertically integrated with its sister company Armo Tool Ltd. since 2017.

ADJ Industries Inc. operates two plants in London, Ontario, with more than 150,000 square feet of space, 40-ton overhead cranes and more than 30 CNC machines. It makes components to customer designs, including locomotive traction motor parts, gas turbine housings, mining spindles and parts for light armoured vehicles and marine vessels. It states that it holds ISO 9001:2015 and CWB welding certifications and is registered in the Controlled Goods Program. It also lists a third building in Ashland, Ohio.

Advanced Security Incorporated (ASI) is based in Timmins, Ontario and serves industrial, government and business clients across Northern Ontario. Its published services are industrial security, loss prevention, uniformed guards, private investigations, K-9 services, and in-house security guard training that leads to Ontario licensing. Trade press reports that it was bought in 2012 by Attawapiskat Enterprises Incorporated and is wholly owned by Attawapiskat First Nation. It later acquired All Security Ltd. to add electronic security systems.

AirBoss Defense Group (ADG) was formed in January 2020 by merging AirBoss Defense with Critical Solutions International. It supplies protective equipment and survivability products to military, first responder and healthcare customers. Its main office is in Auburn Hills, Michigan, and its Canadian plant is at Acton Vale, Quebec. It is a division of AirBoss of America Corp., which is headquartered in Newmarket, Ontario.

Arrow Engineered Products launched in 2023 through the merger of VeriForm Inc., Baumeier Corporation and the OEM Metal Fabrication and Engineered Products division of Steelcraft Inc. It offers in-house engineering, cutting, forming, CNC machining, welding, painting and assembly. Its product lines include ASME and ULC storage and pressure equipment, shell-and-tube heat exchangers, autoclaves, and fabricated components for nuclear, industrial, imaging, medical and defence customers. It states a lineage back to 1923 and is a division of Arrow Machine and Fabrication Group of Guelph, Ontario.
operating_name: Arrow Machine and Fabrication Group (Arrow Engineered Products)

abstract_en: Bluink was founded in Ottawa in September 2010 and now sells identity verification, digital ID wallet, mobile driver's licence (ISO 18013-5) issuance, age estimation and password-free login products. Verification uses ID document scans, selfie capture with liveness detection and biometric face matching, with information machine-verified on Canadian servers. Customers named on its site include FCT, Commissionaires, a Toronto-area law firm and the Government of Canada. It also holds federal and provincial research and development funding.

DigitalSecurity1 Inc. is a software development and cybersecurity firm based in Windsor, Ontario. It designs and builds web applications and information systems, and it provides penetration testing, security assessments, SOC and IDS/IPS monitoring, social engineering testing, source code review and malware analysis. It also installs networking, security camera and smart home systems. It publishes its own software products, including the free DS1 Hunter web application security scanner, StockHub inventory software and the upcoming WaitLessHub clinic platform.

Harvan Manufacturing Ltd. operates a 49,000-square-foot plant in Woodstock, Ontario that houses CNC turning and milling, welding and fabrication, laser and waterjet cutting, gear and spline machining, finishing, assembly and inspection. It makes parts to customer drawings for defence, agriculture, industrial valve, and off-road and heavy truck customers. The company publishes ISO 9001:2015 and CWB Division 3 (CSA W47.1) certificates and is listed in the Controlled Goods Program public registry.

INKAS Armored Vehicle Manufacturing was established in Toronto in 2000 and armours vehicles for banks, law enforcement agencies, government bodies, corporate clients and private individuals. It states that its armouring designs are developed in-house, that it cuts and forms steel on Bystronic CNC machines, and that it tests ballistic materials at its own shooting range. It reports a capacity of 40 to 50 vehicles per month and is the armoured vehicle arm of the wider INKAS group. Trade press reports it is adding facilities in Toronto, Charlotte (North Carolina) and Fort Pierce (Florida) in 2026.

Ker-Train Research Inc. (KTR) is a Kingston, Ontario company that does research, development and specialty manufacturing of its own patented gear, clutch and transmission technology. It offers engineering services from concept and simulation through detailed design, prototype machining and dynamometer testing. Its applications cover passenger vehicles, off-highway equipment, military platforms and electric drives, including the Gemini tracked-vehicle transmission. The company says it has 25 full-time employees and a 25,000 sq. ft. facility with a machine shop and testing.

Mattagami Security Solutions is a privately owned security agency based in Timmins, Ontario. It serves the Timmins and Cochrane districts and describes itself as operating across Northern Ontario. Its published services are uniformed guards, mobile patrol, hotel security, loss prevention, industrial and mine security, event security and by-law services. It lists no products, manufacturing capability or certifications.

MREL was established in 1973 and is headquartered in Kingston, Ontario. Its Blasting Instrumentation Division makes VOD and data recorders, high speed cameras and related software for mines, quarries and explosives manufacturers. Its Defence & Security Solutions Division supplies German-made Vallon IED, UXO and mine detectors and USA-made Mithix Pro hook and line kits to military, humanitarian demining, bomb disposal and police users. Sales and after-sales support run through a network of authorized dealers and calibration and repair facilities.

Niagara Precision Limited has machined parts and tooling since 1975 at its facility at 32 Seapark Drive, St. Catharines. It runs 3- and 4-axis machining centres, CNC lathes and grinding equipment, and inspects parts on two coordinate measuring machines. The company reports ISO 9001:2015 registration, N299 nuclear compliance and Controlled Goods Program registration. It also manufactures the Roturner patient transfer aid for Jaide Products Inc., which shares its owner.

OES Inc. has operated from London, Ontario since 1980 and works through three divisions: OES Manufacturing (electronics manufacturing services), OES Scoreboards (LED video displays, scoreboards and accessories) and OES Technologies (wire harness quality assurance devices and crimp force monitors). The electronics manufacturing division builds PCB assemblies, sub-components and box builds, and it publishes its in-house SMT, wave soldering, test, plasma cutting, press brake and CNC equipment. The company holds BSI-issued ISO 9001 and ISO 13485 certificates and is on the Controlled Goods Program registry. It lists 16 patents, most of them on wire quality monitoring and sensing.

Perth Precision is a Canadian-owned contract manufacturer based in Stratford, Ontario. It offers design, laser cutting, CNC machining and turning, grinding, robotic welding, powder painting and assembly as a single package. It says it works with ferrous and non-ferrous metals and plastics, and that CNC machines are used on at least 95% of its parts. It publishes a detailed equipment list and states ISO 9001:2008, Controlled Goods Program and CWB credentials.

Precision Plating operates a 9,000-square-foot plating facility at 35 Oakland Avenue in London, Ontario, and says it was incorporated in 1988. It offers rack, barrel and wire plating in anodizing, black oxide, chemical conversion, gold, nickel, silver, tin and zinc, plus stainless steel passivation. It takes small lots through to continuous production runs and issues certificates of compliance to industrial and MIL specifications. It serves machine shops, fabricators and manufacturers in Ontario and elsewhere in Canada.

Quantum5X Systems Inc., which trades as Q5X, was founded in 2002 and makes small, rugged wireless audio transmitters such as the PlayerMic, Incognito and AquaMic, along with controllers, receivers and IFB products. Its products are used by sports leagues, broadcasters and film and theatre productions. It co-developed Axient Digital-enabled transmitters with Shure and sells through an authorized dealer network. No defence, aerospace or government customers are published.

China Steel Inc. operates two plants in Sault Ste. Marie, Ontario, with CNC and conventional machining, waterjet and plasma cutting, plate forming and welding. It states that it holds ISO 9001:2015 registration, CWB Division II certification and Controlled Goods Program registration. Its stated clients include steel mills, defence contractors, paper mills, mines, engineers, distributors and general contractors. It also states that it manufactures military-grade steel components for the Stryker armoured vehicle.

Economic Development is a division of the City of Sault Ste. Marie, Ontario, and runs the Invest SSM and Welcome to SSM sites from 99 Foster Drive. It promotes the city to investors and workers, and helps firms apply for municipal, provincial and federal funding. It runs the Millworks Centre for Entrepreneurship and publishes a tariff-support resource hub. Its published sector focus includes steel manufacturing and fabrication, a growing defence sector, aviation and aerospace, forestry, clean energy and digital industries.
operating_name: City of Sault Ste. Marie (Economic Development)

abstract_en: Communications & Power Industries Canada Inc. operates from 45 River Drive in Georgetown, Ontario. CPI's Power Electronics: Amplifier Products and Generator Products businesses are headquartered there. Its products include satellite uplink amplifiers and klystrons, a Ka-band extended interaction klystron developed with Canadian Space Agency funding for the SWOT mission, and 32 kW to 100 kW medical X-ray generators. It also provides installation, maintenance agreements, training and spares support. It holds a current ISO 13485:2016 certificate and a Controlled Goods Program registration.

Crypto4A Technologies Inc. is an Ottawa-based cybersecurity company that makes hardware security modules (HSMs) and related key and secrets management appliances. Its QASM cryptographic module is the core of the QxHSM and QxVault products. The company says it designs, develops and manufactures them in Canada. The QASM module holds FIPS 140-3 Level 3 validation under the Cryptographic Module Validation Program (CMVP) (certificate #5497) and supports the NIST post-quantum algorithms. The company lists governments, critical infrastructure and defence networks among the environments its technology protects.

Cyberworks Robotics develops OmniSuite, an autonomous navigation software platform that it licenses to equipment manufacturers and system integrators. It also offers autonomous wheelchairs, floor scrubbers and material-handling tugs, with pilots in airports and a hospital. In 2026 trade press reported a Department of National Defence contract through Innovative Solutions Canada for autonomous vehicles. The company is based at the ventureLAB innovation hub in Markham.

GM Defense Canada was incorporated in 2023 as the Canadian entity of GM Defense, the defence arm of General Motors. In July 2024 it won a C$35.8 million Canadian Armed Forces contract for 90 light tactical vehicles based on the Infantry Squad Vehicle, with an option for 18 more. The National Defence announcement says the vehicles are built by GM Defense LLC in Concord, North Carolina. The entity is also pursuing the Light Utility Vehicle program with a Chevrolet Silverado-based prototype.

IMT Precision is the CNC machining and defence manufacturing division of IMT Group, and it was previously known as IMT Defence and Ingersoll Machining. It operates a 140,000 sq ft plant in Ingersoll, Ontario, and says it has over 200 employees. It makes 25mm to 155mm projectile bodies and vehicle components, and it also does CNC machining, forging, heat treating, welding, finishing and testing. The Government of Canada announced up to $305.4 million for a new 155mm shell facility in March 2026.

Jahn Engineering Ltd. is a tooling and equipment builder in Oldcastle, Ontario. It was founded in 1961 and operates with JE Fixture & Tool, which makes check fixtures. It builds hot stamp, transfer, progressive and warm form dies, robotic weld lines and assembly systems, and machines large components up to 10 m x 3.5 m. It serves automotive and heavy truck customers and has said it is moving into nuclear, aerospace and defence work with federal and provincial tariff-response support.

Sentinel R&D builds the ReKam, a payload-agnostic fixed-wing UAV that can be configured for ISR, loitering strike, electronic warfare or counter-UAS roles. It states that it is moving toward automated composite production using robotic fibre placement and resin infusion. In May 2026 it was named in a Canada–Ukraine arrangement creating the Airlogix-Sentinel joint venture, and in March 2026 it signed a non-binding MOU with Volatus Aerospace on an interceptor UAV.

Sterling Information Technologies Inc. was founded in 1993 as a hardware and services sales company and now works in cybersecurity and operational risk consulting. It offers managed detection and response, virtual CISO and advisory services, and governance, risk and compliance readiness. It also delivers training, including its Cyber Defense+ Certification Program for SOC analysts and workshops with the University of Windsor. It deploys third-party platforms from partners such as Xcitium, Cynet, Cyolo and Cyrisq.

The Loomex Group was founded in 2009 to operate Peterborough Regional Airport. It now manages seven airports and holds safety management system (SMS) and compliance contracts at three more sites. It also delivers emergency management, fire and life safety, evacuation support and training, and construction and infrastructure services. It is the parent company of Explorer Solutions (economic development planning) and ACF Associates (aerospace and defence performance management and in-service support).

Accurate Testing & Finishing Inc. operates a single site at 1630 Trinity Dr., Unit 2, Mississauga. It specializes in the chemical processing of aluminum and the application of organic coatings, including sulphuric acid anodizing, conversion coating, stainless steel passivation and spray painting from decorative to military coatings. The company publishes Nadcap certificates for chemical processing, non-destructive testing and the aerospace quality system (AC7004). It states that most jobs are completed within 5 business days using on-site chemical, liquid penetrant inspection and painting processes.

AG-NAV Inc. was founded in 2000 from the geophysical equipment maker Picodas Group Inc. and is based in Barrie, Ontario. It publishes a product line of aerial and ground DGPS guidance systems, automatic flow and gate controllers, and desktop GIS software for flight planning and reporting. The company states that every product is assembled in Barrie and that it sells through authorized dealers on all six continents. Its published markets are agriculture, forestry, mosquito control, aerial surveying, search and rescue, fire fighting and wildlife tracking.

Air Bravo Corp. was founded in 2001 and operates from bases in Thunder Bay, Sudbury and the Lake Simcoe Regional Airport area near Barrie, Ontario. It flies Pilatus PC-12 and Cessna SkyCourier aircraft for charter, cargo and air ambulance work, including contract work for Ontario's air ambulance system. It also provides line and heavy maintenance, structural repair and inspections for PC-12 and other privately registered aircraft.

Airtech Canada Aviation Services Limited has operated since 1977 at Peterborough Airport in Ontario. It does engineering, design, approvals, manufacture, installation and repair work for fixed-wing and rotary-wing aircraft. Its published work includes aero-medical (EMS) conversions, STC'd 1000 hp engine conversions for the DHC-3 Otter, and special purpose modifications such as survey pods, cargo systems and camera installations. The shop does welding, conventional machining and sheet metal forming.

Virtek Vision International was founded in 1986 as a University of Waterloo spin-off and has its world headquarters in Waterloo, Ontario. It makes laser projectors, vision positioning systems and AI inspection cameras. It also makes the IRIS software platform that guides operators through composite ply layup, welded assembly and truss building. AMETEK acquired the company in October 2024, and it now operates through AMETEK's Creaform business. The company says it has sold more than 25,000 projectors, holds more than 45 U.S. patents and serves customers in more than 55 countries.

Angstrom Engineering was founded in 1992 and says its systems are designed and assembled on-site by its own engineers and technicians. Its product line includes sputtering, evaporation, ion beam, ALD, PLD and LPCVD platforms, cluster tools, glovebox integration, space and environmental simulation chambers and Aeres control software. It also offers custom coating services, sputter targets and evaporation materials, and parts support and materials reclaim. Published customers are mainly universities, research centres and a few companies in quantum, optical coatings, OLED and perovskite work.

AOG Heliservices Inc. operates from Norman Rogers Airport in Kingston, Ontario as a helicopter maintenance, repair and overhaul shop and a Bell Customer Service Facility. It performs component overhaul, line and heavy maintenance, avionics work, paint and refinishing, and aircraft customization for Bell, Airbus, Robinson, Schweizer and MD Helicopters types. It also keeps a parts inventory of more than $1M and runs a rental and exchange program for overhauled main components.

Aztec Nomad Inc. describes itself as the exclusive manufacturer of the Aztec Nomad seaplane, a Piper PA-23 Aztec converted to EDO floats. It also offers a pilot door and an engine cowl modification as STC kits for land-plane Aztecs. An amphibian version is stated to be awaiting Transport Canada approval. The company operates from the Muskoka Airport site in Gravenhurst and is closely tied to Air Muskoka, the conversion facility.

B&R Machine Co. Limited has operated since 1971 from a 20,000 sq. ft. plant in Mississauga, Ontario with more than 26 work stations for CNC turning, milling, grinding and honing. It machines parts such as shafts, pumps, valves, aircraft parts, housings and military transport components, and builds sub-assemblies and complete assembled machines with functional testing. It states ISO 9001 and AS9100 certification and is listed in the Controlled Goods Program registry. Surface finishing is outsourced to approved partners.

Besnovo Technologies Inc. (formerly BRIC Engineered Systems) develops industrial automation and robotic laser de-coating equipment in seven product series, from stationary work cells to mobile units for aircraft and marine vessels. It says it is certified to AS9100:D and ISO 9001:2015 and that it took part in several laser de-coating projects for the United States Air Force. A third-party auction listing shows the Ajax laser facility's equipment was offered for sale on March 17, 2026, so the current operating status needs confirmation.

Bombardier Inc. is a Montréal-area aircraft manufacturer that builds Global business jets at its Aircraft Assembly Centre at Toronto Pearson and completes them at the Laurent Beaudoin Completion Centre in Montréal. Since May 2025, select Global aircraft have undergone review, inspection and certification flights at a hangar leased from Chartright Air Group at Region of Waterloo International Airport (YKF) before moving to Montréal. Bombardier Defense modifies and supplies Global 6500 aircraft for special mission use, including as the airframe for Saab's GlobalEye, and is scouting for a Canadian defence modification site.

Bombardier Inc. (Dorval, Quebec) assembles its Global family of large business jets at its Aircraft Assembly Centre, also called the Global Manufacturing Centre, on Toronto Pearson International Airport lands in Mississauga, Ontario. Bombardier states that about 2,000 employees moved from the closed Downsview plant to this site. Assembled aircraft are flown to Bombardier's Laurent Beaudoin Completion Centre in Dorval, Quebec, for interior completion. The Global 6500 built here is offered through Bombardier Defense and has been ordered by the Government of Canada, the National Research Council of Canada, Saab and an Australian maritime surveillance program.

Brock Solutions provides automation engineering, manufacturing execution system (MES) and IoT software, IT/OT cybersecurity, and sustainment services to manufacturers, airports, airlines, ports and water utilities. It manufactures CSA-certified and UL-listed electrical control panels at plants in Kitchener, Ontario, and Irving, Texas. It also develops the SmartSuite software line for baggage, passenger and port operations. It lists Aerospace & Defense as an industry served, with no named defence customers published.

CTS Composites Inc. is a Mississauga, Ontario tooling and fixturing specialist. It supplies patterns and molds, precision fixturing systems, and composite, prepreg, metal and hybrid tooling. Its published equipment includes large-format 5-axis CNC milling, curing ovens, autoclave access, a temperature-controlled clean room and a coating and spray booth. It states that it holds ISO 9001-certified quality systems and verifies tooling with FARO laser measurement.
